ResponsesInList.Title: Duplicate Moodle accounts created by "Sync users from Microsoft Entra ID" task – missing unique constraint in auth_oidc_token table?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello folks. I have reported this to the plugin developer as well about this anomaly We are running Moodle 4.5.4 on RHEL Linux with MySQL with: auth_oidc version 4.5.2 (2024100710) local_o365 (latest compatible) The scheduled task local_o365\task\usersync ("Sync users from Microsoft Entra ID") has previously created multiple Moodle accounts for the same Entra ID user (same numeric samAccountName as username, different emails – one UPN-based, others derived numeric). I have also confirmed that the auth_oidc_token table currently has no duplicate rows for the same `oidcuniqid` + `resource` . Thankfully there are no duplicates yet in the table. However, the table still lacks a unique constraint on `(oidcuniqid, tokenresource)` , so duplicates could easily re-appear once we turn the sync task back on (due to the well-known race-condition / token-lookup-failure pattern reported many times over the years, e.g. #2102 , #1723 , #249 , #231 , etc.). Questions: Is this still considered an open issue in the current 4.5.x release line, or has a unique index on `(oidcuniqid, tokenresource)` been added in a newer version (or in the Moodle 5.x branch)? What is the recommended/best way to fix or mitigate this problem permanently? - Should the plugin install this unique constraint by default (or during upgrade)? Is there an official supported method, or is the community workaround (clean duplicates + manually add the unique index) the expected approach? The manual unique index workaround is something we could test in our test platform, but it would be ideal if the plugin handled it out-of-the-box to prevent the issue for everyone. This may cause an issue if we upgrade to Moodle as this may or may not break the process when the manual index addition is added and for every Moodle upgrade. The index I want to add is: ALTER TABLE mdl_auth_oidc_token ADD UNIQUE INDEX idx_oidc_unique (oidcuniqid(191), tokenresource(50)); Would the above work? Thank you for the excellent plugins – they’re a critical part of our Microsoft integration! Regards Moodle version 4.5.4 | auth_oidc 4.5.2 (2024100710)

ResponsesInList.Title: Manual login not appearing
ResponsesInList.Text: Got command line acccess to server? IF so, cd /path/to/moodlecode/ Then php admin/cli/cfg.php > allsettings.txt That will redirect display of all settings to the allsettings.txt file which you can then view with a browser or from command line. Also recommend forcing the theme to boost via config.php file: $CFG->theme='boost'; manual authentication should be available by default and at least one user (the original installer account) ... if left for defaults ... 'admin' is set to manual.    However, having said that, who knows if there are any accounts still set that way. So, again from CLI, do a query of the DB with a bash shell script located in code/admin/cli/ Create the script using nano text editor: nano getusers getusers contains mysql -u root -p -e "use [moodledbname];select id,auth,username,firstname,lastname,email,lastip,lastaccess,lastlogin from mdl_user;" > users.txt;cat users.txt;wc -l users.txt Things you will have to change above ... the user if you don't know the root user password for the DB server.  The DB name. And the prefix to the table: mdl_ if not the default. All of those can be found in config.php at code root. After saving, execute: source ./getusers [enter] Then: fgrep 'manual' users.txt should show those accounts still set to manual login/authentication. 'SoS'. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: guest site access acting strangely
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Connie, from your description, this might be related to the “Auto-login guests” setting. Could you please check if it’s disabled? You can find it here: `/admin/settings.php?section=userpolicies` or via the menu: `Site administration` → `Users` → `Permissions` → `User policies` → `Auto-login guests` (autologinguests) If this is set to No , Moodle will not automatically log users in as guests when they open courses with guest access. That could explain why: Clicking directly on a course activity briefly shows the content, then the login window pops up. Using the “Guest login” button works correctly, because Moodle then actively logs the user in as a guest. Since your clone site works fine, it’s possible the clone still has this option enabled. Changing it back to checked should restore the previous behavior.

ResponsesInList.Title: OAuth2 with Microsoft creating duplicates with mail aliases
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, We've had an issue that came up since upgrading several Moodle sites to 4.5.5 this summer. Since that update, it seems that when an user has an alias mail different from their UserPrincipalName (UPN) in AzureAD/EntraID, instead of matching these users with their current existing account linked to their UPN in Moodle, OAuth2 is creating a new account that only populates Moodle's username and email fields with the mail alias. Changing their original account's email in Moodle with the alias mail from AzureAD/EntraID allows the user to log in onto that account and doesn't create a duplicate. Looking at Moodle 4.5.5 code change, I see that there was a change in oauth2_client with a new method called 'get_additional_upgrade_token_parameters' linked to this tracker: https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-80380 . That said, it doesn't seem to be about authenticating with OAuth2, but rather a new way to set up outgoing mail from Moodle through an OAuth2 service. We've investigated the corresponding apps in AzureAD/EntraID. It would seem most are set up as multitenant apps. We've tried updating to 4.5.6 as this fix looked promising: https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86004 . Unfortunately, it didn't fix this issue. Creating a new multitenant app didn't work either. Some of our clients are reporting that they can't create single tenant app as they are met with an error message that prevents them from doing so. Did anyone else face this issue? How come previous accounts were created in Moodle with the UPN in the username and email fields, but now it's the alias email? Is this something we can fix by changing the mapping for the OAuth2 service? Thanks in advance, Marius

ResponsesInList.Title: OAuth2 with Microsoft creating duplicates with mail aliases
ResponsesInList.Text: The following changes seem to have been brought up with 4.5.5: Endpoints for OAuth 2 issuer: userinfo_endpoint https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/ → userinfo_endpoint https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oidc/ User field mappings for issuer userPrincipalName email → email email

I mean, it says " Discovery means that the OAuth 2 endpoints could be automatically determined from the base URL for the OAuth service ". ResponsesInList.Title: oAuth2 'discovery' - only manual?
ResponsesInList.Text: After putting the code into debug and stepping through to figure out what's going on, the logic reveals that: 1. when you create the service, it tries to discover the endpoints. if something goes wrong here, it won't retry. 2. when you edit the service, the only reason it will retry discovering the endpoints is if you change the base url. So I have to edit, then change the base url to be something wrong, save. Edit > change the base url back to be correct, save. This triggers the rediscovery. I wish there was a "Rediscover" button that bypasses this need to double-edit.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Asynchronous Sync Task with
ResponsesInList.Text: Below is all the steps I took to get things working. I started thinking my PHP 8.1 install was too low for 4.4 for using LDAP. https://moodledev.io/general/development/policies/php https://www.php.net/supported-versions.php I decided to upgrade to PHP 8.3 and take the opportunity to upgrade to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. I removed all versions of PHP to make sure I was going to be using a clean PHP install. Upgraded to to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (used multiple checkpoints / snapshots for the VM ). Installed PHP 8.3.6 and the extensions. Updated the php.ini for max input vars https://docs.moodle.org/404/en/Environment_-_max_input_vars The site broke with nginx 502 error. I reviewed logs in /var/log/nginx/moodle.error.log and found that the 502 error was due to old configuration of /etc/nginx/conf.d/moodle.conf I updated this line from this in moodle.conf: fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.1-fpm.sock; To this: fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock; (I may change this to php-fpm.sock later and test to avoid this issue in the future) Restarted nginx and ran nginx -t, and the site was loading again without 502 error. I tried running the past failed ad hoc tasks which continued to fail and generate the notification emails. Since all the failed tasks were related to LDAP, I decided to remove / delete the ad hoc tasks. I went to Site Administration > Server > Task processing and changed Failed ad hoc task retention period to 1 hour. Saved changes. I then ran the following tasks: Clean up ad hoc task metadata Cleanup of task logs Going back to Site Administration > Server > Ad hoc tasks and confirmed no ad hoc tasks shown. I went back to Site Administration > Server > Task processing and changed Failed ad hoc task retention period to 1 Day. I've seen other applications have issues whit a configuration setting post-upgrade even when all the setting fields were correct. On a hunch, I made a change to the LDAP configuration to get a 'fresh save' of the configuration. I had a 2nd LDAP server I could use, so I changed the Host URL to that other server and saved changes. I would have made any change to any of the fields just to make a new 'fresh' save for the LDAP configuration and chose the Host URL since it was the 'easiest' option. I went to Site Administration > Server > Scheduled Tasks Ran these two taks: LDAP users sync job Synchronise system roles from LDAP No Ad hoc tasks were created and no notification emails generated. I changed the LDAP configuration back to my original settings and re-ran the LDAP sync tasks which ran successfully without generating ad hoc tasks or email notifications. I reset the "Failed ad hoc task retention period" back to 4 weeks, and let the scheduled LDAP sync tasks execute on their own according to the schedule. They ran successfully and still no ad hoc tasks or email notifications. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Odp: Re: Can't connect to LDAPS, LDAP is working
ResponsesInList.Text: `openssl s_client ...` is testing that the LDAP server responds to a connection attempt with SSL (TLS) negotiation, it's not testing an LDAP request. Also, the unable to verify first certificate messages suggests that any local .pem, .cer, etc. files aren't being read or aren't correct. The command to test an LDAP request is ldapsearch , probably something like `ldapsearch -H ldaps://ad1-xxx.domain.local:636 ...` . You'll need to work out the exact options for your LDAP server, this reply may help. The parameters to `-D` and `-b` would be those from your Moodle settings, the auth_ldap page's Distinguished name and Contexts respectively. I've always just used `TLS_REQCERT ALLOW` in `ldap.conf` and skip certificate verification. It's not perfect but at least passwords are encrypted in transit.

ResponsesInList.Title: Odp: Re: Odp: Re: Can't connect to LDAPS, LDAP is working
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you. I'll try ldapsearch and come back with an answer.

ResponsesInList.Title: Odp: Re: Odp: Re: Can't connect to LDAPS, LDAP is working
ResponsesInList.Text: Leon you are great!! In fact ldapsearch with the -d1 parameter showed me that the server was looking for a ca.pem file, which was not in the /etc/ssl/certs directory. 3 weeks of struggle, and it turned out that the appropriate certificate file was missing, even though the certificate itself was created but under a different name and indicated in the openldap configuration file. Many, many thanks, I am in your debt ;) Now moodle connects via ldaps:// . The topic can be considered closed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Sync - Update userdata from AD instantly (not after user login)?
ResponsesInList.Text:
My bet is that this is due to MDL-73703 , that was introduced in 4.4 (and backported to some earlier supported versions). That changed moved the "on login" updates from being synchronous in the cron job execution, to being run in asynchronous scheduled task (to spread the update work across a bigger time range, and better control the server load). Thus effectively "delaying" those updates to the time when those asynchronous tasks are actually run. On the other hand, when a user logs in, the "on login" updates (only for her/his user!) are done synchronously as part of the login process. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTML SSO LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text: You probably have some PHP file that is outputing some content (usually some white space, or some empty new lines), before .../auth/ldap/ntlmsso_finish.php calls to `redirect()` . The `config.php` file at the Moodle root directory is one of the usual suspects (but not the only option). It could also be the `auth/ldap/ntlmsso_finish.php` file itself! Make sure you don't have any empty lines or white spaces before the opening `<?php` tag in your PHP files, or after the closing `?>` tag if you have it (you shouldn't have one, to prevent this kind of trouble precisely ) Otherwise, some other piece of code is outputing some content to the page, before .../auth/ldap/ntlmsso_finish.php calls to `redirect()` Saludos. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication using Security Group not OU
ResponsesInList.Text:
Assuming you starting objectClass filter is this one: 
```text
(&(objectClass=user)(memberOf=cn=Moodle Users,ou=Groups,ou=staff,dc=domain1,dc=lan))
```
 and that you want your users to be a member of either "Moodle Users" group (with that distinguished name) or the "Moodle Bosses" group (with a distinguished name of `cn=Moodle Bosses,ou=Groups,ou=staff,dc=domain1,dc=lan` ), then the following objectClass filter should do the trick: 
```text
( &
    (objectClass=user)
    ( |
        (memberOf=cn=Moodle Users,ou=Groups,ou=staff,dc=domain1,dc=lan)
        (memberOf=cn=Moodle Boses,ou=Groups,ou=staff,dc=domain1,dc=lan)
  )
)
```
 I added spaces and new lines before and after the parenthesis for clarity purposes, but you can remove them in the final objectClass filter, and it would be just this one: 
```text
 (& (objectClass=user) (| (memberOf=cn=Moodle Users,ou=Groups,ou=staff,dc=domain1,dc=lan) (memberOf=cn=Moodle Boses,ou=Groups,ou=staff,dc=domain1,dc=lan)))
```
 Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: For anyone wanting to follow this chat.  I was able to use multiple groups in the object class..ChatGPT helped with this.... ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to track change of new email address by the students
ResponsesInList.Text: - Students can change their own email address Isn't this the default behaviour in Moodle? Role Authenticated user has capability moodle/user:editownprofile . - Students cannot change their own email address to another address that is already used This is the default behaviour for user accounts using manual authentication . If you're using a different authentication plugin please provide details. - Customer advisors can combine two accounts, merging one student account into the other // this keeps progress in their courses (does not reset) - When merging, the old email address is logged - During merge, the student advisor can see EVERY change that will happen before clicking GO Other system: the enrollments system finds out about this and merges sales orders to the new student account (maybe using the list of old email addresses) Have a look at the Merge user accounts (tool_mergeusers) plugin. If you have further requirements specific to your environment you may need to modify this plugin, or develop your own plugin to track changes using the Events API and respond to these.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is this authentication order correct?
ResponsesInList.Text: Follow up - tip for after migration move to another server. While server is accessible and you can login, there could be many places in the moodle that need adjusting now that the new server/environment has a different IP address. And with Moodle 4, things have moved in the admin interface ... kinda like playing 'who moved my cheese'! So the tip: in moodlecode/admin/cli/ there is a cfg.php script.   It list all the settings by their shortnames .... ie, backend. php cfg.php > allsettings.txt Redirects a very long scrolling screen to a text file that admin could view with nano - a text editor.   Nano has search.   Search for 'LDAP'. Doing so might lead you to changing config of LDAP authenticaton settings that worked at servers old IP, but now doesn't with servers new IP. For 'quick fixes' (including quick testing), one can add $CFG->[shortname]=[value]; to config.php file ... and then later make change to that area via the Moodle Admin UI which would then change appropriate tables in the DB. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Logging Student Password Resets
ResponsesInList.Text: From what I know, user ID 1 is guest and should always remain manual.  It does have a password (which is 'blank'), user ID 2 is the account created when Moodle was first installed and should always remain manual - even if one changes the auth for all other users. User ID 2 login/pass being manual means that even if the auth for all other users fails for some reason, that admin level user will always be able to login to 'fix' whatever. User ID 0 is really backended system ... like cron job/task - where no user ID number is needed to perform whatever. You see it in mdl_logstore_standard_log. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Mapping User Fields for Custom OAuth2
ResponsesInList.Text: I have an addition that I think may help some administrators that need to integrate custom OAuth2 services with Moodle. The documentation can be found at https://docs.moodle.org/401/en/OAuth_2_services . Suggestion Under Further configuration options , I would recommend adding a note to the Configure user field mappings section after the existing paragraph : To map nested fields returned by the user information endpoint, use dashes to separate field names. For example, if your service returns JSON like this `{"data": {"attributes": {"first_name": "Syed"}}}` , then you would map the firstname internal field to the value `data-attributes-first_name` . Reason for suggestion I recently found myself having to integrate a custom OAuth 2 provider. I could not figure out how to get nested fields out of the user info JSON return value. Eventually, I went to read the source code of one of the pre-defined OAuth 2 providers so I could determine how to do it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could not upgrade OAuth 2 token. HTTP status for remote endpoint: 0
ResponsesInList.Text: The HTTP status for remote endpoint value is the response for Moodle's HTTP request to the OAuth 2 issuer endpoint. This should be 200 OK . Status 403 Forbidden would indicate a failure to authenticate. Status 0 suggests the Moodle server cannot make the request at all. From memory this request is to the endpoint URL configured in Moodle with name "token_endpoint" so check that URL is present and correct. Then check the web server software is able to make these requests. Security systems like SELinux can block the web server from making HTTP requests.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problems with Clever SSO Provider in 4.1...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ben, Your Moodle configuration should be pretty straight forward as you just need to plugin the client ID and secret. You should be all set there. On the Clever side, if you want flows from the portal to work the main thing is to configure your default redirect URL to be the root Moodle URL, and then provide the callback URL as an additional allowed value. For example: Once you have that setup, you should be able to validate two flows: 1. A user goes directly to foobar.org and clicks on the Clever button to login (see this this test case video which illustrates execution of the test case in the tracker issue). This is exactly in parity with support for other providers like Google, MS, etc. 2. A user clicks on your application from the Clever portal. This will redirect them to foobar.org, and then devolve into the flow above. It does require two clicks (one on the Clever portal, one on the Moodle login page). We have users logging in via Clever successfully today using the two flows above. Note that a "one-click" login flow from the Clever portal that does not require the second click on Moodle's login page will not work. This is because Moodle expects a state query parameter that includes a valid sesskey to prevent CSRF attacks as mentioned here when the oauth callback is invoked. Clever initiated flows can, of course, not provide that value. Hope that helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Logging in with Gibbon
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you expecting Moodle to read user information from Gibbon but manage passwords separately? Or are you expecting Moodle to use the same passwords as Gibbon? In your screenshot Password format is "Internal". This means Moodle will manage passwords separately. When the Synchronise users task (\auth_db\task\sync_users) scheduled task is run it will email users with details of how to access the site. So check the cron is set up for your site and test that it can send email . If you want Moodle to use the same passwords as Gibbon then Gibbon must store the password in one of the formats supported by Moodle . ResponsesInList.Text: Please see: https://docs.moodle.org/400/en/Location There is a small paragraph for All Country Codes linked page above (English). ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for your answer, that was helpful!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to map the country field with external database authentication?
ResponsesInList.Text: Core Moodle includes a user field that allows the selection from a list of ISO 3166 country names to be stored and displayed in the dropdown selection box on a user profile page. These values can be seen here. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_3166_country_codes The country name you are using may not always exactly map to the ISO name, e.g. the official name of what I think of as “The Czech Republic” is stored as the ISO country name of Czechia. These values are stored in a file called lang\en\countries.php in the form $string['GB'] = 'United Kingdom'; So as you say it is not a free form field, but a key/pair mapping. It will also depend on what country name you are using (i.e. is it the ISO name as listed in that Wikipedia link) https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/lang/en/countries.php

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO moodle and binded url
ResponsesInList.Text: You don't say which SSO mechanism you're using. But browsers restrict some functionality when HTTP (insecure) is in use, functionality which works with HTTPS (secure). From memory using NTLM for SSO with LDAP doesn't work with non-HTTPS sites because browsers won't perform the challenge/response over HTTP. I'll also add that a Moodle site should have one URL only – e.g. https://moodle2.corp – and all user access should be via that URL. The docs explicitly say : Do not try to set this with any PHP code that can generate a variable URL. This is not supported, can cause strange problems and will stop command line scripts working completely.

ResponsesInList.Title: Users authentication failure
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone! We are using Moodle 3.9+ with Classic theme and this week we are facing with an issue during the users’ login. In particular, some users are not more able to login even if the credentials (username and password) are valid. We are analyzing the problem and it seems that the problem is due to the hash algorithm used for storing the passwords. Following the use case: If the hash algorithm for the stored password is $2y$04, the user cannot login and he has to change the password (even if the password is still valid). If the hash algorithm for the stored password is $2y$10, the user correctly logs in. For the new user, there is not that problem. The user is able to change the default password (we force the password change at the first access) and the user correctly logs in. We are not setting the type of hash algorithm to be used by Moodle for the password storage and it seems that the chosen algorithm is random. Does someone know if recently some Moodle settings are changed related to the authentication? How is it possible to avoid and permanently solve that problem? Thank you for your help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Users authentication failure
ResponsesInList.Text: Has there been any recent upgrade of Moodle or PHP? Or any server migration? If so, is there a $CFG->passwordsaltmain value in config.php that wasn't migrated?

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Users authentication failure
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Sorry for the delay in answering. No upgrade, no change in configuration lately. The issue is observed only for accounts which in the past had the password hashed with fasthash, i.e. only 04 iterations and the system did not upgrade as it should do by default to 10 iterations when the user changes the password. The users which force-change the password these days have the hash correctly upgraded to 10. Why in the past this did not happen and they still have 04 after password change? Why now the system doesn't know to check the password hashed with 04 as it is correctly in the database , for the users which had change their password in time? It does only for new users, since end of March 2022, who have force-password-change flag and the new hash is done in background without any impact to the user experience. So for us the only solution is to ask the users to do Forgot password. Thank you

ResponsesInList.Title: SSO into Account Created via External Database Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: I am a web developer and am new to Moodle - I have a question regarding authentication. I have an online platform, and have setup a Moodle installation as an 'add-on' service in a subdomain with the files located locally on the same server . I would like to use External Database Authentication to sync the accounts from the main platform, into the Moodle installation (which I have working). Next, I would like the users to be able to click a button and SSO into the Moodle installation from the main platform without having to re-authenticate. Is there a feasible way to achieve this SSO functionality while using the External database authentication? Is there a better was to achieve what I am trying to do?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO into Account Created via External Database Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle's external database authentication (auth_db) doesn't support SSO because it's not really the same thing: auth_db reads user information from a database optionally including a password value which Moodle uses for user authentication. SSO would require Moodle to trust some third party – your platform in this case – and have a mechanism to obtain user information and verify that they're logged in. The normal way forward would be to implement some existing SSO standard that Moodle supports on your platform, and configure Moodle to integrate with that. SAML2 and OAuth 2 are two common choices. Or you could implement your own system to do this either with a Moodle plugin or by customising core Moodle source code. The disadvantages of this are that such a system may introduce security vulnerabilities, and changing the source code gets in the way of getting support and keeping your version updated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP broken after upgrading from 3.10 > 3.11
ResponsesInList.Text: What you type in the "Host URL" setting is split at ';' characters, and each part gets white spaces stripped from the beginning and the end of it. But that is the only processing that is done with each part before using them in the PHP `ldap_connect()` function. As you can see in the documentation of that function, the first parameter of that function is either a URI (URL), or a hostname (that includes an IP address). So both things are supported and should work equally well. If they don't, then something in the LDAP module of the PHP version that you are using is not behaving as it should. Edit: now that I re-read the ldap_connect documentation, I noticed that the examples of the URI version of the parameter don't include a trailing slash, while Moodle's examples do. Maybe that could be the source of the problem?

ResponsesInList.Text: That's why you see A required parameter (code) was missing – there is no code= in that URL. It looks like: Moodle has passed the grant type authorization_code to the OAuth 2 issuer, and the issuer does not support that grant type and has passed back error=unsupported_grant_type to Moodle. So you will need to find out what grant types the issuer supports and whether it supports authorization_code . The issuer may have logs to help you investigate this problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: E-mail authentication
ResponsesInList.Text:
What does SQL query: 
```text
SELECT name, value FROM mdl_config WHERE name = 'auth';
```
 say? It should be a comma-separated list of authentication methods. If email isn't listed you could add it in, for example: 
```text
UPDATE mdl_config SET value = CONCAT('email,', value) WHERE name = 'auth';
```
 or if the list currently empty: 
```text
UPDATE mdl_config SET value = 'email' WHERE name = 'auth';
```
 Support for Moodle 2.9 ended almost five years ago , you should plan to upgrade to a supported version.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue with setting up LDAPS
ResponsesInList.Text:
If ldap_test.php can connect using StartTLS but Moodle cannot that suggests that there's either 1) something the web server user account cannot access, or 2) something the web server process cannot access. For 1) this can be easily tested by running ldap_test.php as the web server user. You need to know the user account the web server software runs Moodle's PHP as. On Linux this is typically either apache , www-data or php-fpm . Once you've determined the correct user, run the script, for example if it's www-data then run the following as root : 
```text
sudo -u www-data php -d error_reporting=E_ALL ldap_test.php
```
 And see if it works. If you're having trouble identifying the correct user, the ownership of files in moodledata/filedir may reveal this. For 2) this is normally something like SELinux or a chroot jail restricting access. I think both of these are unlikely if Moodle can connect to the LDAP server without StartTLS.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue with setting up LDAPS
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you still got TLS_CACERT path/ldap.crt in ldap.conf ? Can user apache read file path/ldap.crt (for example sudo -u apache cat path/ldap.crt ). Because if apache cannot connect but root can then it could be a file permission issue. I have used strace (for example sudo -u apache strace php ldap_test.php ) to find which file-open call was being blocked by filesystem permissions. strace produces a lot of output but unless you can work out what apache cannot access (but that root can) then you might need to use this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue with setting up LDAPS
ResponsesInList.Text: Also, in addition to what Leon said about file permissions, if this is a Linux distribution that enables SELinux and configures it in enforcing mode (RHEL, CentOS, Fedora, and some others), make sure the SELinux policies allows the apache use to connect to LDAPS. If the Linux distribution is using AppArmor instead of SELinux, you need to check its policies instead. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Multi LDAP and duplicate username
ResponsesInList.Text: Greeting ! I set Ldap1 and Ldap2 And there is Ldap1\john and there is Ldap2\john. Ldap2\john can't sync if already Ldap1\john sync. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multi LDAP and duplicate username
ResponsesInList.Text: All usernames in Moodle must be unique (as they must be in Ldap1 and Ldap2). The only way you could have users from multiple LDAPs where the usernames are not unique would be to specify a different LDAP attribute in User attribute , one that is unique across LDAPs. Typically that would be the email address, for example Ldap1\john may have email john@example.com and Ldap2\john may have email john@dept.example.com. Of course this means that all users logging into Moodle must use their email address as the username.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multi LDAP and duplicate username
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm afraid that Moodle requires unique usernames. That means that if you are using a LDAP attribute for the username (like 'samaccountname' in MS Active Directory, or 'uid' or 'cn' in OpenLDAP) that may be duplicated accross LDAP directories, you will have this problem. In these cases you need to use a LDAP attribute that guarantees uniqueness across LDAP directories. If you are using MS Active Directory, 'userprincipalname' is a good candidate. It's value has the forme 'username@ domain .dns.name'. So the part after the '@' character will be different for each Active Directory domain. With LDAP, using rfc2307 or rfc2307bis schema, you are a bit short of options if you don't want to modify Moodle code. The only attribute that is 100% guaranteed to be unique accross LDAP directories in that case is the distinguished name. Which is long, ugly looking and with a syntax that most users will have trouble remembering. So if you don't want to use the distinguished name, the only other option that I see if modifying Moodle's code. You keep using whatever user attribute you are using. And in the part of the LDAP code that creates the user, you simply add to the user name something that is unique per LDAP directory, in a way that you know for sure it's not going to be present in the user nam. For example, the name of the LDAP plugin ('ldap', 'ldap2', etc) with some "separating character(s)". E.g., say you have username 'john' in both 'ldap1' and 'ldap2' LDAP plugins. You can create synthentic usernames 'john##ldap1' and 'john##ldap2'. That would be the usernames from Moodle's point of view. Of couse, you need to undo that change when authenticating the user. So you also need to change that part of the code. But in that case you now what to do: just strip the extra part you added when creating the user, before trying to authenticate it. You'd do that change in the 'user_login' method of the LDAP plugins. You would also need to change the following LDAP plugins functions, as they all deal with usernames, directly or as part of 'user' objects: get_userinfo, get_userinfo_asobj, user_exists, user_create, user_signup, user_confirm, password_expire, sync_users, ldap_bulk_insert, user_activate, iscreator, is_role, user_update, user_update_password, sync_roles, ldap_find_userdn, get_ntlm_remote_user and is_user_suspended. Sounds like a lot of work, but it's not that much. It just happens to be sprinkled all over the place Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: OAuth2 but filter via e-mail address
ResponsesInList.Text: How about: Upload the teachers' accounts to Moodle . Presumably only their email, usernames (same as email?) and auth ('oauth2') need to be set. firstname and lastname need to be present if using a CSV but they could be set to a common value and get overwritten by the OAuth 2 mapped field on login. Enable Prevent account creation when authenticating under Site administration ▸ Plugins ▸ Authentication ▸ Manage authentication . That way teacher accounts should be successfully authenticated by the OAuth 2 plugin because the accounts exist in Moodle, but the students won't be allowed access because Moodle won't create the corresponding account for them. Beyond that I think you'd be looking at a custom plugin or core code changes as the current OAuth 2 functionality allows any authenticated user who grants Moodle access to their info.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting Invalid Login Error
ResponsesInList.Text: So the likely causes are: the Moodle server is unable to connect to the LDAP server, or the LDAP server does not recognise the username or password the user has entered. First test the connection (point 1) by going to Site adminstration ▸ Plugins ▸ Authentication ▸ Manage authentication and clicking Test settings for the LDAP server entry: It should say "Connecting to your LDAP server was successful".

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting Invalid Login Error
ResponsesInList.Text: In fact, point 2 is more likely if you're getting "Invalid login, please try again". Moodle sends the username as the LDAP attribute specified in Moodle in User attribute with the entered password to the LDAP server. So maybe user details or passwords have been changed on the LDAP server. Also check the config changes report to see if anything has been changed on the Moodle site. If it's still not working please share the value of your User attribute field and the type of the LDAP server (for example: Active Directory or OpenLDAP).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Log in with Apple (OAUTH) ?
ResponsesInList.Text: What advantage would there be for you as admin of your Moodle and especially your students using your Moodle IF there were such an authentication plugin? There already is a similar functionality (Login with Google, Login with Facebook) which was popular enough to become part of moodle core. Apples "Login with Apple" is said to be based on OAUTH as well - so it should theoretically work with the existing Moodle OAUTH module when configured correctly. The advantage is, that Students don't have to remember their login/pass to enter moodle - this reduces the barrier for using it. Remembering a user/pass combination is for sure no problem for a university student - but moodle is not only for universities. The school I work for (as moodle admin/dev) is focussed on people who dropped out of the school system and tries to get them back into it. Lowering barriers of reentering is a key concept here. And a comment: Authentications require 2 ends ... the Moodle plugin is one end, and the other would be Apple. I would imagine, if there were a plugin for Moodle, it would have to interface with something like Jaml - which is an admin interface for controlling apple devices issued by an entity ... like a school issuing iPads to students or iPhones issued by an entity. The "sign in with Apple" functionality doesn't require centralized control of apple devices. It's a service usable for any website or app. I imagine the functionality 1:1 as the existing moodle function "Login with Google". ( https://developer.apple.com/sign-in-with-apple/ ) Does your entity issue Apple devices to students? No. But everybody has a smartphone - and there's only two operating systems out there... "Login with google" reliefs ~80% our students (all the android users) from having to remember yet another password while still keeping authentication safe. Now it's about the other 20%. Would you be willing to take on admin of such an application? I'm evaluating if I should program such a plugin and just ordered a used iphone to run some tests. ResponsesInList.Title: How to prevent account creation when authenticating just for one issuer?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm aware the manage authentication option to "Prevent account creation when authenticating". But what if I need to permit account creation to one oauth2 issuer and prevent doing this for another one? More exactly, my instituition has its own oauth2 issuer that I need to leave open to new account creation. However I'd also like to enable oauth2 Google authentication, but not to create account. Anyone know how to configure this? ... any changing in some php file? Thanks for any help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to prevent account creation when authenticating just for one issuer?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm afraid you need to modify the PHP code. Account creation prevention is a global setting, not a per authentication plugin setting. Much less a per OAuth2 provider setting. You basically need to modify the code in these lines: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_39_STABLE/auth/oauth2/classes/auth.php#L574-L586 where the "Prevent account creation" check is performed. You have the `$issuer` object at that point, that holds the `issuer` property of the OAuth2 token. So you just need to check if the issuer is the one that you want to be able to create accounts and let the authentication flow continue. Otherwise you just keep the current code to trigger login failed event. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to prevent account creation when authenticating just for one issuer?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, Iñaki! But could you help me with the code to check my issuer? Supose my issuer in mdl_oauth2_issuer table is configured as id = "1" and name = "myissuer". I tried set this information in Line 574 something like this, but
not worked: if (!empty($CFG->authpreventaccountcreation) && $issuer='1' ) or if (!empty($CFG->authpreventaccountcreation) && $issuer='myissuer' ) Thanks a lot! Osvaldo The entire code of L574-L586 is here: if (!empty($CFG->authpreventaccountcreation)) { // Trigger login failed event.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to prevent account creation when authenticating just for one issuer?
ResponsesInList.Text: Any help?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to prevent account creation when authenticating just for one issuer?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Osvaldo, you need to change this line: 
```text
    if (!empty($CFG->authpreventaccountcreation)) {
```
 to this one: 
```text
    if (!empty($CFG->authpreventaccountcreation) && ($issuer->get('name') !== 'my-identity-issuer-name')) {
```
 Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to prevent account creation when authenticating just for one issuer?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks a lot, Iñaki!

ResponsesInList.Title: Setting up Azure SQL database for external authentication

I have created a database on Azure with the student details which my database is running, however, I'm having difficulties matching the information I have about my database with what Moodle needs for external authentication. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting up Azure SQL database for external authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle's external database authentication relies on PHP having a supported extension for that database, and Moodle then supporting this extension. Is the Azure database a type of SQL Server instance? If so PHP on the Moodle server would need the sqlsrv extension which is available from Microsoft . You'd need network connectivity from the Moodle server to the database server. You'd need a single table returning all the information you need for the users in Moodle: at least username and password, and optionally first name, last name, email, etc. If the Azure database doesn't have such a table use a database view to emulate this. Passwords can be either 1) stored in the external database using one of the supported encryption types, 2) stored in the external database unencrypted (not a good idea), or 3) stored in Moodle only and just use the external database for the user profile fields. You'll need to factor in any other requirements for these passwords, e.g. if there is another system you also want to authenticate with the Azure database then both this system and Moodle would have to understand the password format.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not able to enable LDAP Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: If the Moodle server is Linux and the web server is Apache , check SELinux isn't enforcing with the command getenforce . If so try setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect 1 to allow Apache to make the LDAP connection. The domain controller will use a certificate signed by its own authority which the Moodle server can't verify. Try adding TLS_REQCERT ALLOW to ldap.conf (in /etc/openldap/ldap.conf on CentOS, C:\openldap\sysconf\ldap.conf on Microsoft Windows). If I may, some further advice: I think Use TLS : Yes + ldap://… (not ldaps://…) is preferred over Use TLS: No + ldaps://…. I normally put the AD domain name, e.g. domain.int , in the Host URL field (no ldap:// or ldaps://) and leave it up to AD's DNS to return a domain controller. LDAP encoding should be "utf-8", cp1250, etc. is only used if Version is "2" . I think Member attribute and Object class should both be blank. They'll then use defaults based on the User type setting. An Object class of "*" could potentially return computer accounts which you definitely don't want. If there are still issues getting this to work, please let us know more about the environment: Moodle version, web server type (e.g. Apache, Nginx, IIS ), server operating system, PHP version.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: error/Could not upgrade oauth token
ResponsesInList.Text: I think it's what it says: Moodle is configured to use a proxy for web access. Moodle (from the web server not the browser) attempts to connect to the configured token endpoint but the proxy server is refusing to allow the connection replying with status 403 Forbidden. Presumably Moodle has a web proxy configured so check that's configured as expected. Under the hood Moodle is using Curl to make this request so if you're familiar with this you can test connecting to the token endpoint from the Moodle server using the command curl to troubleshoot the settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO Bypassing Login Page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Katie, Did you know that you can actually specify an alternate login URL in Moodle? We use it to make the login link (or button depending on your theme) take the user directly to the SSO Oauth2 system using the standard Oauth2 plugin included with Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO Bypassing Login Page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Benjamin, The reason it is logging you out and right back in again is because you are only ogging out of Moodle but not your SSO provider. In order to properly log out, you need to be logged out of you SSO provider. You may also need to logout of Moodle too afterwards. The trick to getting this to work is to find a way to end up logged out of both. There are two possibilities that I know of. Some authentication systems provide Moodle with a logout URL automatically. I don't know for sure if yours does. It may be something that you can configure in the authentication plugin settings. In my case, after studying the SSO provider's documentation, I discovered that it supported a redirection parameter. The URL is where the SSO provider sends the web browser after you are logged out of SSO. The result is that the user ends up logged out of both systems. So I did some customization to change the logout URL toinclude the extra parameter. Now when the user logs out, they are now clicking a link that will log them out of the SSO system and then get redirected to the Moodle logout URL. Unfortunately Moodle lacks an alternate Custom logout URL option like the one for logging in. So far this has been working great - for the most part. There remains one a small annoyance which I have not had time to work out yet. After logging out, when I click on a link to the course I was in before I logged out, instead of taking me to the course description as one would expect, it takes me to the SSO login page. So what I think I need to do now is to create a custom logout.php that will also delete the session cookie so that Moodle stops trying to redirect me back to the last page I was on. I will probably add an option for that but I am not sure that I will be able to programmatically override the default Moodle logout URL path. You may still need to do some custom work in the theme. Hope you find this helpful. Best regards, Michael

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What's the exact difference between 'manual' user and 'oauth' user
ResponsesInList.Text: Some auth plugins will authenticate users with different auth methods. For example auth_saml2 will authenticate users with other methods which means you can populate users in Moodle with, say, LDAP but still use SAML2 for SSO which is useful as you can't populate users with SAML2. As far as I can see the only difference between "Manual accounts" and "OAuth 2" when using OAuth 2 authentication is that if the user is set as "OAuth 2" then changes to the user on the OAuth 2 server (e.g. first name, last name) will be updated in Moodle. If the user is manual then they won't be updated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO in moodle using custom server
ResponsesInList.Text: In steps 5-7 is "my system" Moodle? Or is it a third system between the school system and Moodle? I think you need to investigate the existing SSO services supported by Moodle. What you're describing sounds very similar to a SAML use-case or OAuth2 . Either way I think it would be easier to base any implementation on some existing standard instead of implementing an authentication service from scratch. The decision would be based on what, if any, SSO service the school system currently supports. Otherwise it will be necessary to implement an SSO service that uses the school system as the back end. Something like SimpleSAMLphp may help you implement a SAML Identity Provider on top of the school system. Step 4 suggests that the school system contains password information for the students. One of the challenges might be finding out how to verify entered password values with what the school system stores. For example, these may be stored as plain text (hopefully not!) which would be easy to verify, or they may use a well-known hash algorithm such as SHA-1 which it should be straightforward to verify. Or they may use some custom storage format which may need some investigation to determine how to verify these (if it's possible at all). For step 6, I would hope this isn't necessary, both SAML and OAuth 2 allow you to populate attributes such as email, first name, last name, so hopefully these can be included in the redirect from the authentication service to Moodle on successful authentication. Unless there's some requirement I don't understand. So my recommendation is: find out what authentication services the school system can provide, if any; find out what SSO services Moodle supports and see if they could integrate either directly with the school system or via some authentication service you'll have to implement on top of the school system; find out if any candidate SSO service allows you to obtain all required student information needed for the specified flow of information. A last thing: SSO sounds like the right way to implement this but if read-only access to the school system's database is possible from Moodle then it might be possible to use External Database authentication , although password verification may be a challenge.

the new LinkedIn Developers site at https://www.linkedin.com/developers/ . You can learn more about our Version 2.0 APIs, our developer program, and how to migrate your apps. The only other thing I can think of is that you say you are running Moodle in a test environment. The OAuth2 API requires that the identity provider (in this case, LinkedIn) must be able to invoke a callback API on your server , and that means that the server can't be behind a firewall - or at least, port 443 must be reachable from the outside world. But you've probably already realised that. Best, --- Les

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Shibboleth Suddenly Stops Working
ResponsesInList.Text:
In my Shibboleth experience "suddenly stopped working" often means metadata expiry, so the first thing I'd check is that the identity provider (IdP) has the current metadata for the service provider (SP), i.e. Moodle in this case. The logging output appears to be the IdP complaining that it can't match an SP AssertionConsumerService URL with that listed in the SP's metadata. I'm guessing something like this is happening: The unauthenticated user goes to Moodle and tries to log in. Moodle redirects the user to the IdP for authentication The IdP authenticates the user. The IdP then wants to send user information to the SP via the URL that the SP provided in step 2. But the IdP can't match this URL to any it knows about so the process fails. 
```text
2020-04-16 16:59:59,177 - WARN [net.shibboleth.idp.profile.saml.impl.PopulateBindingAndEndpointContexts:410] - Profile Action PopulateBindingAndEndpointContexts: Unable to resolve outbound message endpoint for relying party '
https://engage.elearning.sruc.ac.uk
': EndpointCriterion [type=


{urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata} 


AssertionConsumerService, Binding=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST, Location=
https://engage.elearning.sruc.ac.uk/Shibboleth.sso/SAML2/POST
, trusted=false]
```
 So I'd 1) check the SP's metadata making sure this lists an exactly matching AssertionConsumerService element, both the URL (" https://engage.elearning.sruc.ac.uk/Shibboleth.sso/SAML2/POST ") and the binding ("urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST") must match, and 2) check the IdP has a current copy of the SP's metadata which contains this AssertionConsumerService.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Could not upgrade oauth token in custom oAuth2 config
ResponsesInList.Text: This error will occur if Moodle's request to the OAuth 2 service token_endpoint URL fails. The most obvious reason for this would be that the URL is wrong so check that first. The Authenticate token requests via HTTP headers setting should normally be off (the default). The OAuth 2 service may be logging something in response to this failed request which could help identify the problem. The failing request causing the error comes from the Moodle web server to the OAuth 2 service (not from the browser) so if it's a  Linux server with SELinux is enforcing (check with the command getenforce ) you may need to allow Apache to make outgoing network connections if you're using this.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle's LDAP authentication is great, however it would be better if we could use multiple LDAP systems for authentication. I have seen several posts from people using Active Directory in an educational environment with for example, separate Active Directory domains for staff and students. There are ways to talk to multiple LDAP servers if you have an Active Directory forest and are talking to an appropriate Global Catalogue server , however what if you have domains that are not in a forest and what if you have some other LDAP system that you would also like to authenticate against - for example, say you have a student Active Directory domain that is not in a forest with a staff Active Directory domain, and what if you also have another LDAP server such as Apple's OSX OpenDirectory or Linux OpenLDAP or Novell eDirectory? The good news is you can use as many as you like - my solution to this problem is quite simple - duplicate the LDAP plugin and make some small changes - here's how to do it (using Moodle 1.8): *DISCLAIMER* I accept no responsibility for anything that may go wrong with your system as a result of this procedure. I suggest taking a backup of your system and database first just in case. Backup ANY files before making changes. Better safe than sorry, however we are not going to be changing anything old, just adding something new. Find the 'ldap' folder in html/auth/ Make a copy of the folder, and call it something different - e.g. ldap2 Note that by doing this step the admin will not be able to get into the authentication page of Moodle until the changes below are applied (they will get a blank page). If you panic, simply delete the new folder (i.e. ldap2) and all will return to normal. Look in the newly created ldap2 folder and edit the file auth.php Change the following lines: Line 24: class auth_plugin_ldap extends auth_plugin_base { to class auth_plugin_ldap2 extends auth_plugin_base { ...note we are simply adding a '2' on the end of the class name.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8

To solve your auth_ldap2title problem you need a new file in your language pack - if you copy your existing auth language file, eg yourmoodle\lang\en\auth.php , and call it auth2.php , that should solve your problem. A couple of questions about this - do I take it that this still only allows each Moodle installation to connect to one domain's LDAP, you just get the choice of which one, or will a Moodle now try validating against each domain for which there's an auth2, auth3 etc file?  In other words, if I put this fix into one of my Moodles will I just get the choice of which domain to authenticate against, eg staff or student, or will that Moodle then check both domains to try and authenticate? Do you know if this will work on 1.7 and earlier?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Ahh thankyou for pointing me in the right direction - I have added the following lines to lang\en_utf8\auth.php which works: // Secondary LDAP plugin (PF20070620) $string['auth_ldap2title'] = 'LDAP server'; $string['auth_ldap2description'] = 'This method provides authentication against an external LDAP server. If the given username and password are valid, Moodle creates a new user entry in its database. This module can read user attributes from LDAP and prefill wanted fields in Moodle. For following logins only the username and password are checked.'; // Everything else uses the same variable names as the main LDAP plugin, so no problems there. In answer to your question - Moodle will try to authenticate supplied credentials on all 'enabled' modules (i.e. the 'eye' is open in the list), in the order that you have set. For example, ours here now will check an account against the first LDAP server in the list, and if that fails will try the next authentication system in the list, which in my case happens to also be an LDAP server module, pointing at a different LDAP server. Users with accounts on either server can log in (there may be a problem with users with the same username on all servers and different passwords but I've not tested that yet). I could keep adding servers in this way and it would simply try them all in order. ...not sure if it will work on 1.7 and earlier - I guess if it has a modular authentication system like 1.8, then it should be a similar procedure as all we are doing is basically providing Moodle with an extra authentication module for it to try to authenticate users with. I think it might be an idea for Moodle to ship with maybe three LDAP modules by default as I think that would cover most users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text:
I've been meaning to post this for ages, but here's what our developer hacked together to get Moodle authenticating against two AD servers in different forests. It's similar to what you've done and might help those who are developing the Moodle authentication code. Sorry if some of it isn't too clear - the guy who wrote this isn't around any more to ask! So, ripped straight from our internal documentation wiki: (all the nulc references are to our organisation: Newcastle-under-Lyme College ). Moodle LDAP Authentication In order to authenticate against multiple AD domains (such as different Student and Staff domains), several functions had to be rewritten. This page details the changes that were made to the Moodle 1.7 line in order to allow it to authenticate against multiple AD domains. This code will not work unmodified on other versions of Moodle, as authentication functions seem to change with each point release. Database modifications It is not necessary to perform major database changes for this modification. In the mdl_config table, all records with ldap in the name must be duplicated and modified to read ldapad2. These config entries are follows: ldapad2_expiration = 0 auth_ldapad2_stdchangepassword = 0 auth_ldapad2_forcechangepassword = 0 ldapad2_objectclass = objectClass=* ldapad2_memberattribute = ldapad2_user_attribute = sAMAccountName ldapad2_opt_deref = 0 ldapad2_search_sub = 1 ldapad2_contexts = ourcontextsgohere ldapad2_user_type = ad ldapad2_bind_pw = ourbindpassword ldapad2_bind_dn = ourbinduser ldapad2_preventpassindb = 1 ldapad2_version = 3 ldapad2_host_url = ourhosturls ldapad2_expiration_warning = 10 ldapad2_expireattr = ldapad2_gracelogins = 0 ldapad2_graceattr = ldapad2_create_context = ldapad2_creators = auth_ldapad2_changepasswordurl = auth_ldapad2_changepasswordhelp = LDAP Authentication library Copy auth/ldap directory to auth/ldapad2 Edit auth/ldapad2/lib.php and replace all instances of $CFG->ldap with $CFG->ldapad2 Edit auth/ldapad2/config.html and replace instances of ldap with ldapad2 except in print_string or get_string functions except line 356: $help .= get_string("auth_updateremote_ldapad2","auth"); Modified Moodle Functions See attached file. It goes in: lib/moodlelib-nulc.php In file lib/setup.php line 192 (add): 
```text
 
require_once($CFG->libdir .'/moodlelib-nulc.php'); // NULC Specific modifications
```
 In file login/index.php change line 120 to: 
```text
 
$user = authenticate_user_login_nulc($frm->username, $frm->password, $frm->authtype);
```
 Custom Login Page Any custom login page must include either a select box or radio buttons which must pass the chosen authentication method (ldap, ldapad2, internal) in the variable authtype.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 2.0(!)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Bob, if you go back in the conversation, you will see that there are step by step instructions to do it in Windows. Anyway, I'll rehash them here, including additional remarks to address some things that have happened to several people since I wrote those instructions I'll go step by step. I'll assume you already have the patch executable (patch.exe) and command line php executable (php.exe) installed and available in your PATH (you really need them in your PATH!!!). It is a good idea to check the Moodle documentation page on how to apply a patch in Windows Download the .zip file with the 3 files. Make sure you download the right .zip for your Moodle version! Unzip it and copy the 3 files to the top directory of your Moodle installation. Let's say it's under C:\Moodle\server\moodle. Open a command prompt window and cd into c:\Moodle\server\moodle. Apply the patch from the first file, using the instructions you can find in the Moodle documetation page we mentionned above. Run the ldapname.php file with the name you want to give to your second LDAP auth plugin. Let's say I'll call mine 'ldap2' (without the quotes); php.exe -f ldapname.php ldap2 Now you only need to go to the Notifications page to install, enable and configure the new 'ldap2' plugin. If you need to add a third LDAP auth plugin (a fourth, a fifth etc.), you just need to repeat steps 4 and 5 (using the new LDAP auth plugin, of course!). You only need to repeat steps 1 to 3 if you upgrade your Moodle version. If you get a conflict in step 3 or 4 (with a message of 'HUNK failed' or something like that), that means my patch is not up to date with newer versions. If that's the case, just drop me a message here on privately via Moodle messaging. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text:
We use separate AD servers for staff and students and I solved this with a small OpenLDAP server configured to function as a proxy. The configuration is such that talks to both (or as many as you need) servers, rewrites the paths to make them look like they belong to a single LDAP within a single root. This is the config - it connects to two ldap servers, teachers on 1 and students on 2 and presents them both as if under a single tree: OU=Techers,DC=COMPANY OU=Students, DC=COMPANY I configure Moodle to use the root of the proxy server, and to connect using the MANAGER user. We have just a small problem with this which I posted in another topic here - Moodle does not update user autocreation does not work if the user profile fields are setup to update on every login (this is with the CAS plugin) ------------------------------------ 
```text
include         /etc/ldap/schema/core.schema


moduleload      back_ldap


moduleload      back_meta




database meta


suffix dc=COMPANY


rootdn "cn=Manager,dc=COMPANY"


rootpw {SSHA}***********************************




uri "ldap://server1/ou=Teachers,dc=COMPANY"


suffixmassage "ou=Teachers,dc=COMPANY" "real ldap path where teachers are in server1"


idassert-bind bindmethod=simple   binddn="user to connect in server1 full path"   credentials="********************"   mode=none   flags=non-prescriptive


idassert-authzFrom "dn.exact:cn=Manager,dc=COMPANY"




uri "ldap://server2/ou=Students,dc=COMPANY"


suffixmassage "ou=Students,dc=COMPANY" "real path where students are in server2"


idassert-bind bindmethod=simple   binddn="user to connect in server1 full path"   credentials="*********"   mode=none   flags=non-prescriptive


idassert-authzFrom "dn.exact:cn=Manager,dc=COMPANY"
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry, I migth be very late for this but I used multiple LDAP-Servers like this: in the LDAP Server Field (Host URL ) you may type in more than one server separated by semicolons like this: ldap://yourAd.domain.edu:3268;ldap://10.51.3.17:3268 (The port 3268 being Microsoft's Global Catalog Port which is compatible with the default LDAP Port) or you may use DNS-Round-Robin to achieve the same redundancy on yourAd.domain.edu instead of using SamAccountName you may use mail if you have the same SamAccountNames on two or more domains like we do. Simply set the USER ATTRIBUTE Field of your LDAP-Settings to mail so as to use the eMail-Addresses of the users as Moodle usernames. You have to enable extended characters in your Moodle-Server-Policy for user-account-names first because of the @-sign. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Alan, you were using the right file, but the wrong procedure (for Windows). The problem is the patch file (0001-bla-bla-bla.patch) has Unix line endings. And patch.exe for Windows doesn't like them (that's why you got an assert failure). You need to convert the Unix line endings to Windows line endings before trying to apply the patch. That's why the instructions on how to apply a patch on Windows
tells you to "Open the patch file with Wordpad, and click 'File' >> 'Save as...', choose a different name for the file eg ('mynewpatch.diff') and "Save as type" >> 'Text Document - MS-DOS Format' " (in the link I provieded before). Saludos.
Iñaki

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Iñaki. Thanks for providing this to the community. I have a suggestion for making this work better on a Mac. At about line 47 of ldapname.php you have: } elseif (stristr(PHP_OS, 'win')) { This causes the script to detect the running os on a Mac as windows and as such, attempts to use the xcopy command. The reason is that PHP_OS on a mac gets set to Darwin. I added simple logic so now it looks like this: if (stristr(PHP_OS, 'Darwin')) { system('cp -a "'.$ldap_orig.'" "'.$ldap_new.'"'); } elseif (stristr(PHP_OS, 'win')) { $ldap_orig = str_replace('/', '\\', $ldap_orig); $ldap_new = str_replace('/', '\\', $ldap_new); $ldap_orig_langfile = str_replace('/', '\\', $ldap_orig_langfile); $ldap_new_langfile = str_replace('/', '\\', $ldap_new_langfile); $patch_file_orig = str_replace('/', '\\', $patch_file_orig); system('xcopy "'.$ldap_orig.'" "'.$ldap_new.'" /S /E /I'); } else { system('cp -a "'.$ldap_orig.'" "'.$ldap_new.'"'); } Regards, Jamie

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Miika, I know this answer is a bit late, but the problem is has strict rules on how to name plugins. And they are stricted than I thought they were (it seems the developers made them stricter around Moodle 2.2 but I didn't notice, and didn't update my patch to take them into account). Currently plugin names can only contain lowercase ASCII letters, numbers and underscores (but numbers and underscores are strongly discouraged by Moodle developers!). And the plugin name must start with a lowercase ASCII letter. That's why your copy of the plugin didn't show up in the Notifications page: it wasn't considered a valid plugin name, and thus it was completely ignored. I have update the patch scripts to comply with the rules and reject any plugin name that would be considered invalid by Moodle. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: When I tested this on Totara 2.7.6 (Moodle 2.7.9) if NTLM is enabled the problem is in ntlmsso_finish.php It reaches an end state here: // If ntlmsso_finish() succeeds, then the code never returns, // so we only worry about failure. if (!$authplugin->ntlmsso_finish()) { // code to redirect with error code } I changed my code to then attempt a connection on ldap2. if (!$authplugin->ntlmsso_finish()) { // My Change. try ldap2. redirect($CFG->httpswwwroot . ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to use multiple LDAP servers with Moodle 1.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tomas, you are not missing any configuration, as Emma has pointed out. On the other hand, it turns out that I didn't notice that the patch was failing to take into account the new scheduled tasks sub-system files. So the scheduled tasks were not being created for the cloned plugins. I have updated the patch to take that into account. Bear in mind that the cloned plugin scheduled tasks are only created during plugin installation (that's the way Moodle behaves, not something patch-specific). So this won't benefit existing users much (unless you backup your cloned plugin settings, uninstall it, re-install it and restore your plugin settings). I'm attaching updated patches for Moodle 3.1+ (current as of today), and Moodle master. I'll upload and update version for Moodle 3.0+ in a few hours. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SAML, LDAP and user synchronisation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I just finished installing and configuring the SAML2 plugin. Before using this plugin a user's login was handled by ldap. After having solved the installation and configuration error/problems (only a few, so I would recommend SAML2), I logged in successfully to Moodle. But I was greeted by a placeholder site stating "You have logged in successfully as [...] but are not authorized to access Moodle.", which I found was true. When looking at my user's configuration, it stated "Choose an authentication method: LDAP server ". But there is a simple solution, the plugin offers a configuration key "Allowed any auth type", which is by default set to "No" (if you copy and paste, please be aware that it really says "Allowe[d] any auth type"). Change it to yes and your users can login via LDAP or SAML.* *To be a bit more specific: the LDAP plugin has the higher priority. After installing the SAML2 plugin, the login website will show the usual login form and an additional button for SAML login (bearing the name/alias you gave for your IdP). Now when the users use the usual login form, they are handled by LDAP and when they press the new button they are redirected to our IdP login website.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Oauth2 Moodle sign up
ResponsesInList.Text: I'll start by saying ' what we want to do isn't always available - workarounds included! ' - and to go along with that ... there are good reasons! You probably need to look at what's there already and why ... Guest account already exist ... profile can't/shouldn't be edited by a guest user themselves.   Using any mysql tool you have query the mdl_user table ﻿ ﻿ my sql > select id,username,firstname,lastname,password,email from mdl_user where id=1; You'll see that the guest user was the first user created and even though you might see a password it is hashed, etc. and it shouldn't be changed.  Email address is root@localhost ... good!  Don't want a guest user to become spam king/queen in your site! For guest user to see courses, courses themselves must allow guest access in defining parameters of a course.  And Guest user cannot use any activity/mod/block or whatever that's interactive or allows input like posting to a forum or uploading a file, etc. All users using Google's Oauth2 ... is fine ... just not Guest and the first person to install the moodle instance ... if left for defaults, user is 'admin'. Can't emphasize this enough ... at least one user needs to ability to login manually ... ie, that username/password in left panel of the login screen.  IF all the other authentications fail for some reason, manual admin account will be the only user who can login. Persons do use Google configured for handling mail for a domain ... ie, not all Google email is @gmail.com. 'SoS', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Oauth2 Moodle sign up
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alessandro, When you say 'Allow new people to sign up as guests', I'm guessing that you want new users to have an account and not just be logged in as a guest, right? You can disable all login possibilities except Google OAuth by just enabling OAuth 2 authentication and setting up the OAuth 2 Google service only. You can then choose whether new people will have an account created for them automically or not, by disabling or enabling the setting 'Prevent account creation when authenticating' in Site admin / Plugins / Authentication / Manage authentication.
