ResponsesInList.Title: Re: state laws (questions) for maintaining identity & inserting non-module pages
ResponsesInList.Text: Instructions for US-state-identity-Qs.code Copy out the code for the 2 programs into their own 2 files and name them us_state_sec_quests.php and us_state_sec_quest1.php as given and, place them in your moodle folder. copy out the sql "create table" and "insert" statements (with sample questions & answers) into a 3rd file and import it into your moodle database Because, among the states we work with, we knew of only 2 state's, so far, that have this "questions" law, we preface their userid's with FL. or NC. ... so, we check to see if the student has a period in the 3rd position of their userid, denoting that they need to fulfill this requirement; if not, the program ends and the topic outline returns. That check has been commented out, here, in US-state-identity-Qs.code (everyone taking the course will have to answer the Q's) Logic: Check if they have answered the (8) Q's, if so, close window. [else] build the screen[window] and load all the Q's when submitted, check that all (8) are answered. if all answered, save the answers, write a cookie informing the javascript not to re-call this program, end the program, return to the topic outline. [else] re-prompt for answers again. each program contains instructions for inserting its javascript into the database - use a tool like phpMyAdmin . After you get it up and running as is, feel free to make changes. - Greg

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: state laws (questions) for maintaining identity & inserting non-module pages
ResponsesInList.Text: Greg, It's very important that you sanitize your data when interacting with a database from a PHP script. This prevents issues such as SQL Injection . The scripts, as posted, potentially allow a malicious user to take over a Moodle install by carefully crafting the data that they submit to either script. This is because you are placing raw $_GET variables straight into queries. There is a strong API in Moodle for all database interaction which would definitely be worth your time reading. The developer docs is a good place to get started. A quick remedy would be to replace all your $x = $_GET['x'] calls with $x = optional_param('x', 0, PARAM_INT) and replace all your database access code with Moodle's get_record() and insert_record() methods (among others). You should go through the rest of your code and ensure it's also secure. Hope that helps, Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bind settings for LDAP authentication for moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Quote from your quote "MS-AD requires this". The bind user account you create in MS AD is used only by the Moodle server software in authenticating users - ie, looks up user name and the password the user provides.   Moodle users should never see/know.  How to setup LDAP/MS AD service is not within the scope of this forum.  Suggesting consulting something MS ... like? http://social.technet.microsoft.com/Search/en-US?query=set%20up%20LDAP&ac=2 I do consulting for many schools that use MS AD and have to co-ordinate with the AD Administrator.  They create the non-privileged account (ie, NOT an Administrator level account credentials) that is used in configuration of LDAP authentication using Microsoft AD in Moodle LDAP authentication. Maybe Emma has a good tutuorial/reference. Your error, however, shows ' mnethostid ' ... that's MoodleNetworking Host ID and appears to be attempting to create a temporary table ( mdl_tmp_extuser ) to use when syncing.  One does NOT need Moodle Networking to authenticate vs any LDAP server so turn off Moodle Networking and it's authentication. FYI ... in Moodle networking, ID 1 is your Moodle server.  ALL Host Moodlenetworked servers is ID 2.   Any other Moodle server(s) that has been MNet'd with yours will begin with ID 3. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

There was an improvement in this area as part of MDL-28585 work (that is available from Moodle 2.5 onwards). If you are using MS AD (it doesn't work with other LDAP servers), have enabled password expiration handling and configured the LDAP auth plugin to handle password changes (bind user with the right permission , etc.), then Moodle can handle password expiration and password change[1] on first login. The only drawback is that Moodle still doesn't force the user to change the password. It just lets the user change it, but doesn't force it (there's an open bug for that: see MDL-32584 ) Saludos. Iñaki. [1] You just need to set the change password on first login property in AD for the desired users. By the way, setting a 'changeme' password in AD doesn't work, as Moodle only checks for that particular password in internal authentication plugins (manual, email, etc.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: The distinguished name needs to have the full path to the user.  It should be in this format: cn=deepakg,ou=MoodleUsers,ou=People,dc=yourdomain,dc=com  (for example) This user needs to have permission to read the ad users that you are needing to authenticate. The next thing that is important to get right is the context .  It should look like this: ou=people,dc=yourdomain,dc=com (for example) If you have additional groups under that ou that you want to include, check the box for that. Your server url should look like this:  ldap://yourserver.yourdomain.com (for example) Those are the most important settings to get right.  There is a link in the docs to a utility that you can use too.  It will give you more information.  You also need to make sure that your firewall is allowing the connection.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a way! There is a special php script (not a web page!) that is inside your Moodle directory, under auth/ldap/cli/sync_uses.php. When you run that script from the command line using something similar to this: php -f sync_users.php it will create all[1] the LDAP users in Moodle, and delete any old user from Moodle that are no longer in your LDAP server. It will optionally update your users information from the LDAP server if you have configured some attribut mappings to be updated 'on every login'. [1] If you don't want all of them, you can use a LDAP filter expression in the objectClass configuration setting, to only select a particular subset of users. The filter expression is a bit tricky, but your LDAP administrator could probably help you with that too

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: auto login to moodle from http url
ResponsesInList.Text: You might first consider what you are trying to accomplish with having an automatic anonymous login -- perhaps you can use the site configuration to achieve the same thing (i.e. all courses open to everyone, etc)? Otherwise, one approach you could use would be to craft an HTML page that hard-codes the userID and password into a form.  I think you'll need to use a form instead of a hyperlink because I suspect (but have not checked!) that Moodle expects to examine the POST information for login credentials, not the GET information. Something along these lines: <form action="index.php" method="post" name="login"> <input type="hidden" name="username" value="username_to_log_in_as" /> <input type="hidden" name="password" value="password_to_use" /> <input type="submit" value="Login" /> </form> ...the above is just a sketch but could get you going in the right direction.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: auto login to moodle from http url
ResponsesInList.Text: It used to be possible to pass usernames and passwords in URL 's in the form http://username:password@url.com , but that was withdrawn by Microsoft a few years ago on security grounds (by security update 832894, according to http://support.microsoft.com/default.aspx?scid=kb;en-us;834489 ). As far as I'm aware it's not possible to pass your username and password to Moodle in the URL in the way you've described.  I'm sure the developers could do it if they wanted, as it should be an easy job to parse the query string from within PHP and extract the details, but it would open an enormous hole in Moodle's security, not least because your password would be visible in plain text for anyone who wanted to see it. I think Bruce's suggestion would be your best bet, as the UN and PW would be passed invisibly.  That will only get you to the front page of your Moodle though, I'm not aware of any way of getting you straight to a specific course. Incidentally, for anyone running multiple Moodle installations, I have a script which will log you in to any one of them simply by selecting from a dropdown list box - I can post the code here if anyone wants it. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP contexts - request for enhancement
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Robert, you can already specify all that in the LDAP authentication settings, although in a less flexible way. You can specify the scope of the search (sub, base) by using the 'Search subcontexts' setting. You can also specify the filter by using the 'ObjectClass' setting (yes, you cas use any valida LDAP filter here). You can do the same with the LDAP enrolment settings. The "drawback" is that both the scope and the filter you specify are the same for all specified contexts (that you should specify as just the base search DNs). This is a compromise that was felt was good enough for almost all people, as it simplifies both the internal code (PHP uses different functions for earch kind of scope search) and the knowledge needed to configure the plugin (not everyone is a LDAP expert that knows about the syntax you mention). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.6 & LDAP Auth Sync
ResponsesInList.Text:
> When I go to edit the profile it just shows todays date! - I wonder if this is something to do with the format of date/time within AD? It totally has to do with the format of date/time. In MDL-40613 I see that you mention user account expiry attribute. That attribute uses a completely different time format than what the user profile field for dates uses. The latter uses Unix epoch timestamps measured in seconds (see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time ). The former uses the number of 100-nanosecond intervals since January 1, 1601 (UTC) (see http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/ms675098%28v=vs.85%29.aspx ) Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Authentication stack
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, In our Moodle, at Universitat Rovira i Virgili, in Tarragona, we have specific needs on authentication change when user logs in. Any Moodle site has two auth plugins always enabled (manual and nologin), and others optionally enabled. In our case, we should need the database and ldap auth plugins enabled. Is there some doc explaining exactly where and under which conditions the auth type of a user loging in is updated? Is the promotion of auth type between all types allowed? For instance, a user may have a manual account (i.e., manual auth), but at a certain date, the user may appear at LDAP , and the user's auth type should be updated to ldap automatically, and in the other way around. In particular, from most important to less important auth types, we have certain rules/conditions by which the user's auth type has to be promoted (or demoted): ldap (most important) database manual (less important) The authentication API really accepts a lifecycle like this? I know I can look at source code to follow the flow control and deduce the possibilities. However, I thought may be there is some kind of related official documentation. Many thanks in advance. At least, I'll share our discoverings here afterwards Jordi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authentication stack
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Jordi, when a user authenticates for the the first time, Moodle search the user using the enabled auth plugins (according to the sequence given to the plugins) and then bind the user to that auth plugin, for example LDAP, and the auth plugin is registered in the user account. However, you can change the auth plugin for a particular user changing the related user's profile, but Moodle does not change it automatically when a user disappears form an auth backend and appears into another, you need to do it changing the auth for each user, for example using web service "core_user_update_users". When changing auth plugin in the user profiles, make sure the account data match exactly those available in the different auth back ends, otherwise you will end up with duplicated accounts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authentication stack
ResponsesInList.Text: Many thanks Andrea. It is something we did in M1.9, and we expected to have evolved in some way to make it easier (for instance by means of an extended API on the auth plugins, or something like that): detect wether a user exist on the remote auth back end, or otherwise try to log in by the other plugins according to the ordered auth plugin stack. In our case, we have an almost 90% of users from LDAP, but there are other users that came from an external database or they are loaded by csv files (creating them as manual if missing). Let's suppose we have the following stack of auth plugins: ldap db manual What we have to implement is as follow: Detect if the user loging in appears firstly in ldap. If so: If the user was already ldap, go on normally. Otherwise, Update auth column to ldap, notify by email and go on normally. If there are problems, Moodle will redirect to the URL where to change the password. If user does not appear in ldap, but appears in external database, proceed in the same way as in ldap. Otherwise, if the user was in ldap or database, but not now, it is changed to manual authentication only under specific situations. This stack will add a little overhead at login time, mainly when the user is not found in ldap; what actually happens in very few cases. Do you have any idea to do that in a clean manner? We may collaborate proportioning a patch to do that if it is interesting for the Moodle community. Thanks in advance, Jordi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authentication stack
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jordi, Currently Moodle does not use the auth plugin stack in the way you described (a sort of 'fallback' is used to seek a first time user). From a general point of view auth back ends should be reliable sources of user credentials, a situation where it is not clear where and when a user pop ups in a given back end in some way breaks this assumption.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Create a new user in Moodle and LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Gianluigi, I think that your expectations don't match what Moodle currently does This functionality is to allow users to auto-create accounts in Moodle (and in the process, create the associated accounts in LDAP servers). When you (as an admin) create a user in Moodle, the LDAP auth plugin is not involved at all. Nothing calls the code to create the user in the external LDAP server. That's why you don't find your newly created users in the LDAP server. On the other hand, when a user signs up to auto create a new Moodle account and you have configured LDAP auth as the "Self registration" preferred method, things work a little bit differently. With self-registration, the account is created the same instant the user fills in the sign up form. But the account is locked (not activated) until the user receives the sign up confirmation mail and uses the confirmation link with the right secret. At that moment, the account is activated. So when Moodle creates the (internal) account, we need to create the corresponding account in the LDAP server. But it has to be created as a locked (disabled) account. This is where all your questions quick in. RFC2307 (and 2307bis) mandates that a user account has a homeDirectory attribute, and a loginShell attribute. So we need to provide them, otherwise the LDAP account creation fails. We just provide 'safe default' values (which can bite you in your back if you try to use any of these accounts for any onther purpouse than LDAP authentication). The third question is: why put an asterisk in front of the password value? Because the only way to create a locked account via LDAP using RFC2307 schema is providing an imposible to produce hashed password value. And if you are using MD5 or SHA1 hashed passwords[1] in your LDAP server, there's no way the hashed value starts with an asterisk. So there's no way for the user to type "a right" password, and thus the account is locked for all purpouses. [1] Note this is critical in this case!!! If you are using plain passwords in your LDAP server, and the user knows Moodle simply adds an ' ' before the original password, she can simply type the ' ' followed by the original password and the LDAP server will authenticate the user correctly (and Moodle aswell). As the final step, when the user clicks on the confirmation link, Moodle calls the code to confirm the user, which in turn calls the LDAP code to remove the '*' from the LDAP password. This 'unlocks' the LDAP account and the user can login into Moodle. The whole process is a bit convoluted, but that's (basically) the way it works. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blank page after login
ResponsesInList.Text: In my case, this problem (i.e. a blank screen after login attempt) was due to a strange behaviour in Moodle networking ( mnet ). Although networking is turned off in my installation, it seems that Moodle still goes ahead to renew the certificate, incrementing the value of mnet_localhost_id in mdl_config in the process of doing that. However, the value of mnethostid in mdl_user is not correspondingly changed, and this seems to be what caused the problem. So, I suggest that in addition to the things already mentioned in this thread, anybody having the blank screen should also check the mnet -related stuff. I had a similar problem in the past with a change in mnet_localhost_id when networking was not enabled, but on that occasion, the error given was something to do with an invalid authentication database. This is probably a bug in Moodle networking (i.e. mnet ), since mnet values in the database should be left alone if networking is not enabled, but I may be wrong. I'm running Moodle 1.83+

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can not login Moodle 2.5 using administration account
ResponsesInList.Text: LDAP users  will be refresh on each cron run. If you have two account of admin you have to drop manual account. Keep LDAP account untouched. Update password in LDAP and run cron or sync LDAP. You are done.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can not login Moodle 2.5 using administration account
ResponsesInList.Text: The admin account (first one created) is not automagically assigned to any course. Since that account is all-powerful, no need, as it can see all courses - even if hidden.  That account, probably should not be enrolled in any course, either.  If you have turned on 'mymoodle' and login as the admin user, you will not see 'mymoodle' (ie, 'your courses') - admin user is NOT in any courses.  Use the Site Admin menu to navigate to 'your' courses. Actually, have seen situation where LDAP communications between Moodle and the LDAP server failed.  If all users authenticate via LDAP, NO ONE has access.  NEVER a good idea to setup a situation where NO ONE has access.  Best, I think, to have at least one admin level account set to manual. Admin accounts also pull the most data upon initial login which is also recorded in sessions (DB or file).  Sometimes, when one person who uses the initial admin account and one other set to admin levels, that person gets a little confused.  Probably best for this one person NEVER to login with both accounts using the same browser.  If you ever have the need of doing that, use separate browser for each user (different cache - Safari/ FireFox do NOT share browser cache). Clear browser cache.  Clear browser cookies for the site.  Might also clear all server caches ... http://site/admin/purgecaches.php Then, TIA - try it again. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Username Change with External Database Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: It's an ongoing flaw with the external db authentication to key on username rather than idnumber. In your example it manifests as creating duplicates - but it creates other varied problems too, related to mutable usernames. A solution is to modify the auth and sync to key on idnumber, and populate the idnumber with the primary key of your external database, and ensure idnumber is locked to editing. That way the sync will update the username where the idnumber matches. Sorry I can't thnk of a simpler solution to this problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Username Change with External Database Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: If you open up the file: /auth/db/auth.php and look at the comments to the function sync_users you'll notice this: * Sync should be done by using idnumber attribute, not username. And that comment has been there for over 5 years You'll want to: - Change the call to get_userlist() to retrieve a list of idnumbers rather than usernames - Change the obsolete users check to look at idnumbers rather than usernames - If you remove users, to do it based on idnumbers rather than usernames - When updating... to updated based on idnumbers rather than usernames etc etc... You might also want to change config.html because you're not interested in 'fielduser' but interested in the external database key field (idnumber) - which shouldn't ever be the username if the username is mutable in your external database (as it probably is in nearly every case). Or you could wait until it gets fixed (it probably won't get fixed)

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle Authentication Plugin Changes not Reflected in the Database
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a quick question about storage of authentication plugin settings: Where do they go? If for example I save the hostname test.hostname.local into the CAS server configuration page at "server/admin/auth_config.php?auth=cas" and then check for its value in the moodle database within the table: mdl_config_plugins, I see that the value has been updated. But, if I change this value directly in the database, it is NOT reflected in the site administration page. This almost suggests that this setting is saved in two places.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Authentication Plugin Changes not Reflected in the Database
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Jeff, you are probably using a Moodle version that includes the MUC (Moodle Universal Cache ). This component caches a great deal of information to speed up many operations (including access to the DB). So it may happen that as you are not doing any changes to the setting through the Moodle code, the MUC still holds the (previous) cached, value as it assumes it's still "fresh" (valid). And when the config screen asks for the setting value from the DB, the MUC returns that value. You can purge (invalidate) the caches by going to Administration >> Site Administration >> Development >> Purge all caches Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Authentication Plugin Changes not Reflected in the Database
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks. That did the trick.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: self-registration automaticaly set to course creator
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Harry. I've seen you ask the same question in several different ways over the last few days and although I have thought very hard about this I am really struggling to see how you can get Moodle to manage this automatically. When users sign up the default role is authenticated user and then they are given roles in courses - or even site wide such as course creator - by the admin. Now you could change your default role to course creator (I think) but then your students as well as your teachers would be able to create courses and create havoc on your site. You then have a list of all the teachers who want to be course creators. * You then go to Site administration>Users>permissions>assign system roles and give the users in that list the role of course creator. *I think I read in another post a helpful suggestion from someone saying why not make the teachers have "teacher" in their username to make it much easier for you to identify them in the list when you choose the course creator. That seems to me an even better way to do it. * You could also read the documentation about the Course requester role This is quite complex but it would do what you want - but again - it is not automatic.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: First time LDAP Setup
ResponsesInList.Text: LDAP is for authentications.  Nothing will happen to the manual accounts.  If, however, you want all those users to authenticate via LDAP, their profile will need to be changed such that their login uses LDAP (user can have only one authentication method).  Existing enrollments/grades/assignments/etc.  will not be lost ... unless you delete accounts (uhhh, don't do that!). Also sounds like you have the impression that LDAP will remove accounts.  Been my experience it won't ... only add users. Couple of things ... The users that will now be using LDAP ... are their logins in Moodle the same as the username in LDAP?  Example: ktask (manual) but in LDAP ken.task  To Moodle those are two different users. If so, that would mean, to Moodle, they are a new student and thus won't be enrolled in anything ... and worse, all their grades/assignments, etc. are under their old account and they will NOT see their stuff. Sync of LDAP and Moodle accounts could get a lot of junk IF pointing your Moodle to the top level of the tree ... ie dc=xxx,dc=net.  That will sync all accounts ... even the tinker ones. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

The syncing reads how you have configured the LDAP in Moodle.  If you've configured Moodle LDAP authentication  to dc=x, dc=net it will sync the entire tree - or try to.  If you configure Moodle LDAP authentication to use ou=students, dc=x,dc=net then it will attempt to sync that part of the tree ONLY.  If you configure Moodle LDAP authentication to use ou=teachers, ou=student, dc=x, dc=net then syncing will attempt to sync both OU's. If you did the csv changes first, then set up the Moodle with LDAP and run the sync script, then additions/deletions would/should occur - syncing. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: using user data from moodle in another external database?
ResponsesInList.Text: The basic answer is no, the external db authentication method does not push anything, it only queries/pulls data from the designated external source. Typical solutions to this are - To write something for the other application to pull from Moodle, if you are treating Moodle as your central user database ; or to look at centralizing the user data in a system designed to do that using methods like CAS, LDAP , Shibboleth for authentication by multiple apps. (Not to say you couldn't write something for Moodle to push that data out, but usually applications are designed to poll/pull from a central data source instead of the other way around.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lost password alternatives? Overly complicated or required for security purpose?
ResponsesInList.Text:
My question now is anyone know how to change the auto generated password to be less random? There's at least three ways to do it: Disable password policy (in Administration >> Security >> Site Policies). This produces very simple (and unsecure) passwords, but also allows the user to set unsecure passwords themselves. Lower the complexity requirements. For example, you can disable requiring digits, so your users won't mistake a 0 for a O, or a 1 for a L. Again this makes your passwords less secure. Edit lib/moodlelib.php and find the lines containing the definitions for PASSWORD_LOWER, PASSWORD_UPPER, PASSWORD_DIGITS and PASSWORD_NONALPHANUM, and remove only the problematic characters (0 or O, 1 or L, etc.) This way your passwords can still be quite secure. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Log into Wordpress by Moodle DB
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Moten, unfortunately for you, you've no chance to use that plugin unless: someone will update that plugin to support the new Moodle password schema too. This is the best option you downgrade your PHP version: absolutely no, for security reasons, unless you're running a patched version like the "PHP 5.3.3" available in RHEL or Debian BUT in these enterprise distros the crypt* issues have been backported so... no chances with this option you hack the Moodle code to disable the new Moodle password schema, e.g. returning true immediately in lib/moodlelib.php::password_compat_not_supported() . This hack could be used until (1) will be done but you need to force password renewing for those Moodle users logged in after the new password schema landed into the main stream (2.5, MDL-35332 ) - probably most of your users if they regularly log into your Moodle since your 2.5 update - to let the old password schema to be applied. This option gives you a migration plan option, targetting (1), but you need to accept to lower the security at least from what Moodle decided to be the good one HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Database Authentication with Internal passwords - email not being sent!
ResponsesInList.Text: After some intensive research, I finally figured out how it works. When u run the Auth sync file, it actually created one user record in MDL_USER table with no password. And then it creates another record in MDL_USER_PREFERENCES table with an id corresponding to the one just created in the USER table, but with the "NAME" attribute set to "create_password". So when you run the cron.php file, it will check if the user preferences table has any entries with name attribute set to "create_password", and if there are it will set the new password and send email to the designated user, and delete away the record in the user preferences table after that. So why some is facing the issue of not receiving email? Well it is because the codes that are responsible for the above operations are encoded in a IF loop that will only execute if a randomised number is less than 20. Search for "random" in the file cron.php The codes responsible for above is in this loop. Then search for "creating" and u will see the codes for above operations. To make sure that cron.php always check for new user account, move the whole chunk of codes for checking new user account out of the random IF loop. Good luck! Cheers.

ResponsesInList.Title: Single sign on bombshell
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, We've committed to an externally hosted site and now we've been told that the site must authenticate using Active-Directory and users shouldn't have to login again if they are signed on to the internal network. Is this even possible!? I've done some research and NTLM doesn't seem an option for external servers, Shibbleth seems very complicated (although it appears that it will do the job). Don't be fooled by the above, I'm at the outer limits of my knowledge here. What seems like a relatively simple project just got complicated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single sign on bombshell
ResponsesInList.Text: It seems that because the authentication server (s) and the moodle server(s) are located outside the trust boundaries of each other then the only option without using a pass-through authentication would be session cookies. How it would work: User logs/authenticates to AuthServer AuthServer creates the (encrypted) session cookie and stores on the local machine AuthServer refers the User/Session over to the MoodleServer_SessionCheckPage The MoodleServer_SessionCheckPage checks for existance of the session cookie if session cookie exists then proceeds to create the session from the cookie and passes the user to the MoodleServer_Main if session cookies does not exist then bounces the user back to AuthServer login Note : Make sure that you refer your users to a password reset page on your AuthServer and not the MoodleServer.  Also either disable the "logout" link/button in Moodle or link it to your AuthServer login page rather than Moodle's login page. I realize this seems to only be theory, as I cannot provide you specific code snipits, take comfort in knowing this works and I hope this helps.  There's alot out there for your developers to reference for session state and session cookies.  Google is your friend.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single sign on bombshell
ResponsesInList.Text: I have seen this issue solved by using a VPN between the networks so the external host simply appears internally. The advantage is everything you do with AD is the same to it and the applications. However, a VPN may or may not be possible/practical/affordable at the external hosting end. Worth asking them about it. If so, the work is all on the IT end

I configured up the "external database" login plugin using the " Site administration " -> "Plugins" -> " Authentication " -> "External Database " page. I set up the plugin to use the exact same settings as the main Moodle database (but you can set it up to use a dummy database, by copying the mdl_user table structure so that the necessary fields are there). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can moodle recognise if a student or staff log on?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there. Well the short answer is "no" but there is a longer answer. Users in Moodle are "authenticated users" and don't normally enter with a student or teacher role even though they might have that role i the "real" world. See Assign roles So the not so short answer is that an administrator would have to decide for each user in each course which role they have. The longer answer is that it  is possible with various authentication methods to upload users or enrol users into courses with specified teacher/student roles (but again the admin has to do that in advance. ) See Authentication ( LDAP for example) or Upload users

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I include/exclude OUs from LDAP sync_users.php?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Eric, you can use any valid LDAP filter in the objectClass setting and Moodle (2.0 onwards) will only process those users that match the filter. In addition to that, you can specify several search contexts in the Contexts settings, separated by semicolons (;), and again Moodle will only process those users that are inside those contexts (and subcontexts if you enable the subcontext search setting). Using those two settings so should be able to configure pretty much any combination of included/excluded OUs (and many other criteria). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP auth not accessible outside of college
ResponsesInList.Text:
Make sure you specify the college internal IP subnets in "Site administration >> Plugins >> Authentication >> LDAP server" (see 'Subnet' parameter). Moodle will only attempt the SSO login if the client is coming from one of those subnets. If you are using some sort of reverse proxy for the external connections to your Moodle site, make sure you exclude the IP address of the reverse proxy from the allowed subnets (otherwise Moodle will think external clients are coming from the allowed internal subnets). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication but not reach the user name
ResponsesInList.Text: Not sure it's wise to allow Moodle to update LDAP - although potentially it could.  Most LDAP server admins that I have worked with would prefer that accounts be changed only on the LDAP server by authorized server admins. Moodle requires username, first name, last name, and an EMail address on bulk uploads, but seems to change somethings with LDAP authentications ... one must have Country as well as City/State.  Any of the moodle *required* fields for a profile that is NOT obtained from LDAP will result in the user being thrown into their profile.  And, even though they don't know it, when they make/change entries, Moodle is attempting to make changes to LDAP - which is not setup. So think your issue is related to configuration of LDAP in Moodle.  At the bottom of that form there is the section on Data mapping. First name = givenName Surname = sn EMail address = mail City/Town = l Country = c Those attributes must exist in LDAP and could be different in your setup.  Under each, there is a drop down list: Update Local Think it wise to have that set to for each above to: on every login Update external: set to never (which is default).  Even if you set this one otherwise, LDAP server might reject changes unless it's setup to allow ... again ... don't think that wise at all. You've not mentioned what your Moodle server's 'flavor' is ... Windows or Linux.  If Linux, one could use ldapsearch from the command line to test access to the LDAP server (can't change/edit ... just query/test). 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication but not reach the user name
ResponsesInList.Text:
Just a small note to complement Ken's excellent information (thanks Ken!). Moodle only redirects the user to the profile page if the first name, last name or email is not filled in (either directly by the user, or obtained from and external source like LDAP). So in this particular case mapping the firstname, lastname and email fields would be enought. In fact, if you are using Moodle 2.2 or later, so can set a default country and city for all your users, that will be used if they don't specify one (or is not obtained from external sources like LDAP). You can set these defaults in "Site administration >> Location >> Location settings". Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternate Login URL
ResponsesInList.Text: In the config.php file of the site add the following line to regain access: $CFG->alternateloginurl=''; This 'blanks' the URL (sets it to nothing) and overrides the setting in the mdl_config table Use phpMyAdmin or similar tool to edit the mdl_config table and remove the setting for 'alternateloginurl'. Then comment out the added line in the config.php file by putting // in front.  Why leave it?  Well, it appears you want to use an alternate login URL for some reason and if one begins to 'tinker' again with this feature and the next attempt also fails (resulting in lockout), it will enable acquiring accesss again should changes don't work again. BTW , you might want also to put a 'blank' index.html file in your series7 directory to prevent curiosity seekers from seeing the moodle2.zip file and using that to see exactly what version of Moodle 2 you are running. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

Good Morning,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Password Recycling
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi,

After doing some further research and testing I have come up with the following solution which I'll post here in case others have the same problem in future.

Probably the easiest solution, is to ensure that Moodle doesn’t store the LDAP password.

In http:/yourmoodlesite/admin/auth_config.php?auth=ldap

Bind settings

Hide passwords

Select yes to prevent passwords from being stored in Moodle's DB.

This way when learners log in the password is checked from the LDAP server not Moodle.

Also check the LDAP password expiration settings.

Expiration

Select No to disable expired password checking or LDAP to read passwordexpiration time directly from LDAP

Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: only pull people with certain attributes
ResponsesInList.Text: I do not think you can "synchronize" custom profile fields from LDAP ; at least it did not find it in Moodle 1.9 Admin screens. But again you can add few lines to the sync_users function in auth/ldap/auth.php User creation is done here : $user = $this->get_userinfo_asobj(addslashes($user->username)); // prep a few params $user->modified = time(); $user->confirmed = 1; $user->auth = 'ldap'; $user->mnethostid = $CFG->mnet_localhost_id; if (empty($user->lang)) { $user->lang = $CFG->lang; } If you want to add a "constant value" to one custom column of mdl_user table just add $user->mycustomcolumnname="my value"; In my place, I have added an integer column to mdl_user named ldap_sync to know if that user has been created by cron sync or not so I have $user->ldap_sync=1; Now if you want a custom column to be synched with LDAP you must add a mapping in function ldap_attributes() before the return such as $moodleattributes['mycustomcolumn']='myldapattribute'; function ldap_attributes () { $moodleattributes = array(); foreach ($this->userfields as $field) { if (!empty($this->config->{"field_map_$field"})) { $moodleattributes[$field] = $this->config->{"field_map_$field"}; if (preg_match('/,/',$moodleattributes[$field])) { $moodleattributes[$field] = explode(',', $moodleattributes[$field]); // split ? } } } $moodleattributes['username'] = $this->config->user_attribute; return $moodleattributes; } In my site I have there $moodleattributes['eduPersonAffiliation']= 'eduPersonAffiliation'; so I always read that attribute for LDAP and since I also have an custom column in mdl_user named eduPersonAffiliation, its value is automatically set from LDAP. Watch out for multiple values, Moodle read only one of them and you can never now which one is retrieved... If you enable user modification and/or removal, you may have to add some of these lines alos in relevant parts of function sync_users(). These patches are for Moodle 1.9. Actually I do not understand what you plan to do in two stages. The way auth_sync_ldap works is that : - It will add to Moodle user table all accounts that have you attribute destinationIndicator set and remove all accounts that do not have it, if you say so in Administration/Authentifcation setup screen. Cheers

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When are old users erased
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle 1.9 only one bit in the database was set to 1 (DELETED). And this was very handy in a lot of cases where our students came back after a couple of years, as I simply set that bit to 0 again directly in the database and they got back also all of their old courses. In Moodle 2.3.1 I have been told that DELETING a user unenrolls him/her from any courses they were in. So even if they stay in the database with the deleted bit set to 1, reviving them will not bring back their courses. Instead you could use the DEACTIVATE function now. But this trick could also be used on 1.9 simply setting the AUTH field of the user to NOLOGIN or some other auth plugin of the server you deactivated to prevent such users from logging in. Now the practice proved that users coming back, even users using their private eMail-Address as username, will not be accepted if their eMail-Address is alredy present in the database. So we had to UNdelete a lot of users. In Moodle 1.9 I did this simply and directly in the database. In Moodle 2.3.1 I do not know if it is that simple or not. So creating new accounts for already present eMails would best be done by uploadusers with the option IGNORE DUPLICATE eMail-Address. Or you decide to not delete users any more but only deactivate them. I have still to read the docs about deactivation, hoping that this keeps their enrolments as is. In principle we have to deal with two phenomenons: private eMail-Addresses changing from time to time and the opposite, private eMail-Addresses not changing for years. In our University we have a third phenomenon: we use shibboleth and before that LDAP Authentication. So even if people leave the school it is only a matter of time until the next student with the same name starts to study in our University and hence he/she will get the same eMail-Address, as firstname.lastname@ourEmailDomain.country So when deleting accounts you should alter the eMail-Address, e.g. firstname.lastname@ourEmailDomain.com.TimeStamp which would yield in every deleted user having another eMail-Address if the record is kept and never purged from the user-table. And this would allow for future same names to be created as new Moodle-Accounts without eMail-Conflicts. And on the other side to UNdelete a record if really the same person is coming back. For the moment I am thinking to only disable and not to delete any more. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blocking sub-domain addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: I had a similar problem recently except for denyemailaddresses. I may have come up with a solution, my one and only contribution to Moodle code, and that problem may be cured in recent versions of 1.6 beta. Please see: http://moodle.org/bugs/bug.php?op=show&bugid=5250&pos=1 From the above This is the line in moodlelib if (strpos($email, $deniedpattern) !== false) {   // Match! Aha...relying on the fact that strpos returns 0 if the string BEGINS with a string and then reversing them. How about if (strpos(strrev($email), strrev($deniedpattern)) === 0) { // Match! The above was used apparently. Hence, in recent versions of 1.6 beta, strings in denyemailaddress will match from the domain (or right hand end of the denyemailaddress string) and ignore subdomains, without using "@". I guess that the above type of reversed-string matching could, or should be applied to the allowed email addresses (domains) too. Tim

ResponsesInList.Title: Odp: Problem with reading details from Active Directory
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I found a solution. Thanks to Inaki. So if you are using a single LDAP plugin (with NTLM SSO enabled) to authenticate users from more than one domain, and you want to use data mapping you need to use userPrincipalName in your LDAP settings and patch the ntlmsso_magic() function in auth/ldap/auth.php. This is function to replace: function ntlmsso_magic($sesskey) { if (isset($_SERVER['REMOTE_USER']) && !empty($_SERVER['REMOTE_USER'])) { // HTTP __headers__ seem to be sent in ISO-8859-1 encoding // (according to my reading of RFC-1945, RFC-2616 and RFC-2617 and // my local tests), so we need to convert the REMOTE_USER value // (i.e., what we got from the HTTP WWW-Authenticate header) into UTF-8 $textlib = textlib_get_instance(); $username = $textlib->convert($_SERVER['REMOTE_USER'], 'iso-8859-1', 'utf-8'); switch ($this->config->ntlmsso_type) { case 'ntlm': In function you need to configure the mappings between your short AD domain names and the long ones. It's here: 'DOMAIN1' => 'domain1.forest-root.local', 'DOMAIN2' => 'domain2.forest-root.local', 'DOMAIN3' => 'domain3.forest-root.local',

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removed from AD users still in database after ldap sync
Re: Removed from AD users still in database after ldap sync
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michael, this is expected behaviour. Moodle doesn't remove the deleted user records from the user table. It simply marks them 'deleted' and modifies some fields (as you've seen) to avoid collisions with newer users. This is so content "owned" by the old user (like forum posts, etc.) can still be present in the system. Otherwise, it would need to either delete them (and all the content dependent on them, like forum replies) or assign them to another user. If you remove those user records, the content "owned" by them will be orphan. I suspect some code will not handle this situation gracefully Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Auth from Microsoft AD: Data Mapping "Email address" with 2 diffrent AD Attributes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, use commas (,) instead of semicolons (;) to separate the attributes (don't ask me why commas instead of semicolons; it's been like that since the beginning). And *DON'T* put spaces around the commas (it *might* work with some LDAP servers, but it's not guaranteed). Also bear in mind that the last attribute having a non-empty value "wins". I.e., the code doesn't stop as soon as it finds a non-empty value attribute in the list. It reads and processes the full list. So if you specify "StaffEmail,StudentEmail" and both attributes are set, then StudentEmail will be used. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP and security groups
ResponsesInList.Text: The short answer is: it's not straightforward, but it can be done The long answer involves creating LDAP filters to select only the subset of users you are interested in. Beware that the filters need to take into account both teachers AND students. Also note that this imposes a bit more load on the LDAP server while doing the searches for the users. The task is greatly simplified if, in addition to having a security group for your teachers, you can also have a security group with your students. Unfortunately in this case, you can't use nested groups, so you would need to put the students in the group directly (i.e., you can't use a group of groups). The following example is valid for MS Active Directory, so if you are using other LDAP directory you will need to adjust it. Let's assume we have a MS Active Directory domain called 'mydomain.local'. We have OU called 'moodle' hanging from the directory root. Inside it we have another OU called 'users' and inside that OU we have two security groups called 'students' and 'teachers'. We are going to use these two groups to group students and teachers respectively. Note that we can place the user accounts anywhere in the directory, we just need to put the two security groups in this place (to know their distinguished names beforehand). So you would fill in the 'Contexts' LDAP setting as usual. Then we can then use a LDAP filter like this to let only the users beloging to those groups. The filter is shown in multiple lines to make its structure more apparent, but you'd need to type it as a sigle line in the 'objecClass' LDAP setting: `` You can find out more about LDAP filters syntax in RFC-4515 ( http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4515 ) By the way, this filtering is applied only during syncing (but during loggin in) in Moodle 1.x, but is applied both during loggin in and syncing in Moodle 2.x Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm about to kick off a small pilot of Moodle using 30 or so users with manual accounts ahead of us buying in an MIS integration package that will run in conjunction with LDAP authentication. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Users moving from Manual to LDAP - what is best practice?
ResponsesInList.Text: The easiest way to change the authentication type from "manual" to "ldap" for a lot of users is to update the auth column on the mdl_user table in your Moodle database . For all users: UPDATE mdl_user SET auth = 'manual'; For one user: UPDATE mdl_user SET auth = 'manual' WHERE username = 'whatever'; If you're switching from MANUAL authentication to LDAP authentication then you don't need to do anything with the password - Moodle will use the users LDAP password for authentication. But going from LDAP to MANUAL might be more tricky...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP not listed in Upload Users menu after upgrade from 2.0 to 2.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rosario, the message is just a warning, not an error. I.e., the users are still added and work flawlessly. And as far as I know, nothing has changed in the mdl_user table (only a couple of additional fields added from 1.9 to 2.3, as far as I can see). What Petr says in the bug entry (well, my interpretation of what he says) is that the warning is there for a reason. If you upload your users via CSV and then you also use LDAP sync, (some or all of) your CSV-uploaded users might disappear (depending on your LDAP settings). It's exactly the same situation for external db, CAS, or any other external authentication plugin (specially if they have sync scripts). That's why only the internal authentication plugins are availble in the drop down menu (i.e., they are safe in this respect), and why you get the warning (not error!) with any other external auth plugin. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: If you have a Tree or a Forest of AD domains, as each domain has a different LDAP "root" (and possibly a different organizational structure), Moodle can't work with it. The current LDAP auth code only copes with a single directory "root". If you use the Global Catalog Services, Active Directory "hides" all the different individual directory "roots" and presents a "unified root" (it's not strictly this way, but you get the idea). It has a couple of quirks in certain scenarios (if you want to use LDAP enrolment, in addition to LDAP authentication), but otherwise can be a solution to this kind of setups. On the other hand, if you don't know if you are using Global Catalog Services or not, then you aren't , as it has to be explicitly configured (using the non-standard service ports I talked about earlier). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle and AERIES (California based SIS)
ResponsesInList.Text: Just wanted to share working settings on Moodle and AERIES for those curious about getting User Authentication working on Moodle using an AERIES Database (MS SQL Server ).  (AERIES is a Student Information System in California: if you don't live out here, this may still help provide clues to other SIS systems based on Windows Server/ IIS .) Assumptions Made: You're running the latest copy of AERIES.  You're using AERIES CS on a Windows Server with IIS 7 installed.  I also assume you know the basics of IIS (how to shut down a server, how to make a new site, etc.), and you've already installed and have running Moodle (either by hand, or using Web Platform Installer... which is NOT easy to do, BTW : there is a mix of lowercase, uppercase and numbers for the Database user password for Moodle.  It's not mentioned anywhere and it's asinine as heck, but after a mix of such, it worked.  I also used MySQL for Moodle's database: one, easier to configure; two, a level of abstraction away from the SQL DB -- if MySQL goes down, it doesn't affect AERIES and vice versa, plus Eagle Software doesn't have to contend with your Moodle install if they need to slash and burn ABI after a faulty upgrade. So, Moodle is humming along, and now you're faced with creating 100's of student accounts.  Or are you? First, we've got a SUP table to play with.  Make a field in SQL Management Studio (replace XX if you haven't made any yet, if you like).  This will hold your student password to get into Moodle.   Nothing magical about this field, just make the datatype nvarchar, and pick a field length (I go with 100, in case the student wants to use a sentence for a password.)  I named mine SUP.MDL, you might feel differently about that. Then, make a query to fill the new column with a default password.  I'm not at work and I can't remember the EXACT query, but it should be in the ballpark of this.  Again, run this in SQL Management Studio: UPDATE SUP SET SUP.MDL = REPLACE(CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), STU.BD, 1), '/', '') FROM SUP RIGHT JOIN STU ON SUP.SN = STU.SN WHERE SUP.MDL IS NULL This should convert the Student Birthdate into a 6 digit birthday to use as their default password: run this once and close it.  New students can choose their Moodle password at Registration, so it's unnecessary to keep running this (or have Student Services populate this with a Query of their own in AERIES.  Your call.)  Once done, go into AdminCS and Force an Update.  (This will avoid column errors in AERIES Client since the column is new and unknown.) Next, the settings in Moodle: Plugins, Authentication, Manage Authentication.  Sign on as an administrator to see this link, of course. -- Click on Configure on the External Database line. -- Enter in the following: Host IP (Local Address: your server is all that needs to find it.) Database: mssql_n Use sybase quotes: YES. DB Name, User, Password: Depends on your installation.  You should have made a read-only user who has read only access to the STU, SUP tables to read needed data. Curveball: Table should read "STU LEFT JOIN SUP ON STU.SN = SUP.SN".  You'll need to enforce the relationship in your SQL query on Moodle.  A left join does the trick. Username Field: STU.SN (Six digit Student Number, should match their ID Card so Barcode/Magstripe signons to Moodle are possible.) Password: Whatever field you made in SUP to hold the password.  I went with SUP.MDL for my installation. Password Format: Plain Text.  It's not hashed, or else an office worker would be unable to change the password. Debug ADOdb: YES until you know it works, then NO on production mode.  This gives helpful errors on bad logins so you can troubleshoot what happened with your SQL statement and modify accordingly.  Shut it off once it works. Set the rest of the form up as you want: choose which fields you want to populate with data from AERIES, pick whether or not you want to deactivate, delete or do nothing to users who aren't found in AERIES and still have an account on Moodle.  We have a lot of boomerang kids and this is a small district, so we opted for Suspend Inactives. -- Now save those settings, and head back to the Manage Authentication screen. Click the eyeball on External Database, and set the failover how you like it. Now, we're not finished.  If you try to sign on now, you'll get a 4004 error.  This means that the encoding used to save data on T-SQL in SQL Server and the encoding used on Moodle are two different things.  You need to follow these instructions and grab a copy of FreeTDL for your PHP Installation.  Setup is simple: place the .dll file in your PHP's /EXT directory, then insert the line "extension=filename.dll" for the FreeTDL you picked for your installation (Filename varies: Threaded/Not Threaded, etc.) under the Extensions heading in php.ini to load it on your next IIS restart. Restart IIS and try to sign on as a Student: open up AERIES and look up a student's ID Number (NOT the Permanent ID or SSID) and MDL Password in the Supplemental Data form.  If it works, shut Debug ADOdb off and enjoy! Again, this walkthrough makes a lot of assumptions about your installation, YMMV.  Don't be afraid to Google any error message you get and KEEP TRYING. (Carefully, of course: acting rash makes servers crash.)  You'll eventually get it together.

ResponsesInList.Text: I have a commercial Moodle site and would like to set up individual login pages for each of my clients.  The desired processing flow is shown below. The basic idea is to allow each client to have its own, branded login page where their employees can go to login and the next page they will see is the main page of the course that they are to take. I would create the login pages and pass to the Moodle authentication module the username, password, and destination URL . I know that it must be possible to do this using the Moodle login functionality because the login function already has the capability to transfer users directly to specific pages in the Moodle site immediately after login (for example, if you send someone a link to a lower level page, they will be intercepted by the login screen and then transferred directly to the target page after Moodle authenticates them. Can someone on this forum give me specific instructions on how I can set up a login form and pass the target page to the Moodle login routine, presumably through a hidden variable? Thanks, D. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Customized Login Pages for Commercial Moodle Site
ResponsesInList.Text: For your customised login page, all you need is something like this in each company's page: <FORM name = "moodle" action=" www.mymoodle.com/login/index.php " ENCTYPE=x-www-form-urlencoded METHOD="POST"> <INPUT TYPE="TEXT" NAME="username"> <INPUT TYPE="TEXT" NAME="password"> <INPUT TYPE="SUBMIT" value="Log In"> </FORM> Note that the NAME in the two input boxes has to be "username" and "password". How you would then incorporate an automatic redirect to the course I'm not sure, as I've never done it.  You might get away with putting the url of the course in the "action" instead of the login page.  Try it - it'll either work or it won't! If you can't set it up exactly as you're hoping, you could consider having separate Moodles for each company instead. HTH Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP: "Removed ext user", clarification needed
ResponsesInList.Text: I know, this topic has appeared a couple of times. I just want a confirmation whether I understand it right. Moodle version is 1.9.16. In LDAP (Users -> Authentication -> LDAP- Server -> Cron synchronization script) there is parameter "Removed ext user" which can be set to: "Keep internal", "Suspend internal" or "Full delete internal". This is how I understand them: - Keep internal: If the sync script does not find a record in the LDAP for a user, nothing happens. The user 'fcourse can not login due to the missing record, but once it reappears in LDAP he can continue everything from where he left. - Suspend internal: The sync script changes the login method for those users who have LDAP as their login method but do not exist in the LDAP database , the login method to "No login". Even if the user reappears in LDAP, but the sync script has not yet been run, the user can not login.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP: "Removed ext user", clarification needed
ResponsesInList.Text:
If the user reappears in LDAP, the sync script will create a new record (even if the "ID number" is the same?) Yes, a new user record will always be created, as the "ID number" is cleared as part of the old user deletion. Is it a sensible thing to do? I would say so. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP: "Removed ext user", clarification needed [SOLVED]
ResponsesInList.Text: The clean-up went without a single hitch! To sum up: - this particular site had Users -> Authentication -> LDAP-Server -> Cron synchronization script -> Removed ext user set to "Keep internal" for a couple of years. - I ran the sync script once with this parameter set to "Full delete internal", which did the clean-up. - I've set it back to "Keep internal". @ Iñaki A big "Thank you!" for your advice!

So after a bit more tinkering I found that if I added 'Domain Users', i.e. everyone into the group IIS_IUSRS then the automatic SSO works for all users. However, I'm still not convinced about the security of this and can only assume this is something to do with the php trying run under the user trying to log in rather than the webserver? (app pool identity?) I haven't played with IIS 7.5 yet, but up to IIS 7.0, the access to a protected page file (i.e., one configured not to allow anonymous access to) is controlled by the NTFS permissions of the file (and the permissions of the folders up in the path of the file). So as long as 'Users'[*] group (which contains both machine local users and domain-wide users, by default) has read permission and execute permission on the file that should work. [*] Replace 'Users' group with any security group you want to use to control access to that file (page). So I block permissions inheritance on that file (copying the permissions from the parent folder) and add the 'Users' group (if it's not already there) with read and execute permissions. I also completely remove IIS_IUSRS permissions on the file (only on that particular file), although I'm pretty sure there's no need for it once you remote 'Allow Anonymous Access' setting from the file in IIS settings. That should be enough (it certainly is with IIS 6.0 and 7.0). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: I would need to check the code more thoroughly, but at first glance I would say that not using 'samaccountname' as the 'user attribute' would break NTLM SSO (I'm strictly talking about NTLM SSO, I'm not 100% sure about Kerberos SSO). The reason is that, as far as I've able to check, when authenticating via IIS or Apache against a DC, you can only use NTLM or Kerberos (I'm excluding Basic and Digest Authentication here). NTLM is always a netbios-domainname\samaccountname value, and Kerberos is a (this is where I'm only 90% sure) samaccountname@dns-domainname value. So it's always samaccountname plus some extra details (and we strip those extra details in Moodle, as they are not relevant) Which means that in Moodle we need to work out who the user is from the samaccountname. And we work out who the user is by searching in the LDAP directory an entry whose 'user attribute' value matches the value we get from the web server (i.e., the samaccountname). So if we don't use samaccountname as the 'user attribute' in Moodle, unless the attribute we use holds exactly the same value as the samaccount attribute, we are not going to find the user in the LDAP directory. Which in turn means the SSO login process is going to return with a fail, and we are not going to let the user in via SSO. At least this is my understanding of the issue

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP auth problem w/ 1.7?
ResponsesInList.Text:
You need to alter the length of the idnumber field in of the mdl_user table in your database (using phpmyadmin or a SQL sentence), and then you need to edit .../moodle/lib/moodlelib.lib, at function truncate_userinfo() (around line 2281 for 1.7.1+) and change the line that reads: 
```text
'idnumber'    =>  64,
```
 to: 
```text
'idnumber'    =>  XXX,
```
 where XXX is the same length you used above for the idnumber field length. If you are using auth_ldap_sync_users.php, you also need to change .../moodle/auth/ldap/lib.php, in the auth_sync_users() function, where it creates the temporary table using something like: 
```text
execute_sql('CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ' . $CFG->prefix .'extuser (idnumber VARCHAR(64), PRIMARY KEY (idnumber)) TYPE=MyISAM',false);
```
 and chage that 64 to XXX like above. Saludos. Iñaki.

In that case, edit .../moodle/lib/moodlelib.php and search for the line that reads (around line 3561 in Moodle 1.7.1+): 
```text
return email_to_user($user, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 and add this line above the previous one: 
```text
email_to_user($from, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```

ResponsesInList.Title: users synchronization in AD
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings Moodlers, I am a familiar with Moodle, I have a question about the synchronization users with Activedirectory, the problem shows how can i modify the user information in Active directory through moodle user profile ? thanks for your cooperation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: users synchronization in AD
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, you need to cover at least three things: 1. You need to setup your LDAP servers to be able to use LDAP+SSL and configure Moodle to use LDAP+SSL too. You can have a look at http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/LDAP_authentication#Using_LDAPS_.28LDAP_.2B_SSL.29 for some help. 2. You need to use a binding user that can change other users details. This usually means a user that is part of the 'Account operators' group or the 'Administrators' group. I would use the former if at all possible (to reduce the attack surface). 3. In the 'Data mapping' section of the LDAP settings page, you need to configure the fields you are interested in updating in Active Directory and set 'Update external' to 'On update'. That should do it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.2, IIS 7.5, NTLM SSO & Google Chrome - Any Success?
ResponsesInList.Text: Scratch that - it seems our in house developer has had a look, and made a few changes to the authentication PHP files. I've pasted what was changed below. All that needs to be done on the auth.php is: Under the loginpage_hook() function there is: if(check_browser_version('MSIE')) This needs to be changed to: if((check_browser_version('MSIE')) || (check_browser_version('Chrome'))) The same also needs to be applied to the ntlmsso_magic.php file. We have also added our servers to Chrome's "AuthServerWhitelist" and “AuthNegotiateDeligateWhitelist” files via Windows GPO. Obviously we take no liability for any damage this may cause, but it seems to have fixed our issue, and maybe a few others too! If anyone has any queries please post them in here and I'll do my best to answer them

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Self-enrollement for just one module?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there. Well you could set up one course so that it allows guest access and so students could read (but not participate in) the module. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authentication Thoughts
ResponsesInList.Text:
Can Moodle cope with multiple Auth connections from the same type of datastore? As a general rule, it can't. Depending on the auth plugin, you can use some (external) tricks to make it work (like having an external auth db that uses views from several other auth db, to appear as a single auth db). Also can Moodle use the above method of auth with a mix of email, flat file, external database, radius etc Yes it can, as long as you only use one auth plugin of each kind (see above). Alternatively you could use some external auth system (OpenID, Shibboleth , etc) that uses all the disparate auth systems and present a single view to Moodle. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentification
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jedidiah, I have also been interested in limiting account access based on an LDAP attribute, but have not found a way to do this.  The best alternative I am aware of is to have the Moodle-allowed user accounts in a specific LDAP container, and then limit the LDAP search to that context (and it's subcontexts if desired). If anyone knows of a way to limit logins based on an LDAP attribute, I would also be interested in learning about it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentification
ResponsesInList.Text:
In the upcoming Moodle 2.0, you will be able to specify any valid LDAP filter as the objectClass value to filter the allowed users. If you want to have that feature in 1.9, you will need to modify function ldap_find_userdn() in auth/ldap/auth.php, using something like the attached patch. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentification
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Iñaki, Can you describe a little more how this will work in Moodle 2.0?  The reason I ask is because the LDAP settings page seems to be exactly the same between Moodle 1.9 and 2.0, so I am not clear where the LDAP filter can be utilized in 2.0.  You mentioned the Object Class field, but I don't see any difference between 1.9 and 2.0 for that field. Thank you for any clarification you can provide.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentification
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Greg, there's no difference in the GUI, only at the code level. In 1.9 (and below) the objectClass field value is used in some places to 'filter' the objects you get from the LDAP server . But the login code, where the user is authenticated against the LDAP server, is not one of them. This means that any user inside any of the configured LDAP contexts is able to log in (provided she has the right username/password, of course ). In Moodle 2.0 we've added the objectClass field value to the login code [1], as an additional 'restriction' (in addition to being in the right contexts and having the right username/password). This means that you can specify any valid LDAP filter (using the LDAP filter syntax specified in RFC 2254 ) to only allow a subset of the users in the configured contexts. For example, given Jedidiah Rex's requirement that users must have the authorizedService attribute set to Moodle in order to be able to log in, we could set objectClass to something like: 
```text
(&(objectClass=user)(authorizedService=Moodle))
```
 Saludos.
Iñaki. [1] More precisely to the ldap_get_userdn() function, that is used in a few more places too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Proposal for cas auth upgrade for avoiding direct attribute retrieval from ldap
ResponsesInList.Text: I would like to make a proposal regarding the cas authentication plugin. I noticed that until moodle 2.2.1+, the cas plugin uses ldap connection to retrieve the required user attributes. Also in the “cas server settings”, in moodle administration menu, you can choose only between cas 1.0 and 2.0 protocol, but not SAML 1.1. The disadvantage of the current cas auth plugin is that moodle is able to retrieve attributes from ldap ignoring the permitted set of attributes configured on cas server for the specific service. Since latest php cas libraries support SAML 1.1 protocol, moodle sould allow users to select this option too. If this protocol is used, then moodle could retrieve the required attributes (using the function phpCAS::getAttributes) from the cas server without the need of an ldap connection, exploiting the new enhanced architecture and features of latest version of cas server and SAML 1.1 protocol.

ResponsesInList.Text: Yes the ip address resolves when using the name of the new server with ping from the Linxu command-line. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing LDAP Server- error
ResponsesInList.Text: We fixed it.  It's working now. It was a simple DNS configuration problem. The old server used to act as the DNS server as well as AD.  When we set up the new server it took over the DNS and AD and the other worked as a backup. The server running Moodle never updated this in the resolv.conf file even after restarting.  So the whole problem was shutting down the old server eliminated Moodle's access to DNS. That means I mis-spoke when I said that the name resolved.  It resolved when the old server was running but not when the old server was shut down. Now that we have it pointed to the correct server everything is up and running. Thank you for your time and all of your help.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I would like to know if it's possible to have 2 different auth methods for the same user. So, we don't want to force them to use Shibboleth... Is it possible? It was possible in Moodle 1.9... can't do it now on Moodle 2.1... Missing something? Thanks! susana

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2 auth methods for the same user.. Possible?
ResponsesInList.Text: YES IT IS!! Before using Shibboleth I used LDAP to our Active Directory, where we used the SamAccountName as username. In our case firstname.lastname When I changed to Shibboleth, I switched to the user's eMail-Address so as to be unique even across our two Active Directory Domains. (we had conflicts in LDAP when two users had the same firstname.lastname, because Moodle's LDAP config allowed for more than one LDAP- Server , but the first one that contained firstname.lastname was taken for authorisation.) So, using the mail-Field of our Active Directory, I changed all userenames in the Moodle Database and also their auth from LDAP to Shibboleth with sql -queries. Now, when Shibboleth is down, I ENABLE the former LDAP auth module and tell the users to use the manual Moodle login box. I have inserted the AAI-Login-Box above the Moodle default login Block, see here: https://moodle.fhnw.ch And when Shibboleth works, I disable LDAP auth. (So that only manual and AAI users can log in) So in your case disabling the MANUAL auth Module is not possible, because you would also prevent the Moodle Admin from logging in. But as long as the usernames in Shibboleth/LDAP-mapping are the same you use for manual auth, everything works right. The only problem I see is with their passwords wich are stored separately in the Moodle DB for manual auth. In my case it is much easier, as the LDAP and Shibboleth look-up go to the same Active Directory user database anyway, so that the password is always the same independently from the auth module I use. OOOHHhh, Im speaking about Moodle 1.9.x I have a Moodle 2.05 Test-Server where I use the same Shibboleth auth module, which works fine. But I did not test my LDAP settings there. But I think this will work. The only problem I see are the passwords in manual auth. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2 auth methods for the same user.. Possible?
ResponsesInList.Text: If a user is auth="shibboleth" then he/she can't login using moodle username/pass. Even if the password field is filled... But I'm sure there must be way to enable both auth methods... susana

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2 auth methods for the same user.. Possible?
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, I am not sure... yes you must be right: existing users I would have to switch them from shibboleth to ldap with a query in the database. And new users would login with ldap and hence get auth=ldap but not shibboleth. But I am not sure of this, I would have to make a test. Actually I do not remember whether after the shibboleth service failed I really switched the users from auth=shibboleth to ldap. I think rather not, because I was surprised that they could log in, only after ENABLING the ldap auth module. Which would mean that independently of the auth setting of the users, the user authentication works in the order you specify in the auth module list. First manual, then shibboleth and finally ldap. I will test it right away and report back. NOPE, it DOES NOT work automatically. You have to switch the users' auth setting either to shibboleht, ldap or manual. Which in my case, just to have a fallback ermergency solution when our shibboleth Identity Provider fails, is enough. So according to what I read years ago when I wanted to use mutliple LDAP-Servers to be checked against, so as to be able to lookup a user with firstname.lastname in BOTH AD-Domains we have, the only solution was to change the ldap-auth-Code so as to check against the second Domain , when password for firstname.lastname failed on the first Domain. So maybe, in your case, you should combine both manual and shibboleth lookup in the same auth-Code you could call manualandshibboleth/auth.php This new auth plugin should be placed in the yourMoodleRoot/auth/ directory and should contain the auth.php script which would combine the logic to check manual and shibboleth. But I think the whole thing is not worth the extra work. Consider only the problems you would create for your users when they change their password which is lookedup by shibboleth and hence would not correscpond to what they typed in in their Moodle manual account or vice-versa, if they change the local password in Moodle and this one would be different from the shibboleth one. I think it is better to make the switch to Shibboleth and offer them a new login-box for shibboleth login. In this box (feel free to look at mine) I would simply comment out the code that lets them do the manual login. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Database Authentication Error? -2.1.2
ResponsesInList.Text: UPDATE: SOLVED I scraped some custom code from a previous environment and it was oversight on my behalf that I didn't notice the use of rs_fetch_record(). The solution was simple: I went into an old moodle(moodle-1.9.12) and in a file lib/dmllib.php is where rs_fetch_record() is defined. Really it was simply a matter of replacing $var = rs_fetch_record($rs) with $var = $rs->FetchObj(); I also had to replace rs_close($rs) with $rs->Close(); I hope this will help anyone in the future who runs into this issue. Tom
