ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Sync Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: It looks like the problem is you are only gettting 2000 users from Active Directory, instead of the 11500 you should get. It looks like you are hitting maxPageSize and thus missing a lot of users. The bad news is PHP doesn't support LDAP Paged Results yet, so the only way out is raising maxPageSize enough to get all the users. In fact, if you have users in several contexts, you only need to raise it to the cope with the biggest context , not the whole directory. The good news is PHP 5.4, when it's out, will support LDAP Paged Results, and so Moodle should be able to work with any maxPageSize value (once Moodle PHP code is modified to work with the new paging functions). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP to email based registration
ResponsesInList.Text: Can you tell me what would be involved in switching from an LDAP registration to a email based registration? Is there a way we can automate the update in our existing database ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP to email based registration
ResponsesInList.Text:
Very roughly, you need to do two things: assign a password to your existing LDAP users (as they no longer use the LDAP password). change the authentication method from 'ldap' to 'email'. Both things are stored in the mdl_user table, so it can be automated easily in the scripting language of your choice. If you are using password salting, you need to take that into account when assigning the new passwords. If you automate it in PHP, you can even use Moodle's existing functions to make it even easier Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: External databases & creating hashes in ColdFusion
ResponsesInList.Text: I am trying to set up an automated way to set up and enroll users in a course, once they have placed orders with a client of mine. The client would like to use their own registration system, as they can send out textbook orders from it and have other well-established operations they use it for. I have a function in the registration site, which is in ColdFusion, that generates passwords and user IDs. I've set up another function that passes these over to Moodle's mdl_user table. I've been having a bit of a time adding MD5 encryption to the passwords I am trying to send over. I've tried the Encrypt() function, but while the CF8 documentation claims to support the MD5 algorithm, in practice it doesn't. So I've used the Hash() function, with the following tag: <cfset raw_pass2 = Hash(raw_pass & salt, 'MD5')> Salt is the string from my config.php file (from the Moodle root directory) and raw_pass is the string I need to convert. However, the string I get, and pass over, does not work when I try to log in with the new account. I've tried switching the raw_pass and salt variables, but that result doesn't work either. I'm open to the possibility of another problem being at the root of this: at the time of registration, we only have the username and passwords, as the registrant is reserving spots in the course for their staff. The fields where I insert data are auth , confirmed , username , and password . Are there any others I should be filling out, even if with dummy data?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External databases & creating hashes in ColdFusion
ResponsesInList.Text: You could use the External Database Authentication plugin so you won't have to worry about the details of mdl_user. This will save you from maintaining your code to support Moodle upgrades that change the schema of mdl_user. It does have its own caveats, though -- i.e. it will also be responsible for removing users when it can't find them in the external source, by either 'suspending' them or deleting them, something you may be preferring to handle yourself. You do want to set the mnethostid attribute on every user you create to your Moodle's mnethostid -- the primary key for mdl_user is id,mnethostid,username. It will default to 0 but that probably isn't your real hostid, so that may mess something up. If I were looking into emulating creation of rows in mdl_user, I'd check lib/moodlelib.php, specifically the create_user_record function. From a glance, for instance, it strips spaces and transforms to lowercase the username, sets city to an empty string if not present, and sets the lang attribute to the site config's default language. I don't know however if that is the only function involved in creating users - there are some other tables ( ). If you're not interested in the External Database auth plugin, you could still go the Moodle route by using Moodle's web services. According to http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Web_services , Moodle 2.1 has a create_users() web service call. That would be first choice in theory, above auth/db and your own create user function. As for your Hash call,  I'm not certain why that isn't working. Moodle does this in moodlelib.php hash_internal_user_password() for the salt case: return md5($password.$CFG->passwordsaltmain); String concatenation operator in PHP is the dot (.),  and I looked up Coldfusion and it said string concatenation is &, which is what you have. Maybe you want to make sure again your salt variable is exactly the value of $CFG->passwordsaltmain in your Moodle's config.php. In PHP, $CFG->passwordsaltmain = 'xyz'; means set passwordsaltmain var on CFG object to the value xyz, NOT the value 'xyz' or 'xyz';, the ' are string delimiters and ; is end of line. Did you pick those up by mistake? HTH Credentials: I've only been hacking at Moodle and External Database auth. I've done what you're doing, an external registration system, but it's in PHP and it leverages the external db auth plugin as it was for designed for 1.9 (I wish I could re-code it for web services). I'm not a Moodle developer and only wanted to present my opinion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External databases & creating hashes in ColdFusion
ResponsesInList.Text: Setting the mnethostid field did the trick. Many thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customizing confirmation email
ResponsesInList.Text: I've got the same needs on my 1.8.4 install, and here's how I'm doing it: To print the additional data in your confirmation email, you need to collect it in the first place. If you take a gander around line 3620 in moodlelib.php, you'll see the email confirmation function. I want to collect my students last name as well as zip codes (a custom field I've added to my mdl_user table in the database ). To do this, I've added some extra lines to fill the $data object with a few more things: function send_confirmation_email($user) { global $CFG; $site = get_site(); $from = get_admin(); $data = new object(); $data->firstname = fullname($user); $data->lastname = ($user->lastname); $data->zipcode = ($user->zipcode); $data->sitename = format_string($site->fullname); $data->admin = fullname($from) .' ('. $from->email .')'; $subject = get_string('emailconfirmationsubject', '', format_string($site->fullname)); $data->link = $CFG-> wwwroot .'/login/confirm.php?data='. $user->secret .'/'. urlencode($user->username); $message = get_string('emailconfirmation', '', $data); $messagehtml = text_to_html(get_string('emailconfirmation', '', $data), false, false, true); $user->mailformat = 0; // Always send HTML version as well //send a copy of the confirmation email to the site admin (from moodle admin hacks ) email_to_user($from, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml); return email_to_user($user, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml); } So what's happening here from what I can tell is the $data object is getting packed with a few more elements (i'm thinking of $data as an array), which are then picked up in moodle.php through the $a pointer. One thing you might run into trouble with is the password variable. I'm not certain how the encryption works, and you'll have to experiment to see if anything sensible comes out in the email. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Login failure after disabling "no authentication"
ResponsesInList.Text: Regarding the query: UPDATE `mdl_user` SET `auth` = replace(auth,"original_value","manual") Although this query should work, there is a better way to write it: UPDATE mdl_user SET auth='manual' WHERE auth='original_value' (here, 'original_value' is the old value, 'manual' is the new value) The original query uses a string replace function to change the old value to the new value. That means the query goes through every row in the users table, checks if the old value is a string inside the auth value, and if so, replaces it with the new value, if not, leaves it alone. This has the desired effect, but it will take longer because of the way it is finding rows to change, AND, it has a dangerous side-effect: if the old auth value is a string that also appears inside other auth values, it will affect more rows than intended and change data not desired. For instance, suppose you have two auth plugins, db and dbsync (I'm making this up), and you use the query UPDATE `mdl_user` SET `auth` = replace(auth,"db","manual") to change users who are on the 'db' auth plugin over to the 'manual' auth plugin. Because this is using replace(), this will also change the users who are on the 'dbsync' plugin, because it will find the string 'db' inside 'dbsync'. Last of all, the function call replace(str, from_str, to_str) is specific to MySQL, and may be implemented under a different name, with different syntax, or not at all in other databases, whereas the UPDATE..SET..WHERE query I am suggesting instead is standard SQL syntax that all databases will support. As an added bonus, I think using WHERE to find the target rows to update will work more efficient, which may save some time for large user tables. I am not just nitpicking -- the query should do only what it is supposed to, and not everyone has MySQL.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle in a DMZ with NTLM
ResponsesInList.Text:
> When is the NTLM triggered? NTLM authentication is trigger if all the following conditions are met (I'm looking at the code to list them): NTLM is enabled (in the LDAP auth config settings) You have configured one or more subnets (IP ranges) for the clients you want to use NTLM with. So yes, it's mandatory You haven't specified the 'authldap_skipntlmsso' parameter with a non-zero value in the requested URL . You are the guest user, or you are still not logged in The IP of the client machine (as seen by the Moodle server!!!, so you need to take into account NAT, proxies, etc.) is inside of one of the configured subnets. It's a GET request, or a POST request from another page (not the login page itself). This is to handle a couple of corner cases. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle in a DMZ with NTLM
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Luis, Will NTLM SSO not work if this Subnet field is left blank? maybe the wording is a bit misleading, but the code is quite clear : if you don't specify a value in that field (i.e., left blank or just white space) NTLM will not work.In fact, Moodle won't even try to start using NTLM at all. Does Moodle now accept 0.0.0.0/0 as a subnet? Yes it does, meaning the usual thing: any ip, i.e., the whole IPv4 address space. In Moodle 2.x you can even specify the whole IPv6 address space using equivalent syntax (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0/0). Of course, you can specify both at the same time Moodle 1.9 has accepted it since MDL-19509 was fixed (June 2009). Moodle 2.x has accepted it since MDL-14123 was committed (January 2009). Saludos.
Iñaki.

If you don't find the username (or whatever LDAP attribute you are using for Moodle username) for the missing user there, then Moodle didn't got it from the LDAP server. You would need to add additional logging sentences in sync_users() to log which OUs Moodle is processing, which users gets from each OU and any additional information that can help track the root of the issue. My work-around for the issue was to create the temporary database with the utf8 character set and utf8_general_ci collation and that allowed the script to function properly. One question I do have is what the proper character set and collation is for the tables in the moodle database. ResponsesInList.Title: auth/db - need testers for scalability enhancements
ResponsesInList.Text: I have some pretty serious enhancements to auth/db that I am working on. If you are using 1.7/1.8, have a large number of users, and use the sync script, you might want to try this The changed auth/db is on a modified 1.8 - if they turn out to be good I'll merge them into 1.9. The branch is here http://git.catalyst.net.nz/gitweb?p=moodle-r2.git;a=shortlog;h=mdl18-local and you can get the latest version by clicking on the "snapshot" link on that page. With this code the sync should be much faster overall (time it before and after!) the sync script execution should take a lot less memory it used to fail if you had a large number of users - doesn't anymore if your remote db has a "last time this record changed" field that is a unix epoch, or you can synthetize one using a VIEW, set it in the config page, and watch updates get a hell of a lot faster I am working with 43K user accounts. Both DBs are PostgreSQL 8.1 and both are "local", meaning that I access them via a socket, not ethernet. So I get very low latency. Initial creation has gone from "does not even finish, dies after 20 minutes" to ~60m. Updates without the timemodified take also about 1hr. If I use the timemodified optimisation, updates take a couple of minutes. Unfortunately, I don't have a good example where "it works" before. Only have the "after". NOTE: if you are testing this code don't file bugs in the tracker. Just post here - this is experimental code. Edit: After the (still slow) initial run, normal daily updates (remove/add/delete a handful of accts) take anywhere between 30 and 60 seconds. I like this

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: auth/db - need testers for scalability enhancements
ResponsesInList.Text: OTOH, the branch may be breaking with some stuff I think Petr has been working on. Specifically Seiti's patch re MDL-9212 - I don't think we should ever disconnect explicitly. OTOH, I don't think we should use pconnections for auth/db so this should not be a problem. Connection is closed at the end of the HTTP request or cli script execution. Seiti's problem was with running the sync() - and with the proposed code there won't be a connection pileup. The "suspend" (re-set to auth='nologin') feature. I think it was buggy as those suspended users would never be revived, while deleted=1 users would. I think my patches fix this, but maybe I'm just misunderstanding how it's meant to work. And as of 1.8, I think we should default to saying `SET NAMES 'utf-8'` -- I think all the engines supported by PHP can deal with it. In any case, it should probably be the default. Even if the DB or table are not in utf-8, what that means is that we tell the ext DB that our SQL conversation with it is in utf-8. The ext DB will then translate if necessary.

But this all leads us to a situation that is not very useful: where the ext auth provider (db/ldap/etc) disables and account, and then reenables it, Moodle gets stuck and needs manual intervention. Moodle should just follow the ext auth system. So if we disable the acct when the ext auth system tells us to disable, then we must enable when the ext auth provider tells us to enable it. Another problem is that the suspended account doe
not know the original auth plugin. I agree this is a problem - that's why I think that automatically switching to "nologin" is a bad idea. I have a proposal instead: let's add an option to the user browsing under /admin to see deleted users. So admins can undelete the user (and reassign to 'manual' for example). To clarify - I maintain several installs where Moodle is driven from external systems with auth/db or auth/ldap, and the purpose of these plugins is automation. So accounts in moodle should never get stuck like they do now. With my patches auth/db will revive accounts matching the username. I think I will disable that - but we should also remove the option to set the acct to 'nologin'. Or add an entry to the users_preference table to track the "original" plugin. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: auth/db - need testers for scalability enhancements
ResponsesInList.Text: > I think it is exactly what Petr implemented, using the 'nologin' plugin. As I see it, it's different from what the nologin plugin does. First, with this nologin plugin you _must_ assign this auth plugin to the user, so you loose the user's original auth plugin. Which is a pita. But the current authentication schema (we just loop over the enabled plugins when the user doesn't have an assigned on, but go directly to the user's plugin when it has one setup) limits us severely in this area. If we followed the PAM schema (which is a good reference, IMHO), then we would loop over all of them, and an auth plugin would be anything that given a username and password would say if s/he was allowd to login or not (based on _any_ internal criteria the auth plugin wished). This would allow for suspended, rejected, or whatever black-list criteria you wanted to be implemented (can you say no logins between 02:00-06:00 local server time?), without having to tweak every other auth plugin when you add a new 'special mode' (or state, or whatever you want to call it). If we extended it for the password change process, we could even implement password policy support in a pluggable way (Anthony Borrow would specially like it ). Then you could see what users were suspended, rejected, blacklisted, ... just by having a look at that plugin config settings (because you'd set the list of suspended users in the suspend plugin and so on). Of course this is a bit different from the way we do things today, but I'd say is a more flexible and maintainable way of doing thigs. Either that or we set a new user setting: the mode (or state), which can be an enumerated value, for example: active, deleted, suspended and so on, and then let any auth/enrol plugin to deal with the mode/state in a way it sees fit. Saludos. Iñaki. Just my 0.02 euros

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm running Moodle 2.0.3, and I wasn't aware until all of my users were placed in suspend limbo due to an external database reboot that the suspend & revive logic wasn't finalized. I reported it a few days ago as MDL-29356 - as I wrote on there, I did some searching, and I saw this thread but didn't read into it (didn't expect this discussion to be under 'need testers for scalability enhancements', and also didn't believe yet this was really an unresolved thing; this thread hasn't been touched since 2007). The description for the 'Removed ext. user' setting in the auth/db configuration says, " Specify what to do with internal user account during mass synchronization when user was removed from external source. Overall, I've patched it myself, by changing the deleted=1 criteria to auth=nologin and changing the action from updating to deleted=0 to updating to auth=db. It's OK for our implementation to be blind in this fashion because I don't use any other auth plugins and nologin is only set by db suspend, so I can and do assume in my case that all nologin users were suspended by the db plugin. Although it works, I'm voting for a better designed, tested & certified Moodle.org solution. Most important of all obvious reasons is the fact that auth/db is a critical component of our Moodle and now this custom core patch has to be maintained by us throughout Moodle updates. I do see in the Moodle Roadmap that for 2.3 due in June 2012, there's "Oauth2 - cross-system authentication, for integration with other systems and to replace MNet.", but I'm not sure if this would include or could replace external database sync. Note that my MDL-29356 does duplicate MDL-9281 , however, 9281 is marked as resolved for 2.0, which I don't understand as it's broken in my 2.0.3. Since we have ~300 Students, I didn't want to have to go through the DB and manually change the fields, firstly because we don't bulk import and secondly because I'd have to wait until all the students have eventually logged in - and by then the admin email address would be full of bounce email errors. In order to get the filter working, I added a classification within AD to the Department attribute (set to either Admin, Teacher or Student). This attribute is then assigned to the department attribute within moodle when the user first logs in. Now we have a way to only disable the email address when the user is a Student. I then added the following code at line 3458 in moodlelib.php (between the existing email_is_not_allowed and the !isset($newuser-city) checks): if ($newuser->department == "Student") { $newuser->emailstop = 1; } This code solved my problem, but I thought I would put it out there to possibly take it further. I was thinking someone might be able to add a page within the Site administration (either within Users->Accounts or within the LDAP Authentication page itself) so admins can write a list of 'departments' that should have email disabled by default - provided that the department field is set correctly when importing from AD. You could potentially use any field - or make up a new one, but the department field was already in the database and was easier to implement. Now I need to backup the code so that a new moodlelib.php doesn't overwrite the changes.

This will send the user "You need to confirm your login" page and stop "function create_user_record($username, $password, $auth='')" creating a bare-bones user record. code before: if (auth_user_login($username, $password)) {  // Successful authentication if ($user->id) {                          // User already exists in database if (empty($user->auth)) {             // For some reason auth isn't set yet set_field('user', 'auth', $auth, 'username', $username); } update_internal_user_password($user, $password); if (!is_internal_auth()) {            // update user record from external DB $user = update_user_record($username); } } else { $user = create_user_record($username, $password, $auth); } code after: if (auth_user_login($username, $password)) {  // Successful authentication if ($user->id) {                          // User already exists in database if (empty($user->auth)) {             // For some reason auth isn't set yet set_field('user', 'auth', $auth, 'username', $username); } update_internal_user_password($user, $password); if (!is_internal_auth()) {            // update user record from external DB $user = update_user_record($username); } } else { // $user = create_user_record($username, $password, $auth); } I hope this helps

ResponsesInList.Title: controlling self-registration when using an external authentication source
ResponsesInList.Text: Just want to let you know that I have implemented an option to prevent creation of new user accounts even if user authenticates in external source. See MDL-12604 for instructions to modify POP3 plugin. This is coded in a way which should be adaptable to other plugins. In order to make it a generic feature, a new method is added to the authentication class. What the heck am I talking about? If an external authority source is used, like IMAP, POP3, LDAP , etc, Moodle will automatically create new accounts for users who authenticate in that source upon their first visit in local Moodle, effectively allowing users to self-register. While this is exactly desired in most cases, there is no way to use external authentication for Moodle sites requiring restricted access unless the plugin has specific provisions for that (like LDAP). The code presented here allows admins to decide whether self-registration is allowed or not. If not, the external authority is still used for authentication but only users with existing accounts can get in.

ResponsesInList.Title: Automated emails from Moodle and nhs.net

ResponsesInList.Text: Can you be more specific about the various problems?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated emails from Moodle and nhs.net
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Barbara I'm assuming that your Moodle installation is on a server that is on the NHS N3 network. If none of Moodle's automated emails are being sent then the it is almost certain to be a problem with your Moodle email configuration. I believe that the NHS network uses port 587 for SMTP submissions, so that your value for SMTP Hosts should be some thing like something.nhs.net:587 (where something.nhs.net is the name of the SMTP server). I believe that you will also have to authenticate to the SMTP server so you'll need to enter the appropriate username/password, probably best to use the credentials that go with the no-reply email address specified in the Moodle email config. To make matters worse, I wouldn't be surprised if the NHS SMTP server will only process messages that are sent by the authenticating user, which could be a problem with Moodle as it has a habit of sending messages from user email addresses. Hope this is of some help. Regards, Stephan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated emails from Moodle and nhs.net
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Stephan that's it's likely to be an issue with messages coming from the authenticating user, but it might be the receiving email gateway rather than the sending gateway that is blocking the emails, but kind of for the same reason... I've had a similar problem in the past - the email gateway, which was on the same domain as the moodle server, said 'I can only accept genuine example.gov.uk address from this domain, ie. sent by this server.' So, when a moodle user contributed to a forum and their email address on moodle was fred@example.gov.uk, the email was sent - but the receiving email server said, "this cannot be a genuine example.gov.uk email address as it wasn't sent by the example.gov.uk email servers so it must be spam ... I'll reject it." And because I was the moodle admin and also had an example.gov.uk email address, we had the same problem with self registration, updating passwords, etc. It was possible for my IT dept to add the moodle server IP as a genuine server though, which sorted the problem - but you'll need to talk to your local Trust IT folk.

Where I can only obtain IDnumber, then I can upload through flatfile. Additionally, when loading new users, it would be extremely beneficial to check not just the existing usernames and email addresses, but also the student IDnumber to avoid duplicates. *  operation, role, idnumber(user), idnumber(course) [, starttime, endtime]


```text
where:


*  operation        = add | del


*  role             = student | teacher | teacheredit


*  idnumber(user)   = idnumber in the user table NB not id


*  idnumber(course) = idnumber in the course table NB not id


*  starttime        = start time (in seconds since epoch) - optional


*  endtime          = end time (in seconds since epoch) - optional
```

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rosario, it looks like Suhoshin is preventing Moodle from raising the memory limit to 96MB in lib/setuplib.php (line 905). This may be the reason why certains things are missing in the output (I'm not 100% sure, but it's a real possibility). While you may get the same alert in 1.9.12+, it may happen that that version never really needs more memory than the limit imposed by Suhoshin, while 2.0.x actually needs it. Find your Suhoshin config file (in Debian/Ubuntu it's under /etc/php5/conf.d/suhosin.ini) and raise the memory limit there (parameter 'suhosin.memory_limit'). You might need to restart the web service for the changes to make effect. I'd raise it to a generous limit (say 256MB) to confirm/deny this is actually the root of the problem, and then try to find a lower limit that is suitable for your installation. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP taking over 60 seconds to authenticate in Moodle 2.0.2
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm glad you finally fixed it! I think that if you don't set a limit especifically in suhoshin.ini, it takes de php.ini limit by default. With respect to what's the advice for 2.x, I've seen several numbers floating around (64MB, 96MB, etc.), but given that setuplib.php tries to raise it to 96MB (that's the number Suhoshin shows in the logs) I suspect that's a good choice for normal installs. Anyway, that number depends a lot on the size of your install and the size of your activities . Backups may require more memory than that temporarily (as well as restores) and large complex quizzes may require it too. Upgrades also tend to require more memory Looking at the code, it tries to set the limit to 96MB for 32bit installs, and 128MB for 64 bits installs (this usually needs more memory), and 256MB/384MB for upgrades and cron jobs. The memory limit can be temporarily raised by calling init_set(), if the function is not disabled in php config or if you don't enforce it with suhoshin or similar tools. This is why most people don't notice any problem even if their php.ini imposes lower limits. Saludos. Iñaki.

The First Name maps to givenName The surname maps to sn The email address maps to email The city maps to L (only the letter L, maybe for Location) The country maps to co These are the names of the attributes/variables in Active Directory. You can discover such names with utilities like ldp.exe or other AD-browsers. Of course, if you use LDAP to another type of directory, you must map to those names. Rosario (dalla Svizzera, saluti)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Possible to enforce password standards?
ResponsesInList.Text: I have downloaded patch for windows (from http://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/patch.htm), a copy of 1.7.1+ current as of today and the patch for 1.7.x from the bugtracker. It seems patch for windows doesn't like the Unix end of line convention and aborts with a nice assertion. But I have opened the patch file in Wordpad, saved it as a 'MS-DOS Text File' (to convert it to MS-DOS end of line convention) and tried again. And it has worked like a charm (one of the hunks is applied successfully with an offset of 2 lines, but this is not a problem). What I did: 1.- Download and extract patch for windows from above URL. I placed the patch.exe binary in C:\bin 2.- Download and extract Moodle somewhere. I placed it in C:\moodle-171 3.- Download the patch file and place it in the same directory you put Moodle (C:\moodle-171\password-policy-17.diff) 4.- Open the patch file with Wordpad, and click 'File' >> 'Save as...', choose a different name for the file (I used 'password-policy-17-dos.diff') and "Save as type" >> 'Text Document - MS-DOS Format' 5.- Open up a command text window, and type: cd \moodle-171 c:\bin\patch.exe -p1 < password-policy-17-doc.diff 6.- You should get an output similar to this: patching file admin/settings/security.php patching file lang/en_utf8/admin.php patching file lib/moodlelib.php patching file login/change_password.php patching file login/signup.php patching file user/edit.php Hunk #1 succeeded at 430 (offset 2 lines). And that's it. In Linux you do much the same, but you don't need an external patch command binary (use the one that comes with your Linux distro) and you can skip step 4. Saludos. Iñaki.

The problem appears to have to do with authentication: if, using Firefox, I go to the source code and copy the URL of the image that was supposed to have appeared, I am given a login screen. So, it appears that with Firefox, Moodle is losing track of the fact that the user has already logged in, and is denying access to the photos for lack of authentication. In order to fix the issue, I have to go and reinsert the images and other media in their respective pages, which is a tremendous amount of work, because we have many, many embedded media files in our various courses, all of whose links break after the upgrade. For this reason, we're leery of performing more upgrades (for instance to Moodle 2.0), until we can be sure that doing so won't go and break all of our media links. Any help with this issue will be greatly appreciated. -Erik Norvelle

ResponsesInList.Title: AD sychronization max limit on Windows 2008 server
ResponsesInList.Text: We are using AD as our LDAP server (Windows 2008) According to MS KB: http://support.microsoft.com/kb/2009267 Hardcoded LDAP limitations have been introduced in Windows Server 2008 R2 and Windows Server 2008 to prevent overloading the domain controller. These limits overwrite the LDAP policy setting when the policy value should be higher. Could it handle our 200,000 accounts?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AD sychronization max limit on Windows 2008 server
ResponsesInList.Text: According to that MS KB, no it won't. There's a hard-coded limit of 20,000 entries (MaxPageSize), so even if you raise the value of MaxPageSize to 200,000 in your LDAP policy settings, W2008 will only return 20,000 accounts. For this to work, you need to patch PHP to add LDAP Paged Results support (see PHP bug #42060 at http://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=42060 ) and then patch Moodle to use Paged Results (see https://github.com/jcharaoui/moodle-cegep/wiki/PHP-LDAP-Paging ) While this is not supported by the PHP[1] or Moodle dev teams, there are several people using it in production environments. But YMMV Saludos. Iñaki. [1] Though PHP 5.4 might have Paged Results support, as the patch has already been applied to it (and trunk too)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AD sychronization max limit on Windows 2008 server
ResponsesInList.Text: What about php 5.3.6? Was it patched too?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AD sychronization max limit on Windows 2008 server
ResponsesInList.Text: No it wasn't. PHP policy regarding new features is that they don't add new features in released versions. So PHP 5.3.x won't have official Paged Results support. Only PHP 5.4.x (when it is released[1]) and later versions will official support it. Of course, that doesn't mean you can't patch PHP 5.3.6 yourself and recompile it. That's what people have been doing so far

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternate Login URL
ResponsesInList.Text: You must change the 'your url' to a valid URL that leads to a working alternate login page containing the form fields described above. The text 'your url' is not a valid URL and will break Moodle. It is probably safer to put in the following line instead: $CFG->alternateloginurl = ''; Note that it is two single quotes before the semicolon, not one double-quote. And you must include the semicolon at the end. This line will stop Moodle from going to whatever non-working alternate login URL you entered by mistake, and return it to normal operation so you can go in and change the alternate login URL setting in Moodle. After deleting or fixing the alternate login URL, you should delete the line you added to the config.php file, unless you want the alternate login URL to be completely disabled. NOTE: you should always create a backup of your config.php file before making any changes! Even if you know what you are doing, you are still human and mistakes can happen. Also note that editing the mdl_config table in the database, as described elsewhere in this thread, is probably a better solution than editing your config.php file because it fixes the real problem immediately. But if you are not comfortable working directly with databases, editing the config.php file is a good workaround.

ResponsesInList.Text: Try this.  This is what worked for me.  I had to do this with some Library web based software the other day in order to use a domain name with NTLM.  From a previous post.... In Registry Editor, locate and then click the following registry key: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 Right-click MSV1_0 , point to New , and then click Multi-String Value . Type BackConnectionHostNames , and then press ENTER. Right-click BackConnectionHostNames , and then click Modify . After reading Virkam's reply, it occurred to me the "log out the others" approach has a weakness: 2nd user logs in causing 1st user to be logged out 1st user logs in moments later causing second user to be logged out And the go back and forth. This -does- create an inconvenience and will no doubt deter many, but not the persistent. Two ideas for refinement come to mind: Notify each person that another person is using the account which should be used only by the rightful account-holder. The rightful owner then knows someone else is using the
account, and may choose to change the password so others don't
interfere with his activities . Institute a time delay before a subsequent login will be accepted. To further increase the 'inconvenience', a deterrent to 'abuse' of use of the account. These might have the added benefit of deterring users from sharing their accounts, which may be the -real- problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: iis 401.1 ERROR with NTLM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jamie I've solved it.  Hacking the registry on Windows Server 2008 R2 to accept the domain name.  What a workaround! If anyone else gets this - have a look at http://support.microsoft.com/kb/896861 Click Start , click Run , type regedit , and then click OK . In Registry Editor, locate and then click the following registry key: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 Right-click MSV1_0 , point to New , and then click Multi-String Value . Type BackConnectionHostNames , and then press ENTER. Right-click BackConnectionHostNames , and then click Modify . In the Value data box, type the host name or the host names for the sites that are on the local computer, and then click OK . Quit Registry Editor, and then restart the IISAdmin service.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ldap configuration / setup issues
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I don't know where the prvious poster got the idea that Microsoft Active Directory is not LDAP, but I assure you it does work. Is your moodle server and AD domain controller on the same physical network? So long as your Moodle server can connect to your AD Domain Controller you should be fine, You need to set up a user in AD that moodle can use to query AD. In Moodle/LDAP Host URL = IP Address of the DC/AD Server Version 3 is working fine for me. LDAP encoding, I am using UTF-8 Hide Passwords Now here is the tricky bit. The Distinguished name is the username that you created to search with in this format: CN=<username>,OU=<The OU the user is in>,DC=<the domain name>,DC=local then the password for that account. Your Contexts should look like this: ou=<OU for all the users>,dc=<Domain Name>,dc=local if you have search sub contexts=yes, then any OU's within the OU specified will also be searched for the users. in user attribute, set it to sAMAccountName That should then set you up for AD/LDAP authentication. You may want to set the password to never expire, saves you coming back to change the password.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication with TLS and ldap_start_tls
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, I've figured it out. This is just a quick dirty hack to make it work. For a production setup you would need an enable TLS option in the LDAP config screen that would set a variable and cal the ldap_start_tls function in the /auth/ldap/auth.php file. To get it to work open the /auth/ldap/auth.php file and find the following function: function ldap_connect($binddn='',$bindpwd='') { about 24 lines down you will find this line: ldap_set_option($connresult, LDAP_OPT_PROTOCOL_VERSION, $this->config->version); Add this line after it to give you this: ldap_set_option($connresult, LDAP_OPT_PROTOCOL_VERSION, $this->config->version); ldap_start_tls($connresult); For this to work you MUST select LDAP ver. 3 and you MUST have at least a starting context for LDAP searches. I played with it all day and couldn't get it to work until I added the starting context to the LDAP config screen.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Authentication with TLS and ldap_start_tls
ResponsesInList.Text: I found that for Moodle 2.0.2 the same command ( ldap_start_tls($connresult); ) needed to be placed in /var/www/moodle/lib/ldaplib.php just below these lines: if (!empty($ldap_version)) { ldap_set_option($connresult, LDAP_OPT_PROTOCOL_VERSION, $ldap_version); }

ResponsesInList.Title: Any problem with using Email self-registration and LDAP authentication at the same time?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Is there any problem with using the "Email-based self-registration" and " LDAP server " authentication methods at the same time? I plan to use these four authentication plugins in a Moodle site: Manual accounts No login Email-based self-registration LDAP server Up until now, I have been using the first three authentication methods, but now want to add the LDAP method to make logging in easier for new students (i.e. facilitate single-sign-on within the university). I have read the LDAP authentication documentation , and believe that with the help of our IT people I can make it work. However, before going ahead with this, I'd like to check that adding the "LDAP server" authentication plugin will not cause any problems for existing users. In particular, I'd like to know what happens if an existing user (i.e. one that has been authenticated via Email-based self-registration or Manually) tries to login using their Password and Username for the university system to which the LDAP system is linked? Is there a possibility / danger of them inadvertently creating a second account? i.e. my understanding of LDAP is that when a student logs in for the first time the system "recognises" them because their login details exist on the LDAP server, but because it is their "first time" they have to fill in their name etc. in order to create their account on the Moodle database . However, I can imagine two scenarios that may cause problems: A student who has already been registered to the Moodle system might 'accidentally' use their university Username and password to login to Moodle. Moodle will recognise them as existing on the LDAP server, but new to the Moodle system and so create a new Moodle account. So the problem is that this student will have two accounts. A student used the same login details as his university account when he created his Moodle account via "Email-based self-registration". What will happen when he tries to login to Moodle after "LDAP server" authentication has been activated? Will Moodle recognise him as an existing user, or a new user existing on the LDAP server, and so end up with the same problem in scenario one; one student but two Moodle accounts? No doubt I'm missing something obvious, but would like to be certain before going ahead with activating the "LDAP server" authentication method.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Login problems - password characters
ResponsesInList.Text: While my original set of special characters for passwords was larger, after using it for some time I ended discarding the \|@#¿¡^[]{} symbols because they were problematic for unexperienced users: some were "difficult" to find and many needed the AltGr key to be pressed. Now, in order to stop making any more assumptions, I decided to take my latest set of allowed characters, discard the ' " symbols and test the rest by following the same procedure used before. In all eight tests: * One domain having magic_quotes_gpc = On - with one subdomain with Moodle 1.9.9+ (Build: 20100728) - and another subdomain with Moodle 2.0.1 (Build: 20101225) * Another domain having magic_quotes_gpc = Off - with one subdomain with Moodle 1.9.10 (Build: 20101027) - and another subdomain with Moodle 2.0.1 (Build: 20101225) * And using two input methods (manual entry & file upload) in each case... The resulting hash in the DB "password" field was exactly the same.. phew! So, hoping this might be helpful for someone, here is the set of special characters I would recommend for passwords (well, at least until some dark configuration somewhere forces me to reconsider it): ! $ % & ) ( * + , - . / : ; < = > ? _ Cheers!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [FORGET IT]  Teachers thrown out (from their Moodle courses)
ResponsesInList.Text:
> My question still "In a ldap-authenticated system like this, when does Moodle look again in a course whether somebody is still enrolled or not?" It does it every time they log in. The thing is (in Moodle 1.x) , if the LDAP enrolment plugin can't connect to the LDAP server, it doesn't change the enrolments at all. So if a user was previously enroled, she'll stay enroled as long as Moodle can't contact the LDAP server. On the other hand, if Moodle can connect but can't read anything back from the LDAP server, it will unenrol the user from all the courses where she was enroled through LDAP (and only those). In Moodle 1.x, LDAP enrolment doesn't set an expiration date either, so even if you have a course duration set and run cron.php regularly, it won't affect LDAP enroled users (i.e., they won't get unenroled at all). Moodle 2.0.x should behave the same way (but I've only had a fast look at the code to confirm it). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Joomla authentication plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: (It appears the lang file isn't being read) A couple of things Joel, make sure you turned off the external db authentication. As for the settings: Enter your Joomla database information (this information can be found in your Joomla configuration file). Make sure the Password format is set to Plain text. Under Data Mapping, enter "email" for Email address. New users coming from Joomla to Moodle will be taken first to their Moodle profile to update their information and preferences. Note: This setup will NOT get users from Moodle into Joomla. To get the DB Name, DB Username, and Password fields info, open your Joomla/configuration.php file and find: $mosConfig_db = '____'; $mosConfig_user = '_____'; $mosConfig_password = '_____'; The Table, Username field, and Password fields should be: jos_users, username, and password Also, Sometimes the Moodle admin cannot login into Moodle through Joomla using external authentication because Moodle automatically sets the admin user's authentication to "manual". As a safeguard, create a second Moodle administrator account and set the authentication method to "external db". And, you might try creating a new account in Joomla, then test to see if that works.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CAS version
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Heather, this is either '1.0' or '2.0' (without the quotes). It refers to the CAS authentication protocol version supported by your CAS server. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi thanks for that slightly depressing news. My Moodle is a 1.9.5 so when did the phpCAS thing get updated, do we know? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CAS version
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Heather, the good news is you don't have to upgrade to 2.0 to get the updated CAS client library . The latest 1.8 (1.8.14) and 1.9 (1.9.10) versions already have it. In 1.9.x, it was updated in 1.9.9 and then again in 1.9.10 (there were several different vulnerabilities that were fixed in different versions of phpCAS library, so we end up upgrading a couple of times). If you can't upgrade to 1.9.10+ (you should, there are other security vulnerabilities in 1.9.5 too), you can still upgrade your CAS auth plugin manually. Simply download a copy of 1.9.10+ and unzip it to a temporary location. Remove (i.e., move it to another place, in case you want to go back ) the existing auth/cas directory in your 1.9.5 directory and copy the auth/cas directory from the 1.9.10+ directory to the 1.9.5 directory. Then go to the CAS authentication settings page and check that everything is configured as expected (there's no need to go to the notifications page to trigger an update, as we are not touching the database at all) Regarding the drop down menu for choosing the CAS version, there isn't one (it seems I was clear as mud ). It's a text field, but I think it should be a drop down menu with only valid choices. Judging by the version number you mention in your original post (3.4.2) I suspect you are running JASIG CAS Server, version 3.4.2. If this is so, you should specifiy CAS vesion '2.0' (without the quotes). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Auth - Ubuntu 8.04LTS/Moodle 1.9.4
ResponsesInList.Text: I knew if I kept Googling I would finally turn up something of use. I added this line to /etc/ldap/ldap.conf and everything started working beautifully: TLS_REQCERT never

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Auth - Ubuntu 8.04LTS/Moodle 1.9.4
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Wade, Your thread helped we solve my problem. I think this site will be helpful to copy the config text. http://www.openldap.org/lists/openldap-technical/200910/msg00121.html

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Auth - Ubuntu 8.04LTS/Moodle 1.9.4
ResponsesInList.Text: Wade, Thanks for your great suggestion. The setting you mentioned had solved my problem with configure secure LDAP server. Before that, I had been working for more than half day to slove it! Greate thanks! Later, I googled more to find the detailed reason why "TLS_REQCERT never" works. As default setting, the certificant on server side is demanded by client when starting ldap request session. However, in some case the LDAP server (like my LDAP server) couldn't provide any certificant or any valid certificant, then the LDAP session will be terminated. On moolde frontpage, you will see the error "LDAP-module cannot connect to any servers". After adding "TLS_REQCERT never", LDAP client (here is Moodle) won't ask for any certificant from LDAP server, so the error won't pop up anymore. (Of course remember to restart your HTTP server to let Moodle picked this setting up!) I have checked other possible settings as well. Using "TLS_REQCERT allow"should work as well. "TLS_REQCERT allow" means LDAP server is allowed to just provide any certificant or even a bad certificant to client. I didn't try this setting, but I suppose it should work. Anyway, set TLS_REQCERT to never is good enough to work out this silly issue! Hope my post explained somehow.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom authentication plugin copies password to local database
ResponsesInList.Text:
It's up to your own plugin to decide where to check & store the user password. If you don't want to store and check the password locally, you should: define a class method called is_internal() that returns false, to tell Moodle that it shouldn't store user passwords and other details in the local database; in your user_login() class method, check the user credentials against the external database only. That should do it Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How working with Moodle when username is not unique
ResponsesInList.Text: HI Jakub, Generally speaking, it is one of the assumptions of these kind of systems that the username will be unique, or that there exists some sort of location, server name or organisational unit information which can be used to make a unique username. I expect that if you follow this through, there will be several places in moodle core code and various modules where breaking this basic assumtion will cause some unexpected problems. It would be good to tackle this as soon as you and a migration such as this is an ideal time to do it. Could you think of any kind of " domain " or "location" or "organisational unit" information which you could add onto the existing usernames to make them unique? Otherwise perhaps your migration process could create unique usernames by appending either an incrementing number or perhaps the userid onto the moodle username jakub, jakub-2, jakub-3.  Or make semi-anonymous usernames giving everyone usernames such as as moodle-(userid)  eg.  moodle-57, moodle-58, moodle-59 etc. Perhaps you could continue to use your  your local non-unique usernames and use your authentication plugin to recognise the local usernames and match them onto the appropriate unique moodle names. Avoiding this may cause you some difficulties in the longer term. -- Sean Farrell Edinburgh, Scotland

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP Integration with Mac OS X 10.6 Open Directory
ResponsesInList.Text: I've integrated Moodle (Linux) with Mac OS X 10.6 Open Directory via LDAP . Users get created automatically by running the auth_ldap_sync_users.php script in [moddle directory]/auth/ldap. Works great but... How does one prevent users that have been disabled in Open Directory from being imported into Moodle when running auth_ldap_sync_users.php?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Integration with Mac OS X 10.6 Open Directory
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Andreas, you can use a LDAP filter in the objectClass setting, in the LDAP configuration page. I don't know what Open Directory does when you disable a user. But let's say (for the sake of the argument) that it modifies the 'userEnabled' attribute and sets it to false, while the enabled users have it set to true. You can specify a filter like: `(&(objectClass=user)(userEnabled=true))` which means that Moodle will only sync accounts that are of 'user' type, and have their 'userEnabled' attribute set to true. By the way, in Moodle 1.9 this only works when you use auth_ldap_sync_users.php, not when your users log in directly. Moodle 2.0 will usesit in both cases. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Password Expiry
ResponsesInList.Text: As far as I know, this is not possible. Moodle doesn't record the time of the last password change anywhere (that I'm aware of) and consequently nothing checks such a (non existant) value. You'd need to extend the database to store that value, and a configuration setting to specify how much time passwords last (so you can check if a given password is expired or not) and then add the code to check if it has expired. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Password is not being populated in External Db Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text:
But the password was not populated even if it is marked as internal .
I think all the steps are correct ! do you see any mistake ? No, I don't see any mistakes. But when you set password as internal, it doesn't populate the password field. It creates a pair of records in mdl_user_preferences, where it stores that the user needs a temporary password created ('create_password' preference), and that the password should be changed the next time s/he logs in ('auth_forcepasswordchange' preference). When the next cron invocation runs, it processes the first record ('create_password') and then creates the password. So unless you run cron manually, you'll need to wait for the next cron invocation to see the password field populated with the temporary password. In fact, this kind of 'cleanup task' doesn't run every time cron runs, but only 20% of the times cron runs. So it may take a little time to populate the fileds, unless you run cron manually a few times. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP with Microsoft Active Directory and SPA (Secure Password Authentication)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Robert, I suspect you are still missing a couple of things. The certificate that URL is talking about is not the X.509 certificate of your Moodle web site, but the certificate of the domain controller server you are running LDAP authenticating against. That means that you either have Certificate Services installed on one of your domain controllers (configured as a Corporate CA, for example; this is exactly what I did in my test environment) and create the domain controller certificate, or you create a certificate request for that server and submit it to a recognized certification authority to get it signed. In the last case, be sure to follow Microsoft guidelines when create the certificate as it has to have the right combination of settings. Once you have the certificate created and installed in the domain controller (again, check Microsoft documentation on how to do this), you'll probably need to reboot the server (I think this is no longer needed in W2008, but I'm not 100% sure). You'll need to use this same certificate in the instructions given in the URL of my previous post. You can extract it from the Certificates store of the domain controller. Make sure you extract it as a Base-64 encoded X.509 certificate (also know as PEM format). With all this done, you can then follow the instructions from the given URL. This is what I did to test the patch. Saludos.
Iñaki.

El moodle lo tenemos en un servidor de hosting en Internet, y el AD y el NAS estaran en local. Ya tengo solucionado el tema de generar las contraseñas en MD4 para el AD, lo que necesitaria saber es dónde está el código php de moodle para el alta de usuario y el cambio de contraseña (y asi poder generar la MD4 si se cambia la contraseña o se inscribe un nuevo usuario). Muchas gracias por tu ayuda. Luis ----------------- Iñaki Arenaza escribió: Hola Luis, veo que tu problema es ligeramente diferente de lo que yo creía. Un primer problema es que no es posible recodificar una contraseña que está en MD5 para pasarla a MD4 (sin saber la contraseña original sin cifrar). Podrías modificar el código para generar las contraseñas en MD4 cuando el usuario la introduzca la siguiente vez, pero entonces no podrías validarla, ya que no puedes compararla con la que ya tenías de antes en MD5. La única forma viable de hacerlo sería cambiándole la contraseña a todo el mundo de una sola vez. En todo caso, si ya tienes un Active Directory (AD), no entiendo para que quieren los chicos de AD las contraseñas de los usuarios de Moodle. Porque doy por sentado que ya tienes AD instalado y funcionando en uno o varios servidores Windows, ¿no? Si los usuarios ya existen en AD, cuando configuras Moodle para validar a los usuarios por medio de LDAP contra AD se usan las contraseñas del propio AD. De hecho, ni siquiera se guardan (por defecto) las contraseñas en Moodle. Así es como están funcionando nuestras instalaciones desde hace más de 4 años. Y supongo que el NAS funcionará de igual manera. Lo unes al dominio de AD y automáticamente valida el nombre de usuario y contraseña contra un controlador de dominio (o más de uno, depende de la configuración que permita el NAS), sin tener que mantener una copia local de dichos datos. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Code for new user and change password
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi again Luis, the functions to validate and update the user password are validate_internal_user_password() and hash_internal_user_password(), in lib/moodlelib.php That's where you should change using the MD4 hash instead of the MD5 hash. Bear in mind that while MD5 hash if a standard hash function in PHP that comes compiled by default, MD4 is not. In order to compute a MD4 hash, you need to use the hash() function (see http://www.php.net/manual/en/function.hash.php ), assuming that your PHP compile includes the MD4 algorithm (you can use the hash_algos() function to check it; see http://www.php.net/manual/en/function.hash-algos.php ). Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Authentication vs. Account Provisioning
ResponsesInList.Text: The LDAP and CAS authentication plugins handle ahead-of-time account provisioning. It appears to me that none of the other authentication plugins do this. This might be a big change, but it seems that account provisioning should be handled separately from authentication. We're moving from LDAP to Shibboleth . In Shibboleth, there's (generally) no single directory in which to look people up ahead of time. So we have to write some custom code to do our ahead-of-time account provisioning that we get for free with the LDAP authentication method. It would be great (in my opinion) if Moodle admins could specify authentication configuration in one place, and then account provisioning would be specified somewhere else. If you happen to be using LDAP as your authentication, there can be a checkbox in the account provisioning config for using your LDAP settings to retrieve users. But, as in our case, if you're using Shibboleth, maybe you need to specify an LDAP server (or database to connect to, or file to read, or whatever) and provision the accounts from there. Separating the two items would make things much more flexible. (Pre-emptive strike on the expected "why do you have to provision accounts ahead of time when the accounts are created at first login" question: Often, people are enrolled manually. Provisioning the accounts ahead of time means that the instructor can locate and enroll the student through searching before the user has logged into Moodle for the first time.) Sample screenshot of what it might sorta kinda look like attached.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authentication vs. Account Provisioning
ResponsesInList.Text:
The LDAP and CAS authentication plugins handle ahead-of-time account provisioning. It appears to me that none of the other authentication plugins do this. FWIW, external database also provides account provisioning On the other hand, what you propose breaks a current fundamental assumption in all the authentication plugins: the plugin that creates a user is the one used to authenticate it. Nothing insurmountable, but we'd need to be able to know what "final" authentication plugin we'd need to use when we provision users using a given authentication plugin. I.e., we may be provisining users using the LDAP plugin with a final LDAP authentication plugin (current behaviour), or we may be provisioning users using LDAP plugin with a final Sibboleth auth plugin. The code should be able to deal with both cases (at least). Anyway, you can use the " upload users" feature and specify all the user details, including the authentication plugin assigned to that user, right now, without having to code a single line or modify anything. Isn't that suited to your needs? Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: תשובה ל: Re: External DataBase works only with host=localhost?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Then I'd check a couple things You can ping the database host from your moodle server. This check srouting and/or firewalling on both hosts. Both servers being on the same subnet leaves routing out of the question, but it's a good idea in general. Once you can ping the database server, try connecting to the database service port (e.g., 3306 by default for MySQL , 5432 by default for PostgreSQL , etc.). This checks any firewalling issue again, and that your database server is actually configured to listen to remote connections (not only local ones). By the way, you don't have to put 'http://' in there. That's only for HTTP (i.e., web) connections, nothing else Saludos.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to retrieve MoodleSession cookie from within (customized) login/index.php
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, I need to seamlessly and silently pre-login users from my primary sub- domain into my Moodle instance (on a friendly sub-domain). I remotely post my custom login/index.php passing user credentials into it and need to return MoodleSession cookie to set it in a requesters browser session. I successfully retrieve MoodleSessionTest cookie value, however MoodleSession cookie comes back blank, even though I do see that the both cookie values are successfully set in the browser as a result of script run. Could someone please help me understand behavior of MoodleSession cookie and capture its value? I have a fresh Moodle installation (2 months old). Here is a code extract from my custom login/index.php : ################################################################################### print_footer();

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to retrieve MoodleSession cookie from within (customized) login/index.php
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Oleg, I think the problem is that MoodleSession cookie hasn't been sent to the client yet (you have just posted to a Moodle page, and the HTTP response hasn't been sent back yet, as you are still executing the page request), and thus you won't have it in $_COOKIES by default ($_COOKIES is filled in by the client on the HTTP request). The old saying goes like "you can not set a cookie on a page and test for it in the same page", which is what you are doing. Both MoodleSessionTest and MoodleSession are set in lib/setup.php, but MoodleSessionTest is put into $_COOKIES by Moodle code. That's why you can see MoodleSessionTest but not MoodleSession. Anyway, if you are posting to login/index.php from your remote app, you should get both cookies in the response, so you could get them from there, couldn't you? Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Not reading properly names from a UTF-8 encoded external database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Our Moodle 1.9.4 installation is using an external MySQL 5.0 database for user authentication. The external database is properly set to UTF-8 and of course it contains UTF-8-encoded data. At our Moodle config, the external database encoding is set to "utf-8". So everything looks right and works fine with "normal" usernames, but when Moodle reads a strange character-containing (I mean a non ISO-8859-1 character) username from the external database, Moodle truncates the string at that strange character position, so in mdl_user table it inserts a truncated username. I've tested this with a PHP script (UTF-8-encoded too) and Moodle behaves like my test script when I read from the database without doing a my sql _query("SET NAMES UTF8"); first. Any idea of why Moodle behaves this way even though everything is UTF-8 encoded and set? Thank you! PS: The info from the thread Special and characters con tilde (accute accent) when connected to external database hasn't helped me much.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not reading properly names from a UTF-8 encoded external database
ResponsesInList.Text: The encoding you specify in the 'External db encoding' setting is only used to convert the strings you get from the database into UTF-8 (which Moodle uses internally). But you need to setup the communications with your database in the right character encoding, at least with MySQL. That dependes on several factors (you can read the whole details in the MySQL docs), including the default character set configured in the client libraries. It seems your MySQL client libraries are not configured to connect using UTF-8, so you need to set it with the 'SET NAMES UTF-8' query explicitly. This is why Moodle offers the 'SQL setup command' configuration setting, so you can put there any SQL sentence you need to setup the communication 'in the proper way'. Just type "SET NAMES 'utf8'" (withtout the double quotes) there and it should work as expected :-) Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Swap to LDAP niggles
ResponsesInList.Text: All sorted -the field was in Table "mdl_user_preferences", Field was "name", and data was "auth_forcepasswordchange=1" and the change involved was making this data = 0 For prosperity we ran two MySQL queries -the first as a check which gets all affected users for checking purposes: select id from mdl_user_preferences pref where pref.name like 'auth_forcepasswordchange' and value =1 and userid in And the second that actually does the updates of all affected users: update mdl_user_preferences pref set value=0 where pref.name like 'auth_forcepasswordchange' and value =1 and userid in ( select id from mdl_user where auth like 'ldap' ) We have ~5000 affected users and this took less than a second to run on the test box (read: old PC under my desk) and was near instantaneous on the live system -just in case anyone was wondering what impact this had.. So now after a successful log on (part of which involves changing their Active Directory password) the users no longer have to change their password again!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Odg: Re: Struggling with NTLM Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Marko, Make sure you have correctly setup your subnet mask settings in the LDAP Server Settings page under NTLM SSO. Also, you will need to ensure that the client your are accessing Moodle from is actually coming from that subnet and there is no re-routing in transit. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP bind error
ResponsesInList.Text: FIXED, here is what I did. My server required strong authentication so I edited these settings to enable simple binding. Configuring the Directory to require LDAP Server Signing Using Group Policy Click Start, click Run, type mmc.exe , and then click OK. On the File menu, click Add/Remove Snap-in. In the Add or Remove Snap-ins dialog box, click Group Policy Management Editor, click Add. In the Select Group Policy Object dialog box, click Browse. In the Browse for a Group Policy Object dialog box, click Default Domain Policy under the Domains, OUs and linked Group Policy Objects area, and then click OK. Click Finish. Click OK. Expand Default Domain Controller Policy, expand Computer Configuration, expand Policies, expand Windows Settings, expand Security Settings, expand Local Policies, and then expand Security Options. Right-click Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements, and then click Properties. Click the drop down box AND SELECT "None", and then click OK. Using Group Policy (setting of the client LDAP signing requirement) Click Start, click Run, type mmc.exe , and then click OK. On the File menu, click Add/Remove Snap-in. In the Add or Remove Snap-ins dialog box, click Group Policy Object Editor, and then click Add. Click Finish. Click OK. Expand Local Computer Policy, expand Computer Configuration, expand Policies, expand Windows Settings, expand Security Settings, expand Local Policies, and then expand Security Options. Right-click Network security: LDAP client signing requirements, and then click Properties. Click the drop down box AND SELECT "None", and then click OK. Please put this in the documentation somewhere, PLEASE!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk User Action: Force Password Change
ResponsesInList.Text: Personally though, as mentioned above, if password complexity is in place, I would like to see the ability to set a password - perhaps even one based on a %f%l type template - that meets the password complexity. The problem with this approach (in addition to the code complexity sorrounding the template processing and error handling) is that you cannot guarantee that the generated password complies with the policy, unless you specify a way for the template to signal 'lowercase this part' or 'uppercase this part'. If you don't have this, you need to relay on certain fields (surname, first name, etc.) having a particular case. I'd say this is not robust enough. On the other hand, with the new generate_password() going in in short (see MDL-14104 ), we can simply use it to generate a random password that meets all the configured password complexity settings. This has a drawback: we no longer know the new user password, so we can't tell her/him. But we can specify 'changeme' as the password in the CSV file and, if we have a password policy in place, handle it a special way. We do the check you proposed above and later on, once we have updated or created the user, we set the 'auth_forcepasswordchange' flag for that user (to force a password change upon next logon) and call reset_password_and_mail(). This function creates a new random password (by calling generate_password()) and then mails the user with the password details. What do you think of it? Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk User Action: Force Password Change
ResponsesInList.Text: Anthony, having a look at MDL-13557 I see you mention key logging and password stealing as one of the reasons for the forced password change. But I think in this particular situation a password reset is a much better option. I mean, if an attacker has stolen a victim's password and you force a password change, the attacker might try to login before the victim does, so the attacker will have the opportunity to set a new (temporay) password and then reset it back to the original one (so the victim doesn't notice the password change at all). On the other hand, if you were able to bulk reset passwords, this kind of attack would not be possible. Password reset emails the new password to the victim (and ideally we would force a password change upon next login), so unless the attacker has also access to the victim's email, he won't be able to use the victims account any more (provided the keyloggers are removed, etc.). So maybe two different options are in order here: bulk force password change bulk password reset If the password reset is augmented with the suggestion you make in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=93569 that would provide a more robust solution, don't you think? Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk User Action: Force Password Change
ResponsesInList.Text: Iñaki - Yes, I agree two separate options would make more sense and be more powerful for the administrator. I was simply trying to make a case for a potential use of the force password change but yesterday began to realize the importance of setting a password and a bulk password reset would also be great according to a certain pattern. Used together I think that admins around the world might sleep better Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students who don't have e-mail addresses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sallie You may want to look at this (somewhat lively) thread which discussed this same problem. If you still want to avoid having to enter the email address, then make these changes by commenting-out lines in the code which check for the email address (add '//' to the start of the lines): 1. moodle/user/editlib.php line 84 add // to the start of the line like this: // $mform->addRule('email', $strrequired, 'required', null, 'client'); 2. moodle/user/edit_form.php line 104 add // to the start of the line like this: // $errors['email'] = get_string('invalidemail'); 3. moodle/user/editadvancedform.php line 146 add // to the start of the line like this: // $err['email'] = get_string('invalidemail'); Two big health warnings: - make backups of the original files first before saving your changes. - the line numbers are for Moodle 1.9, so may be different for your version. Just search to find the text of the line instead. - these changes may cause errors in emails which are sent as a result of grading feedback or activity work, so please test on a non-production system first. Finally, there is a very good reason why Moodle developers have designated email as a required field, so be careful when changing these default settings as it could break things we're not aware of. Hope this helps! Ken

If NTLM SSO is working when you go to "moodlesite/auth/ldap/ntlmsso_attempt.php" and it doesn't trigger automatically when you click on the "login" link, then you have probably configured the NTLM SSO subnets setting wrong. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: new user on external sever; how to update LDAP to allow Moodle login?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Alisa, moodle automatically recognises new profiles created on your LDAP server, provided they are created in the containers (contexts) Moodle will be looking into. I mean, if you have configured your Moodle LDAP settings to look for users in the 'ou=students,ou=moodle,dc=my- domain ,dc=local' context (for example) and you create your new students in 'ou=other-users,ou=my-users,dc=my-domain,dc=local', Moodle won't find them, neither automatically nor with the sync process. On the other hand, the sync with your LDAP server will not delete your "external" students, as they will be using 'manual' or 'email' authentication, and the LDAP plugin only manages those users with 'ldap' authentication. Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Syncronisation with AUTH_LDAP_SYNC_USERS.PHP produces fewer accounts than it should
ResponsesInList.Text:
This is a known problem, widely discussed in the forums PHP LDAP module doesn't support LDAP paged results, which means that we the number of 'objects' a given search is greater than the server side search limit, you only get a partial result set. MS Active Directory has a default search limit of 1000 'objects', so anything that requests more objects than that limit, is trimmed to the first 1000 objects. Without having a look at your LDAP settings it's a bit difficult to confirm it, but it looks like you could have a wrong LDAP configuration, as you only get 570 out of 1914 users, which is below the 1000 object limit mentionned above. If you only have 1914 users, you might consider raising the MS Active Directory limit (that shouldn't impact AD performance that much) as specified here http://docs.moodle.org/en/Active_Directory#Group_Policy_Objects . For larger sites with thousands of users, there's a patch for PHP that I maintain at http://www.eteo.mondragon.edu/descargas/php-ldap/ and a Moodle patch that Jérôme Charaoui developed to use the paged results feature, available at http://wiki.github.com/jcharaoui/mdl19-cegep/php-ldap-paging . Saludos,
Iñaki.

See below for another example - this time returning a subset with > 1000 results. Configuring temp table Creating temp table mdl_extuser Connecting to ldap... + 1000 users + 1000 users + 1000 users + 401 users Got 1231 records from LDAP These are all the records that I need to pre-populate Moodle with (3401) I should say that our Moodle installation with our AD as a data source appears to be working fine. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Syncronisation with AUTH_LDAP_SYNC_USERS.PHP produces fewer accounts than it should
ResponsesInList.Text:
auth_ldap_sync_users.php uses the 'user attribute' value to retrieve the users from the LDAP server, and it retrieves exactly that value for each user. I guess you have specified 'mail' as the user attribute judging from your last paragraph. Then it inserts the values in a temporary table. If you have specified an attribute whose value is not unique for each user (e.g., two users have the same email address in your case) then you would get less users than you actually have, as some records would get overwrittern. It looks like this is what's happening to you, as you insert 1000 + 1000 + 1000 + 401 records in the temporary table, but when Moodle counts the number of records in that table shortly afterwards it only gets 1231 records. If you enable database query logging, you could confirm/deny this. Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Syncronisation with AUTH_LDAP_SYNC_USERS.PHP produces fewer accounts than it should
ResponsesInList.Text: The way we had to get around this problem was by editing auth/ldap/auth_ldap_sync_users.php, and around line 44: $ldapauth->sync_users(1000, true); change 1000 to 1. Otherwise it would only pull a fraction of our 37k user accounts into Moodle; I decremented the number from 1000 down to 1 by increments of 100, and using a value of 1 was the only way to get it to work reliably. (We use uid for our unique attribute since it's eDirectory, which is a globally unique identifier.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP authentication- student account not deleting?
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you doing the ldap sync process with your ldap server ? With the LDAP authentication, the only way I've seen an account get automatically deleted is if you're doing the ldap sync process and the user gets deleted from the LDAP server - the account deletion will then propagate over to the Moodle user database . However, if you are using the LDAP sync process and the user gets deleted from Moodle but not the LDAP server, then it will readd the user to Moodle on the next sync. If you're not using the LDAP sync process, the only way I know of to autodelete the user from Moodle would be to use a manual script, etc., since old users remain in the db for in case they get enrolled in a different course later. The only automatic user purging stuff I see is under Administration...Server...Cleanup, and that's just for incomplete registrations, etc., not inactive accounts. We're using 1.9.7+
