I just upgraded from 1.4.3 to 1.6.5 to 1.8.2. moodle/auth/fc/auth.php (mostly port -> fppport fixes): Line 91: $fpp = new fcFPP($this->config->host, $this->config-> port ); Fixed: $fpp = new fcFPP($this->config->host, $this->config-> fppport ); Line 124: $fpp = new fcFPP($this->config->host, $this->config-> port ); Fixed: $fpp = new fcFPP($this->config->host, $this->config-> fppport ); This is the one that fixes the "Host" error with saving data. Line 227: set_config('host', $config-> user , 'auth/fc'); Fixed: set_config('host', $config-> host , 'auth/fc'); moodle/auth/fc/fcFPP.php - this fixes connection error messages: Line 53: print_error('auth_fcconnfail','auth', array($errno, $errstr)); Fixed: print_error('auth_fcconnfail','auth', '', array($errno, $errstr)); Lastly - and this one is entirely cosmetic (fixes printing a double colon): moodle/lang/en_utf8/auth.php Line 125: $string['auth_fchost_key'] = 'Host : '; Fixed: $string['auth_fchost_key'] = 'Host'; I'm attaching copies of the files I modified. Everything worked for me after I fixed the fppport typos but in the process I tracked down the host-saving issue and a problem with the error messages. Hopefully this helps somebody. Jonathan

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP Alternate Login Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Recently we upgraded from 1.8.1 to 1.9.7 Using NTLM authentication page to go to an altenate login page and get automatically signed in. I used to have it set to /moodle/auth/ntlm/oncampuslogin.php However after the upgrade it no longer worked and I was forced to put the full url as in http://myserver/moodle/auth/ntlm/oncampuslogin.php This worked fine for users on the domain but for external access - we needed the FQDN namely https://myserver.ac.uk/moodle/auth/ntlm/oncampuslogin.php and in this case clicking login was taking the user back to the non FQDN http://myserver/moodle/auth/ntlm/oncampuslogin.php and erroring. To resolve the issue :- In moodle\login\index.php around line 264 the following code /// Redirect to alternative login URL if needed if (!empty($CFG->alternateloginurl)) { $loginurl = $CFG->alternateloginurl; Was ammended to /// Redirect to alternative login URL if needed if (!empty($CFG->alternateloginurl)) { $loginurl = $CFG-> wwwroot .'/'.$CFG->alternateloginurl; Thus removing the need to specify http://myserver/moodle/ and allowing internal and external access to  function correctly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advice for single sign on - which method

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Advice for single sign on - which method
ResponsesInList.Text: NTLM should be really easy as it's built into the LDAP auth in 1.9 that you are already using - if you specify the ip range correctly, then your off-campus users won't notice a difference, buy your on-campus users will love it! - When setting up the ip ranges, it would be good to talk to your network admin to find out if there is a specific internal IP address range that includes machines that are connected to AD - machines that aren't connected to AD such as guest laptops using a wireless network won't be authenticated to AD and will have to use the normal forms based authentication as it stands now.... for example - you might have a series of VLANs - one for student lab pcs connected to AD, one for staff machines connected to AD, one for Staff laptops, one for wireless users, one for users in the on-campus accomodation etc etc... - some of these will likely be connected to AD, some won't. The machines that aren't in the domain will attempt NTLM and eventually redirect the user to the standard forms based auth, but this takes a bit of extra time that you can avoid it by specifying the correct IP range for NTLM machines. you could also get a Moodle Partner in to help enable Moodle Networking accross the existing sites - it's a bit messy initially, but it should be possible! hope that helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ignoring session_start and $ldap_user_attribute errors when using LDAP/CAS
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jaswant! I found very helpful talking to phpCAS developers on their mailing list, really useful people. With their help and entering debug strings in the code of moodle, I managed to solve the problem and I hope my solution could be helpful to you. First of all, update phpCAS to the latest trunk. Joachim Fritchi, one of phpCAS developers, patched it to solve some of the problems made evident by my setup: session management was bugged. Secondly, there's something tricky in the way moodle manages users. Once a user logs in, a line in the table mdl_users is entered with some details from the user, including its authentication method. In my case, I realised that "ldap" had been inserted for my user - as I had logged in via ldap so this had been stored. As it happen, the key issue is in the /lib/libmoodle.php, that gets info on the user from the table mdl_users. If a user have previously logged in to moodle, the method of authentication stored in mdl_users is then re-used by libmoodle .php when asked to authenticate. What happens is that if you have previously logged in using some other method, e.g. ldap, this is the one that's going to be used and cas is ignored. This is also misleading, as if you configure your authentication to be "cas,ldap" it will work - leading you to think cas was used when it was not! So always try using "cas" only rather than "cas,ldap". However, all you have to do to avoid ldap or whatever old method being used is to delete the user entries from mdl_users when starting to use CAS authentication. I'm investigating if the fact that these db entries are persistent is in fact a bug. So, quick solution: 1. Update phpcas 2. Delete your entry from "mdl_users" 3. (IMPORTANT) Set just "cas" as auth in mdl_config, and NOT "cas,ldap" (or whatever other means you use). I hope that helps, please let me know!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Last release (1.9): having problems with uploading user
ResponsesInList.Text: So I ran into the same problem, and figured it out. Explanation: (skip if uninterested haha) So i had all the columns lined up perfectly and keep getting that error message "number is not constant!" .. so if you open up your CSV from excel in something like text or wordpad, you'll see something peculiar. What happens is that if for some reason, the last column has ANY empty values, then it is ignored when being converted to CSV and the comma is left out. CSV does not recognize multiple commas at the end of the row as the last entries. Solution Make sure that the last column when creating your CSV contains all entries filled in. I set mine with a user's first name as the last column, as it is the simplest one to use since everyone should have one. The order of columns in the CSV is irrelevant, as they are routed to the profile fields anyway, so you can manipulate it that way. Hope that works! if not, then i apologize for the long explanation!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM Single Sign On - I think im going mad
ResponsesInList.Text:
Sorry for the delay, that doesn't look like an error (as far as I can tell). If you want to check whether NTLM authentication is working with Apache, in addition to having the test.php file you've shown (say, in /var/www/moodle/auth/ldap), you'll need to add the following block of lines inside your apache2.conf: 
```text
        <files test.php>
                NTLMAuth on
                AuthType NTLM
                AuthName "Moodle NTLM Authentication"
                NTLMAuthHelper "/usr/bin/ntlm_auth --helper-protocol=squid-2.5-ntlmssp"
                NTLMBasicAuthoritative on
                require valid-user
        </files>
```
 right below the equivalent lines for the ntlmsso_magic.php file. And then after restarting apache, you'll need to go to http://your.moodle.site/auth/ldap/test.php and see if you are authenticated and your username is displayed in the page. Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authenticating users from other sites to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi! I tried to go about doing a similar thing. I started by reading the following and following the steps to go about creating the basic authentication plugin. It uses my own way of authentication via checking the incoming password's hash against a secret hash key. http://docs.moodle.org/en/Authentication_FAQ Once I had done that moodle accepted my user's login details but still remained the issue of creating users who weren't already on moodle's internal database. It would prompt the user coming in to create their profile on moodle once they had logged in. Now since that is work duplication for the user(He/She has already logged in through my external site and shouldn't have to do so again), I had to think of something to avoid that and bypass the new user registration. I wanted moodle to use my user's existing credentials on the external site to be passed onto moodle and moodle should just accept those and create the user automatically. The result should be the same user being logged in as him or her in moodle home page. Once the requirements were clear I looked at the authentication API http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Authentication_API NB: By this point I had a basic auth plugin which implemented the mandatory function user_login() So moodle calls this when going through all the auth plugins and checks if the user checks out. ~Once that happens it also looks for any user information - name, email address, and other credentials to populate it's database(especially if the user does not exist on moodle yet), that it does by calling an optional function in the auth plugin called get_userinfo($username) - Refer to API above. Note that The api says auth_user_login() and auth_get_userinfo(), they have changed in moodle 1.9 to just user_login($username, $password) and get_userinfo($username). So I implemented the get_userinfo($username) in the auth plugin and in there I basically defined it in a similar way to the get_userinfo() method in the 'FC' auth plugin ( You should be able to find the existing code in your moodle install /auth/fc/auth.php.) $fname = $_REQUEST['fname']; if(isset($fname)) { $userinfo['firstname'] = $fname; //moodle db key firstname } the other moodle db keys are lastname, email, country, city, you could probably look the rest of the keys up in the moodle db itself using phpmyadmin for custom credentials. So I got the credential first name from the REQUEST Object(*) which was passed from my external site as part of the POST request as a hidden parameter alongside username and password. *Had a php script on my external site which sent the username and password to the moodle login website http://moodlecomputer/login/index.php as a POST action page for a form with input elements such as username, password, email, and other credentials needed for moodle to make the new user on its internal database. So the auth plugin picks up the information as above and when get_userinfo() is called by moodle it creaes the user with those credentials, job done!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Google Authentication

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Resource id #36' Bind result
ResponsesInList.Text:
Im an enterprise admin on the domain and i used cn=myLoginID,dc=ourDomain,dc=local I hope this is just a copy & paste typo, but users in Active Directory are by default (unless you create them in a specific OU) inside cn=users,dc=yourdomain,dc=local. So that should be cn=yourloginid,cn=users,dc=ourDomain,dc=local In fact, it may happen that your actual login ID (what MS calls the sAMAccountName) and the value you specify in cn=.... are different. A lot of people put 'full names' in the cn (Like 'Iñaki Arenaza'), but use 'short names' for the sAMAccountName (like 'iarenaza'). Make really sure you are using the right value for the cn. Active Directory Explorer (a tool you can download for free from Microsoft; Google for adexplorer and you'll find it easily) is a great tool to see all the attributes of any AD object (more visual and intuitive than ldap.exe, IMHO ). With that tool you should be able to locate any user in the left AD tree, and once you select it, you'll see all the user attributes on the right pane. Just look for the 'distinguishedName' attribute and that's exactly what you need to connect to AD via LDAP. Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Limit some accounts by IP address
ResponsesInList.Text: While it's not already there in the form you need, part of the infrastructure is available. There was some talk during the 1.6 (or 1.7 can't remember it now) planning, to make the authentication system behave like the Unix PAM auth system, where you can stack modules. The idea was to be able to have multiple auth subsystems enabled at the same time. (Edit: I've found the thread where it was discussed: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=31863 ) The final result wasn't like PAM, but the login logic was changed a bit and several constants were defined (in lib/authlib.php) to be able to make stackable modules a possibility, but we didn't change the login logic. So instead of auth plugins returning true/false, they should return AUTH_OK, AUTH_FAIL, AUTH_DENIED, AUTH_ERROR (these names don't match with the names used by Martin L. in his description but are the same conceptually). And the login code (probably inside authenticate_user_login()) should implement the loop Martin L. describes. This way, implementing new types of black lists should be as easy as adding new auth plugins. They are self contained (no need to patch core further), have their own settings storage (no need to add/modify tables) and can be ordered the way you want to get almost any desired effect (e.g. block this ip range irrespective of the user vs block this user if it comes from this ip range). What do you think?

AD?) or the whole authenticating process depends on the userid? Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: same login account on OpenLDAP and Active Directory
ResponsesInList.Text: It depends on whether the user account already exists or not. If it doesn't, then Moodle will check the authentication plugins in the defined order. So it will check the first one, and if the password matches, it will create the user and store the authentication plugin used to validate that user. If the passwords don't match (but a user with that name actually exists in that ldap server ), Moodle will refuse the login saying that either the username or the password are wrong. If the user doesn't exist in the first ldap server it will try with the second and apply the same logic. Once the users are created, they'll always use 'their' ldap server (the one that was stored in their first login). Saludos, Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Students Unable to move pass Update Profile when logging in

There have been other people talking recently about disabling email in Moodle; however my view is that your school would be better off to allow student email in some form (either provided by the school or opening up external email) if they are serious about using an online learning system like Moodle. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hartmut, You can place the «Site Administration» block back to your title page: to do that you should turn on editing mode and add this block to the page (via the «Blocks > Add» block at the bottom of the right column). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM troubles
ResponsesInList.Text:
Having read permission on the file is just enough On the other hand, if you get the login box it means Integrated Windows Authentication is doing its job and is requesting the user credentials. You can have a look at http://www.microsoft.com/windows/ie/ie6/using/howto/security/setup.mspx (the section called 'Setting Up the Local Intranet Zone'. ResponsesInList.Title: User authentication process (detailed)
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been trying to test (with no luck) some of the authentication plugins in Moodle. I'm having trouble looking for documentation that explains the user authentication process. Maybe somebody can explain it here or point me to the documentation url to answer this simple question. How does moodle handle the authentication process internally, step by step? I mean, does it first look for the user in the user's table that match the username entered and then "executes" the authentications plugins in the order configured by the administrators (stopping at the first success)? Or is it the other way around: it first authenticates the user via authentication plugins enabled and once any of them succeed, it selects the user from the user's table (or creates it if it that not exists)? Or maybe is something completely different from those alternatives. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User authentication process (detailed)
ResponsesInList.Text:
It's a mix of what you say. If the user already exists, the user table records his/her authentication plugin (in the 'auth' field') and Moodle uses that plugin directly. If the user doesn't exist, the enabled plugins are tried in the order configured by the administrator. As soon as a plugin succeeds, no other plugins are tried and a new entry is created for the user in the user table and the 'auth' field is set to the name of the plugin (so it can be used directly in future logins). Most of the logic is at .../login/index.php Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone. Is there a way of changing the default options for people self registering?  I want all new accounts to have the default mailtype set to plain text (0).  Is there anyway to do this? Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Change default enrolment settings
ResponsesInList.Text:
You need to change the default value for the 'mailformat' column in table mdl_user in your Moodle database . If you are using MySQL and Moodle 1.9.x, the following syntax should do it (other versions of Moodle and other database engines may need a different syntax): 
```text
ALTER TABLE table mdl_user MODIFY mailformat tinyint(1) unsigned default 0;
```
 Before executing the sentence make sure you do a backup of your database, just in case something goes wrong (it shouldn't, but you know Murphy never sleeps ) Saludos,
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sync users from ldap problem
ResponsesInList.Text:
The first part (the notice about mdl_extuser no existing) is harmless and expected if you have php error reporting set to log notices (instead of just errors). The second part (the Sizelimit exceeded) warning is telling you that your LDAP server only sent back part of the objects you requested (and thus you'll only deal with a subset of the users). This is a limit set on the LDAP server side and PHP can't currently work with paged results, so you need to modify your LDAP server settings to increase the size limit. You'll need to consult your LDAP serve documentation to see how to increase this (if it's Active Directory, have a look at this: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=72003#p322195 ) Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM over SSL - Okay on Firefox, Not Okay on IE
ResponsesInList.Text: I finally got this right. The main problems were: - I didn´t put the "https" prefix when I add my moodle server to the intranet security zone. The prefix is required to make SSO over secure channels work (just for IE6. On IE7 and IE8 SSO worked fine whitout any prefix). Thanks Iñaki! - The second problem was the SSL protocol adjustments in the http-ssl.conf. You must comment out the line "BrowserMatch ".*MSIE.*" nokeepalive ssl-unclean-shutdown downgrade-1.0 force-response-1.0" , otherwise it won´t work. The last problem is a very specific one. Here in my company all employees have a A3 token with a digital certificate, which we use to login on Windows. I had configured Apache to optionally ask for the user´s certificate when establishing an https connection. When I accessed my moodle server in https, IE asked for my PIN and established the https connection using my digital certificate. For that reason IE, instead of sending my windows credentials for the SSO (Domain\User), send my digital certificate as my credentials! Apache understood that as a "bad credentials" error and denied the SSO login. After configuring Apache to NOT ask for my digital certificate, everything worked all right. I even got my hands on a signed certificate for sake of testing, but I found out that the NTLM over Https works fine with my self-signed certificate. I think it would be nice to include the first two comments in the moodle documentation for NTLM. It would save a lot of hours for a lot of people! Juliano

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: auth_ldap_sync_users.php Ubuntu Cron
ResponsesInList.Text:
Here's how I've run it in the past (everything in a single line, may appear wrapped here): 
```text
 



[ -f /path/to/moodle/auth/ldap/auth_ldap_sync_users.php ] && /usr/bin/php5 -c /etc/php5/apache2/php.ini -d memory_limit=256M -d log_errors=1 -d error_reporting=E_ALL -d display_errors=0 -d html_errors=0 -f /path/to/moodle/auth/ldap/auth_ldap_sync_users.php
```
 to let the script use up to 256 MB of RAM, use the same PHP settings that the web server uses (to make sure you have all the relevant PHP modules) and send all the error logging to your web server logs (though you might want to change this to display the errors on screen if running this from a cronjob, to get both the regular output of the execution and the error messages in your cronjob mail). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP group only
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I got a work around. I created an AD LDS instance on another server and used a combination of batch files to export user accounts from certain group in AD and automatically create proxy accounts in LDS. This way I can flatten the OU structure for use with moodle while still leaving my AD structure and groups as they are. Moodle authenticats against LDS but users still use the AD account creds for authentication.  The LDS account doesn't have a password, it's proxied to AD; one password. If you use the UserProxyFull class you can still map mail, country, etc; if you use UserProxy class you only get to use userSID and name etc. Hope this helps someone get started in some kind of direction. Feel free to message me if you have questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: configuring authentication, and enrolling new users, in a new installation
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok... you can upload them and they will be created as 'manual' (internal) users. You would then need to run a simple sql update on the mdl_user table to change the contents of the 'auth' field from 'manual' to 'ldap' (being careful not to change the ones that should be 'manual' - e.g. admin). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Sync not working with more than one context
ResponsesInList.Text: Iñaki, Well, I think I tracked down the user. We have a single user that is duplicated over all contexts. So all of the users in the first context always make it into the table. Then on the second context it works up until it gets to the duplicate. All users after the duplicate don't make it into the temp table. Is this a bug that can be fixed, so just the duplicates get removed and it keeps adding the rest of the users to the temp table? How does this work? Are the users being added to the temp table and then it is (because of a bug) checking for duplicates and deleting all of the entries after it? Or is it check for duplicates as it inserts the users into the temp table and stopping as soon as it sees a duplicate? I'm assuming the latter is what is happening. A fix without having to delete the user would be greatly appreciated. Thanks much, Garrett

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP Sync not working with more than one context
ResponsesInList.Text:
Moodle doesn't check for duplicates, but the database does. Moodle assumes that there are no duplicates (it shouldn't, otherwise you may have other problems) and tries to insert the users in the temp table. But the database refuses to insert duplicate values, so it ends up refusing all the users that are inserted in the same 'batch' of a duplicate user (up to 1000 for MySQL , up to 1 for other databases). If you are using MySQL, you can avoid this side-effect by modifying auth/ldap/auth_ldap_sync_users.php and changing the line that reads: `$ldapauth->sync_users(1000, true);` to: `$ldapauth->sync_users(1, true);` This way Moodle will try to insert one user at a time, and if that user fails (because it's duplicated) it'll be skiped but the rest of the users will get it. This is the way Moodle 2.0 will work, by the way. But as I told you above, having duplicate users in your LDAP contexts is not a good idea at all Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap: invalid login
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Neil, sorry to say, I don't know if there is an easy answer for you.  If there is, I don't see it.  I would start resolving the issue this way (because it sounds like a really annoying issue): The first thing that I would do is narrow the scope of searching for the problem.  I will assume that the Moodle code is working correctly, so I would look elsewhere.  Is it an LDAP connection issue?  A Moodle configuration issue?  I would start with the LDAP connection. Do you have the same "distinguished name" on both Active Directory servers?  If not, perhaps that is the issue.  I don't know how that would work having the same user on two different AD servers-- especially if the servers are related somehow. Have you already installed an LDAP browser on the server where Moodle is running to test your connections to the AD server? (It's easy , and works remarkably well)  You can either use LDP.exe (instructions here to install and use http://docs.moodle.org/en/Active_Directory ) or you can download the free version of Softerra and use it. Then, use these LDAP browsers with your "distinguished name" user to connect to your LDAP servers and browse to one of your user directories.  If you notice any errors, then you will have to figure out how to resolve them and see if that prompts you to modify your Moodle config. If everything here looks good, then move on to the Moodle config. I am not experienced with connecting to two separate Active Directory servers, so I don't know if your Host URL setting is correct.  However, in a recent post to the forums, it was suggested that you cannot: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=122249 . In any case, set up a test version of Moodle so that you can try out different settings without impacting your production version.  Start out with configuring your user authentication the same way that you have it in production and double check that it behaves in the same way as in production when logging in.  I would remove the ldap at the beginning of your IP addresses.  Perhaps someone else would be kind enough to give you a hint (maybe John from an earlier post) about other changes you could try... Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: CAS redesign
ResponsesInList.Text: We are proposing to our administration a redesign of the CAS authentication module for the reasons as follow: To support the new single-sign-out feature of the latest CAS versions. To allow for more failure on the ldap side and allow for tiered failover in case the ldap load balancers are problematic. To not do ldap lookups if the user exists and ldap updating is not set to every login, emailing the admin when failures occur. To allow for tiered failover in case the CAS load balancers are problematic, emailing admins when failures occur. The biggest changes would be the updating of phpcas to the latest version, supporting single-sign-out, and more forgiveness in case of networking failures. I will update this forum on July 14 with our administration's decision on the redesign/rewrite.

ResponsesInList.Text: Can someone confirm that my understanding of this is correct please? In my LDAP tree (eDirectory) i have a user object e.g. cn=mhazell,ou=student,o=org. I also have an alias that is linked to that user object the DN of this being cn=12345,ou=Student,o=Org. The reason for this is that my student reference number is 12345. I have one Moodle account named mhazell. If I turn on alias dereferencing in the LDAP setup can I log into my Moodle account using either mhazell or 12345? My understanding is that by logging in as 12345 with dereferencing turned on will return mhazell as my user name. Can anyone confirm/deny this please? Thanks, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple LDAP Accounts, one Moodle account
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'm afraid that won't work. Even if your LDAP server aliases both names to the same actual account, they are two different accounts in Moodle. Moodle references the user by its internal user name (which must be unique on the same Moodle site; Moodle networking plays some additional tricks to deal with this) and then maps that user name to an external account (usually by the same name) if using external authentication methods (ldap, cas, db, etc.). But if you type a different username in the login box, you are using a different Moodle user (which is enroled into different courses, has different grades, forum post, etc.) even if it has identical properties (first name, last name, email, etc.) Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Disable Authentication and Account Creation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there. Building a PUBLIC tutorial site, and would like to 1) prevent all visitors from registering, 2) allow all visitors to view course content, and 3) completely disable the creation of accounts by visitors. Have been reading all day, and trying a variety of settings. Time to ask you experienced folks what to do. What should I do?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disable Authentication and Account Creation
ResponsesInList.Text:
Go to Administration >> Users >> Manage authentication and disable all the authentication plugins except 'Manual accounts' and 'No login' (these two cannot be disabled). Next go to Administration >> Users >> Permissions >> User Policies and enable 'Auto-login guests'. Finally set every course (inside each course settings) to be available to guest users, with 'Guest access' set to 'Allow guests without a key'. That should do it Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ynt: More than one LDAP Server Login Error
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a bit trickier. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MNET and Domain Migration
ResponsesInList.Text:
MNET uses the $CFG-> wwwroot value in the certificate it uses to stablish the trust relationship with the remote site. So you'll need to delete the old certificate from the other Moodle site (the one you didn't moved to a new address) and re-stablish the MNET relationship again. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MNET and Domain Migration
ResponsesInList.Text: Okay, but since there is a new wwwroot the accounts do not match up and the instructors do not have access to their classes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MNET and Domain Migration
ResponsesInList.Text:
Yup! Too true. Each new remote MNET host gets a new identifier. Have a look in the mdl_mnet_host table and get the id for the new wwwroot peer (and you the old one too). Then in the mdl_user table you'll need to change the mnethostid value for the users that had the old id to the new id. Be sure to have a full backup of your Moodle database (and that you know how to restore it) before atempting any of this, just in case something goes wrong. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removing users via LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text:
Suspended users are actually assigned the 'nologin' authentication method. The net effect is that the LDAP authentication plugin doesn't touch them at all while deleting users, as it can't know for sure they were LDAP users before (e.g, they could have been suspended by the ext DB authentication plugin). So you'd need to 'revive' them first (re-assigning them to the LDAP auth plugin) and then delete them. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removing users via LDAPet
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hummm, I've just tested with a single account that I previously edited to set 'No login' as its authentication method, and it's been deleted successfully. If you filter the accounts but just add one, does your Moodle setup delete it? (just in case there's a bug when dealing with many users at once; I'm shooting in the dark here). On the other hand, if all of your 'No login' users were LDAP users before, and you have access to your database, you can also execute the following SQL sentence: 
```text
UPDATE mdl_user SET auth='ldap' WHERE auth='nologin' AND deleted=0;
```
 This will make your suspended users 'alive' and the next time you run your LDAP sync script they will get deleted. Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to register an existing ldap-user to moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: If you're using MS AD, first look at the link in Michael's post below mine.  I found I needed to make the following mods/additions to his post: in LDAP Authentication, I set the ldap_bind_dn to the full accountname @ domain name, for example: ldapuser@school.local in LDAP Enrollment Plugin, I set the enrol_ldap_bind_dn to the full accountname @ domain name, for example: ldapuser@school.local in LDAP Enrollment Plugin, I set the enrol_ldap_autocreate to Yes Note:  make sure you pay attention to the OU's you create and the values you enter in the LDAP Enrollment Plugin, as they MUST match, and Michael's don't in his instructions you MUST edit the database per Michael's instructions.  If you don't, and your user's dn is more than 64-characters, it won't work.  (I set idnumber to be 255 characters in my database). After modifying the idnumber field in the mdl_user table, there are 3 files you must also modify (see http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=50627#231911 ): /lib/moodlelib.php, around line 2486, in the "truncate_user_info" function, change idnumber(64) to idnumber(255) (or however many characters you changed idnumber to in your mdl_user table) /auth/ldap/lib.php, in 2 places around lines 404 and 407, in the "auth_sync_users" function, again change idnumber(64) to idnumber(255) /lib/db/migrate2utf8. xml , in 4 places.  2 changes around line 424, change idnumber(100) to idnumber(255) and length "100" to length "255". 2 changes at the bottom of the file, change idnumber(64) to idnumber(255) and length "64" to length "255"

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to enroll students as guests in a course ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Lea, I have had a similar problem and came up with a solution that worked well for me. I am going to assume that you are using a current version of Moodle (1.9.4 or 1.9.5). If not, the advice may not be exactly correct. You will definately need to be using a version of Moodle that allows you to control Roles (version 1.7 or newer). I think that you will need adminstrator access to the Moodle installation in order to solve this problem. So if you don't have admin access you will need to contact the admin to help you. For your course you want to have four type of people: 1) the teacher (you?) 2) students (who have normal student permissions) 3) observers (who can view but not contribute) 4) other people (who cannot enter the course) The difficulty is with #3. First of all, I wouldn't call them guests - the role of "guest" is connected to a setting in course settings -->availability "guest access" The options for the Guest Access setting are: "do not allow guests in," "allow guests without a key," and "allow guests who have the key". Note that none of the options listed do what you want. I would recommend that you create a new role titled something like "observer." To make the "Observer" role go to Site Administration --> Users --> Permissions --> Define Roles . Open the "Guest" role and then click the "duplicate role" button. Find the newly created role (probably automatically named something like "Guest_1") and open it for editing. Change the name to something like "Observer" and change the permissions so that anyone who has the observer role will be able to do what you want them to be able to do in the class. Now that you have created the role, just assign the appropriate people who have accounts at your site to the observer role for the class. Once they login to the site they should be able to observe the class. So the two options for keeping the general public out of a class but allowing select people to observe are: 1) allow guests who have a predefined key be able to enter the class Advantage: guests don't need to have an account Disadvantage: the instructor has to distribute the key, the guest needs to remember it, and if the key needs to be changed it has to be changed for everyone. 2) create a role that mimics the guest role and then assign it to people who already have accounts. Advantage: The observer can login with THEIR password, a log can be kept of the observers activities Disadvantage: the observer must create an account on the site and then be enrolled as an observer by the teacher. I hope that it is clear that if you want to keep the general public out of a class you MUST require either a login or a passkey for those who will be entering the class. There isn't a (low tech) way for the software to "know" who should be let into the classroom unless they provide some sort of password/passkey.

Desired User Account and Roles: The website has been setup to provide access to basically one single course. (this course is the only thing this company provides). We want to be able to create a groups of users that are only associated with themselves. Each group would basically consist of 1 Teacher Role and a group of student roles. All groups make use of the single course we have created on the site. The teacher for each group is able to see only there students grades and only see other members of there group period. This would allow for multiple Teachers in multiple locations to individually handle the pace in which his/her students move through the lessons. Authentication: This part may be a bit more complicated. We want to issue access to the site in a "per seat" structure. Each teacher would be allotted a set number of users. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Special Login Settings and Accounts Configuration
ResponsesInList.Text: The groups part is possible. Put the course into separate groups mode, and edit the teacher role (actually, your probably want your 'Teachers' to be Moodle 'Non-editing teachers') to remove the 'access all groups' capability. The authentication thing is hard, not just in Moodle, but on the web in general. It is the 'HTTP is a stateless protocol' problem. All the web- server sees is a sequence of requests from one user, starting with a login request. If you are lucky, it ends with a logout request, but don't count on it, because most people just close their web browser. Then there session stays active on the web server for some hours, because the web server cannot tell the difference between a student who has actually gone away, and one who is just spending half an our reading one page, but who is going to click on another link eventually. So from a technical perspective, the easiest solution is to find a different licensing model, but if you must do it this way, you will have to refine what you mean by 'a certain number of users logged in at one time'.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Special Login Settings and Accounts Configuration

ResponsesInList.Text: Having the server in the DMZ means you'll need to configure your firewall to let the Moodle server 'talk' to your domain controller servers in the internal network, which might need to open a bunch ports. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM doesn't work when the Moodle server is in the DMZ
ResponsesInList.Text: LDAP authentication just needs port 389(TCP) and optionally port 636(TCP) if you want LDAP+SSL. But NTLM SSO needs the whole 'SMB/Kerberos dance' with several ports, possibly including 88, 137, 138, 139 (some of them TCP & UDP) and probably others. Have a look at your firewall logs to see what traffic is being blocked from your Moodle server to your internal domain controllers. That should give you a clue. By the way, I wouldn't do this myself unless you really know what you are doing. It opens up a big vector for all kind of attacks when (not if) your Moodle server gets compromised. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storing password in session
ResponsesInList.Text: Storing un-hashed passwords anywhere is a very bad idea. You really should rethink your strategy for implementing this. There must be a way using a proper single-sign-on method, or some sort of authentication token.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storing password in session
ResponsesInList.Text: Take a look at the "Ldap Capture" plugin. It will store an encrypted version of you password that can be decrypted with a key.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storing password in session
ResponsesInList.Text: The squirrelmail single-sign-on patches do this very well. They follow squirrelmail's approach of using a one-time-pad to encrypt the password. The problem with simple hash or encrypted password in the session or user cookie -- which Tim and Tyler suggest -- is that the attacker no longer needs to steal the password. They steal the cookie or encrypted version of the password and use that -- in other words you're wide open to a replay attack.

ResponsesInList.Title: PAM Authentication Still Available?
ResponsesInList.Text: So I've been digging through the Moodle forums for information regarding PAM authentication and seem to have hit a bit of a wall now... I am attempting Moodle Kerberos authentication using PAM. php4-pam-auth, which is what the Moodle docs still recommend, seems to be long dead and gone. I have the PAM PECL module installed and working in PHP (since that seems to be the more canonical way of doing PAM auth in PHP now). The server is running one of the latest stable builds of Moodle 1.9. All Kerberos settings on the machine are correct and I can successfully log in to that machine locally and using SSH. Moodle has the PAM authentication option enabled and I've also created a /etc/pam.d/php file that calls pam_krb5 for authentication. That file currently looks like this (debug is just for testing purposes, and I've tried the file with and without the pam_deny line with the same results): auth sufficient pam_krb5.so use_first_pass debug auth required pam_deny.so I can submit a username and password from the Moodle login page and watch PAM debug logs as the information is passed from PHP to PAM and from PAM to Kerberos. In fact, sending a correct username and password from the Moodle login page even results in successful Kerberos authentication in the PAM logs! Awesome, right?! Not so much... Moodle still returns an "Invalid login" error, even when Kerberos successfully authenticates with the provided credentials (showing "httpd: pam_krb5[4924]: pam_authenticate returning 0 (Success)" in PAM's debug log).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PAM Authentication Still Available?
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to check - does it work for you with pam_unix? ISTR having been involved in the early days of auth/pam, and I'm sure I've tested it / used it at some point. Don't think Kerberos was ever used or tested - it's one of the trickiest pam modules to interop with in general.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PAM Authentication Still Available?
ResponsesInList.Text: Aha! Got it! I was just missing a line. I was looking through the documentation for the PECL PAM module at http://cvs.php.net/viewvc.cgi/pecl/pam/README?view=co and found the following in the FAQ section: "* Logs indicate pam authenticated the user, but the function doesn't return true, what gives? Make sure your pam configuration has an entry for both auth and account, if you do not have both, it will not work." So I just updated my /etc/pam.d/php file to look like the following: auth sufficient pam_krb5.so use_first_pass auth required pam_deny.so account [default=bad success=ok user_unknown=ignore] pam_krb5.so Afterwards, Moodle Kerberos authentication via PAM works! :D The only thing I decided to change is I turned off the "Email change confirmation" checkbox under Security -> Site policies in Moodle. Otherwise the user is forced to confirm their email address the first time they log in with Kerberos credentials. Hmmm, I may just do a write-up on all this in case others want to integrate Kerberos with Moodle...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mambo Moodle integration
ResponsesInList.Text: Go into the MAMBO modules editor, and turn off all left- and right-block modules for "main menu | moodle". MOODLE will now display in Mambo without any Mambo sideblocks - just the Mambo header. I've modified the MOODLE theme to have a thin/nondescript header, deferring to Mambo to provide the page header. I left the Mambo top menu, which has a link back to Mambo Homepage; or you can create this link in the MOODLE mainmenu. Be sure to go into MOODLE configuration/variables, and in the interface section, set "framename:" to "_self" to keep MOODLE from breaking out of its wrapper. I've got integration working fine with MOODLE 1.5.2+, only needing to comment out the line mentioned above. A single log-in in Mambo logs the user into both platforms seamlessly. Be sure to set "auth_dbpasstype:" to "plain text" in the MOODLE authentication settings, despite the apparent encouragement in the text on that page to set this to MD5. - will

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP authentication creating new user rather than using existing account
ResponsesInList.Text: I am creating a new user account for an Administrator of an external SIS system, using some very simple code (see below). This code does create the account. I find, however, that upon the user's login a new account is created for the user, even though the account I created through the script matches the LDAP infiormation as regards username, email, city, country, confirmed, and auth fields. Why doesn't the user's login find the existing account and simply use it? What I am thinking is that this has something to do with the passwords not being cached on the Moodle side, but I certainly hope not since that is a requirement of our use of LDAP authentication. Although my own testing seems to argue against this, could the problem pertain to the fact that the account's CN in the LDAP (ADAM) server is mixed case (e.g. "Administrator") whereas the username created by Moodle is lowercase? Note that this effort is for the LDAP-based Administrator account we want to create in advance of interactive logins and batch uploads, so this external Administrator can run some scripts which are restricted to users with special capabilities. (In fact we want this Administrator to run the batch uploads themselves, through a web interface that will check the user's login and capabilities.) For various reasons it is not desirable to ask these Administrators to log in just to create their accounts, then have the Moodle (local/manual) admin give them administrative privileges, and then tell them to do their privileged operations. We want to pre-create their accounts and assign them doanything capabilities through a program run in advance, so that they can simply run their scripts as needed without any intervention by the Moodle admin. (I hope I am explaining this adequately.) Perhaps someone can spot the problem in the following. For creating the new account I simply use $ sql _insert="INSERT INTO mdl_user (username,firstname,lastname,email,auth,city,country,confirmed,idnumber) VALUES ('Administrator','Administrator','Administrator','administrator@XXXX.XXX','ldap','Unavailable','XX',1,'')"; The values all match what is in LDAP according to the mapping of MySQL fields to ADAM attributes. What could be missing? Thanks. Alan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP authentication creating new user rather than using existing account
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle usernames are always lower case (this is enforces in several places in the code). So even if the user types 'Administrator' in the login box, Moodle looks for a user called 'administrator' in the user table. So change the SQL sentence to use a lower case username and it should work as expected Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: EDITED: Re: LDAP authentication creating new user rather than using existing account
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Inaki. I had tested that earlier, although I think I mislead you by including the SQL with the uppercase. Anyway, I went back and did an XML dump of the two administrator records from MySQL (the one created by my script and the other created by the interactive login)... and I suddenly noticed that the mnethostid field was 1 in the latter record but 0 in the former. When I added that to the SQL INSERT the problem went away. I repeated the test a few times, varying some other fields, but my INSERT failing to set the mnethostid seems to consistently cause the problem, and setting it to 1 seems to consistently prevent it! So I think the solution, apart from your suggestion to lower case the username, is to include setting mnethostid to 1.

ResponsesInList.Title: Tomcat and CAS
ResponsesInList.Text: Can anyone possibly help me. I've have spent the last few days tearing out my hair trying to get Apache Tomcat to work on https so that I can ultimately set up CAS to act as auth server for moodle, joomla, mahara and various other web apps we use within the school. Has anyone ever set up https on tomcat? and if so, how on earth did you do it? -Phill (slightly more bald than he was a week ago)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tomcat and CAS
ResponsesInList.Text:
Assuming you have cas set up and working over http, here goes nothing: In order to configure Apache Tomcat to allow requests via HTTPS, the Apache Tomcat Native Connector must be installed, which uses the APR protocol for handling requests. It is recommended that the 1.1.14 version ( http://archive.apache.org/dist/tomcat/tomcat-connectors/native/tomcat-native-1.1.14-src.tar.gz ) or newer be installed due to a bug within the 1.1.13 and older that improperly handled empty HTTP requests. In configuring the Tomcat connector as seen in the "Configuring APR for HTTPS" article, the APR connector requires the SSL key and certificate for the machine along with your CA certificate. If using Windows The Tomcat documentation on APR ( http://tomcat.apache.org/tomcat-6.0-doc/apr.html ) has a link where tcnative-1.dll ( http://tomcat.heanet.ie/native/ ) can be downloaded. This dll contains APR, OpenSSL and the pre-complied JNI wrapper all in one file. tcnative-1.dll just needs to be placed in a directory where Tomcat can find it. The quick and dirty solution is to put it in tomcat's bin/ directory. A more long term solution would be to put it on the Windowsd PATH. If using Linux For Linux, we have to install the APR library and the APR development package (it is assumed that OpenSSL is already installed). These steps are for Red Hat Enterprise Linux: 
```text
# Install the APR package (which may already be installed), then the APR development package
yum install apr.i386
yum install apr-devel.i386

# unzip Tomcat's JNI wrapper for APR
cd /usr/local/tomcat/bin/
tar xzf tomcat-native.tar.gz
cd tomcat-native-1.1.10-src/jni/native/

# compile and install Tomcat's JNI wrapper for APR
./configure --with-apr=/usr/bin/ && make && make install

# find the Tomcat startup script
cd /usr/local/tomcat/bin

# add the below line to the script that you use to startup Tomcat (example: startup-cas.sh
# NOTE: this line must be added before the JVM is started (perhaps add it to the top of the file?)
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/usr/local/apr/lib
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Number of LDAP connections
ResponsesInList.Text: We are running Apache on a Windows Server 2003, and ADAM on a different Windows 2003 server. Why are so many LDAP connections made, to begin with? Shouldn't the code in auth/ldap/auth.php reuse the same connection to do its queries? Should the number of connections depend on whether we call sync_users() with a parameter of 1000 or 1? Should it depend on the LDAP/ADAM setting for MAXPAGESIZE ? Is the memory_limit on PHP or some Apache setting relevant? All your suggestions will be most appreciated! Thanks, Alan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Number of LDAP connections
ResponsesInList.Text: Shouldn't the code in auth/ldap/auth.php reuse the same connection to do its queries? It should, but it currently doesn't Should the number of connections depend on whether we call sync_users() with a parameter of 1000 or 1? No it shouldn't, and it doesn't. It (currently) depends on the total number of users we add/update (as there is a new connection being opened to query the user details, and the closed). And the amount we specify in the call to sync_users just controls how many usernames we retrive from the LDAP server each time, to build the user list, before we process them. Should it depend on the LDAP/ADAM setting for MAXPAGESIZE ? No it shouldn't, and it doesn't. This setting is only relevant to the amount of users we can retrive from the LDAP server in one query. As long as PHP doesn't support the LDAP extension for Paged Results (and it still doesn't), you have to set this to a value greater to the total number of users you want to process with sync_users(). Is the memory_limit on PHP or some Apache setting relevant? As far as I know, only the memory limit is relevant, as Moodle constructs some temporary arrays in memory whose size is directly proportional to the number of users to process. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Number of LDAP connections
ResponsesInList.Text: There is at least a connection for each login, and if you have any field mapping, and additional connection to get/update the user account from LDAP. By the way, the connections don't remain open, they remain in the TCP TIME WAIT state (i.e., they are closed but waiting before they can be reused for other connections). If you have many logins, then you'll have many connections. I don't know if you can tune your operating system to lower the TCP time_wait timeout so closed connections can be reused faster. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: Alan You may want to take a look at this thread http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=114685 Iñaki has created a couple of patches that reuse the same LDAP connection for all lookups and updates when syncing users.  This has significantly increased the performance of the sync script. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using moodle authentication credentials to allow access to another site
ResponsesInList.Text: I believe that you could use the Resource modules "parameters" to pass the "User - id" and "Miscellaneous - Encrypted Code" so that you can then look up the IP for the moodle user in the users table in your other application and md5 it with the secret resource key to verify that the user is authorized. The limitation is that there is nothing stopping a malicious user from the same IP from changing the userid parameter passed to your resource and impersonate them. Therefore your resource cannot assume that it is actually the user id that was passed to it but that it is at least someone from the IP that was authorized so I wouldn't recommend this to authenticate people for access to private data but rather to keep out people passing by. See http://yourmoodlesite/admin/settings.php?section=modsettingresource for more information on the secret phrase for resources and how to do the MD5.

ResponsesInList.Title: User and group management in Moodle.
ResponsesInList.Text: I am trying to decide of the best CMS for a mid size (more than 1000 students) K-12 school in Mexico. My last two candidates are Moodle and BlackBoard. Can we manage classes as groups? If we decide to use groups, can we assign global groups so that all teachers can use these global groups to enroll users to class? If we move a student from one class (group) to another, will he be automatically be enrolled to the new group courses? 3. Can we assign a student to more than one global group?. 4. Is there a notion of parent? Can we link parent account to student account?. 5. Can we set reading access to parents automatically as a subset of student rights (I think I already got an answer to this that it is not possible in Moodle. BleacBoard sale person claims they can do it, but I didn’t see a proof yet in an administration manual or a demo) ? s 6. Can we send an email to all the parents of a global student group (again, BlackBoard claims to be able to do it, still waiting to see it myself.) ?. 7. Can we nest global groups (If a group represents a class can I create a wider group of a grade level containing all classes from that level?). 8. Does a student have a customized portal? Can he view only courses that he is assigned to? (So if a teacher enrolee the student group to a new course, this will be automatically reflected in his portal) 9. Does a student have calendar where he can see his curriculum? For example, if a student goes to her/his calendar and click tomorrows date, can he see all the courses that he is assigned to and then enter one by one to see what homework she/he has? I appreciate any help I can get including references to administrator manuals.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User and group management in Moodle.
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan - I am glad to hear that you are considering Moodle. If you have money and want to pay a Moodle Partner to host your site and help with importing your data, I think you would get more bang for your buck with Moodle (but then again I am biased and have never used Blackboard as a teacher). As a teacher and perhaps as someone who enjoys working with PHP and facing head on any challenges I appreciate the freedom and flexibility that open source offers. 1) Yes, I take information from our Student Information System (SIS) and import it into Moodle. You can also import users via CSV (which you could get from an Excel file). I've not played with mass enrolling students via the Moodle GUI as I have preferred to handle it via sql queries directly in the database (certainly something a Moodle partner could handle). 2 and 3) I'm not sure where things are with global groups - this was attempted in Moodle 1.8 but was taken out and I think it is to be attempted again in Moodle 2.0 (according to the Roadmap). I'm not sure how that code has come along. I would think that you could get some of the behavior you are looking for by creating groups on the frontpage (they could behave somewhat like a global group - but it depends on the specifics of what you are looking for). 4) With Moodle 1.8 there has been significant progress in creating a Parent role that can associated with a student. The Mentees block allows the parent to see a list of their children and facilitates them gaining access to the child's information. There is great flexibility in the roles that you create and the capabilities that you can assign those roles and the context in which you want those capabilities to be allowed or denied. 5) "as a subset of student rights" ... I'm not sure what that means. The parent is a user with their own set of rights. You can give the parent access to view courses without having the ability to write content. You may want to check out http://docs.moodle.org/en/Parent_role for more information. 6) You could certainly group your parents into "groups" or even a specially designated course (for example, Freshman Parents) and send them a mass message (which the parent could either view when they login to Moodle or have forwarded to their email account). The concept of grouping groups together in called groupings. Again, groupings was to be implemented in Moodle 1.8 but I believe that it is now on the roadmap for 1.9 but I have not looked at the code to see where it stands. 8) Yes, the courses block shows the user (teacher, student, parent, etc.) those courses in which they are enrolled in. 9) Yes, Moodle has a calendar and the user (teacher, student, parent, etc.) sees the events on the calendar. Check out http://docs.moodle.org/en/Calendar for more information on the various capabilities. The user can create his/her own events (user events), they can see course events with automatic hyperlinks to the course activity (assignment, forum, quiz, etc.), group events, and site events (like school being closed for a holiday). In short check out http://docs.moodle.org for more information and feel free to write back with any questions. I find the Moodle community to be a very friendly and helpful. After all, it is a group of educators trying to help each other to be better educators. I've taken the approach to rely on the generosity of this community to educate me about Moodle and to help me to resolve issues; however, with limited technical resources a Moodle partner may be a nice backup to have (especially if you have the money). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User and group management in Moodle.
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan - It sounds like you want what I call a "turn key solution". In other words, the users come in, they are given a username and password, login and are ready to start working. That is pretty much what I have provided my school. Teachers and students do not have to bother with course enrollments. I take that information from our SIS and from their perspective it magically shows up in Moodle. This is certainly possible but it does take a little planning and someone has to do that work. If you do not have someone able to do that, then I would suggest paying a Moodle Partner to do the work for you. I just wanted to assure you that it can in fact be done because I have done it. If you are familiar with SQL, I would be happy to send you my notes about how I setup our site which creates the course categories and courses, creates the user accounts, assigns teachers and students to the courses, creates Teacher Repositories (a course where teachers of the same subject can collaborate together and share resources with one another), creates metacourses when the teacher has more than one section of a course, creates groups for each section and assigns the students to them. I've not done parent accounts on a production server ; however, I have created them on a test server. The biggest thing there is deciding exactly what you want the parents to be able to see and do. I have another SQL script that we run periodically to handle add/drops (i.e. changing courses). Changing the students and parents enrollements can be automated with this process so that teachers do not have to worry about it all and in fact I do not allow students to unenroll themselves from a course; however, they can enroll in one if they have the enrollment key (which I find helpful for clubs that have a Moodle presence). I'm not sure I understand your distinction about school oriented vs. teacher/student oriented. A school is made up of teachers, students, parents, administrators, etc. In Moodle-ese, the phrase typically used is that of a learning community. We are all learners from one another. In summary, I think Moodle can certainly accomplish what you are looking for. I would recommend contacting a Moodle Partner so that you can discuss the specifics of your situation and get an idea of cost (if any, depending on how you choose to implement a solution). Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict access at activity/resource level?
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume that by "restrict" you mean that the user should be able to see the activity icon, but when they click on it they are told that they may not access the activity. Not all activities have a capability that can be used to restrict access. Quiz has "View quiz information," Assignment has "View assignment", Database has "View entries," Forum has "View discussions," etc.. Since these are set to Allow in the default Guest role, you can restrict Guests from viewing these activities by overriding Guest in the course context , setting these capabilities to Prevent. Unfortunately, Choice, SCORM, Lesson , Glossary, Survey, Wiki, and Workshop do not have such capabilities and neither do any of the resource types. You can't restrict Guests from entering these activities using a pure Roles and Capabilities approach, although you may be able to restrict what they can do once inside the activity. For example, if you set all of the Choice-related capabilities to Prevent, Guests will still be able to enter the Choice and see the question.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using auth_ldap_sync_users  to update users profiles
ResponsesInList.Text: I would ask your admin guy to create another AD instance just for your moodle project and change the MaxPageSize value to 1000 This MaxPageSize value controls the maximum number of objects that are returned in a single search result, independent of how large each returned object is. To perform a search where the result might exceed this number of objects, the client must specify the paged search control. This is to group the returned results in groups that are no larger than the MaxPageSize value. To summarize, MaxPageSize controls the number of objects that are returned in a single search result. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Verify Student Identity
ResponsesInList.Text: Brian - I have seen this functionality outside of Moodle when I was taking one of those driver education courses to avoid points after getting a speeding ticket. Moodle trusts that the person authenticating to the system is in fact who they say they are. Since Moodle is predominantly used in schools, most places have a usage policy that discourages or prohibits giving out one's password to someone else. I thought I recalled a similar request not too long ago - it would make an interesting feature request. If you could, check and see if you can find it in the Moodle Tracker and if a request does not already exist feel free to create one. Part of the challenge would be where to get the data? Obviously you would want it from the user profile and for it to be fields that are hidden but it assumes an ability to authenticate that. On the driver's license one it asked questions about the vehicle, license tag, etc. So it would not be impossible to design something like this but it does not currently exist. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO with AD2003
ResponsesInList.Text:
It has taken me longer than expected, but here it goes. Attached to this message there is a patch file. You'll need the patch tool (you can get patch for Windows from http://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/patch.htm , download the binary 'Complete package, except sources' package). Once you have patch installed in you system, place the attached patch file in .../moodle/auth/ldap/auth.php, open a console window, go to .../moodle/auth/ldap/ and execute the following command: 
```text
patch -p3 --binary < ntlm-debugging.diff
```
 it should apply without problems. If you see some "HUNK # succeded at nnnn (offset mmm lines)" messages don't worry about them. Next, login as admin, go to Administration >> Server >> Debugging and set your debug level to 'ALL: Show all reasonable PHP debug messages'. The patch will send all the debug messages to the PHP error logs (so make sure you know where they are going to ). Next try to login using NTLM SSO and have a look at your PHP error logs. You should see something similar to this (the exact messages can vary): 
```text
[19-Apr-2008 12:32:38] ntlmsso_finish(): username: administrator, key: 8pVumbsCwp $cf[$key]: administrator
[19-Apr-2008 12:32:38] user_login(): username: administrator
[19-Apr-2008 12:32:38] ntlmsso_finish(): user successfully authenticated. Redirecting to: 
http://192.168.27.2/moodle/



[19-Apr-2008 12:19:30] ntlmsso_finish(): username: administrator, key: eSYcePFE3s $cf[$key]: administrator
[19-Apr-2008 12:19:30] user_login(): username: administrator
[19-Apr-2008 12:19:30] user_login(): can't find the distinguished name for the user
[19-Apr-2008 12:19:30] ntlmsso_finish(): authenticate_user_login failed
```
 The first block of messages corresponds to a successful NTLM SSO login, while the second corresponds to a failed one. In this particular case, we can't find the distinguished name of the user, so it probably means some configuration error in Moodle LDAP settings. The messages for the failed logins will help me diagnose what's making the SSO login fail, so please, post them here. Don't worry about the $key value, it has nothing to do with the user password, but you can modify both the username and the key value before posting them here if you feel like it. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: I too have been wrestling with this NTLM/SSO issue and though I can't explain why, it seems to me that the loginpage_hook function in auth/ldap/auth.php causes it. Anyway, I have a replacement which works for me - interesting to find out if it works for you too. function loginpage_hook() { global $CFG, $SESSION; if (($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'GET' // Only on initial GET of loginpage || ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST' && (get_referer() != strip_querystring(qualified_me())))) // Or when POSTed from another place // See MDL-14071 && !empty($this->config->ntlmsso_enabled) // SSO enabled && !empty($this->config->ntlmsso_subnet) // have a subnet to test for && empty($_GET['authldap_skipntlmsso']) // haven't failed it yet && (isguestuser() || !isloggedin()) // guestuser or not-logged-in users && address_in_subnet($_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'],$this->config->ntlmsso_subnet)) { // First, let's remember where we were trying to get to before we got here if (empty($SESSION->wantsurl)) { $SESSION->wantsurl = (array_key_exists('HTTP_REFERER',$_SERVER) && $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] != $CFG-> wwwroot && $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] != $CFG->wwwroot.'/' && $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] != $CFG->httpswwwroot.'/login/' && $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] != $CFG->httpswwwroot.'/login/index.php' && $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] != $CFG->wwwroot."/auth/ldap/ntlmsso_attempt.php") ? $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] : $CFG->wwwroot; } // Now start the whole NTLM machinery. redirect($CFG->wwwroot."/auth/ldap/ntlmsso_attempt.php"); } // No NTLM SSO, Use the normal login page instead. // If $SESSION->wantsurl is emtpy and we have a 'Referer:' header, the login // page insists on redirecting us to that page after user validation. If // we clicked on the redirect link at the ntlmsso_finish.php page instead // of waiting for the redirection to happen, then we have 'Referer:' header // we don't want to be used at all. As we can't get rid of it, just point // $SESSION->wantsurl to $CFG->wwwroot (after all, we came from there). if (empty($SESSION->wantsurl) && (get_referer() == $CFG->httpswwwroot.'/auth/ldap/ntlmsso_finish.php')) { $SESSION->wantsurl = $CFG->wwwroot; } } This may not be the ultimate fix but I hope it sheds some light on what's happening! This was tested on Moodle 1.9 build 20080402. Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP to clean up users accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: change the authentication type for the user

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP to clean up users accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm afraid you'll need to do the cleanup by hand, at least partially. For all the accounts you want to do the cleanup, you'll need to change their authentication to 'ldap', and the use auth_ldap_sync_users.php (from the command line) to remove the users that don't exist in the LDAP directory, add the ones missing and (optionally) update existing ones. Make sure you don't set authentication to 'ldap' for users like admin, guest and other accounts you don't want to be syncrhonized with your LDAP directory. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No Login / No Error with LDAP Auth
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Bruce, What do you have in the User Attribute field? In order to just use their AD username, put "sAMAccountName" in that field. If you want to use AD email, then put "mail" in that field. (Without the quotes). Hope that helps, Brian Edit - Rereading your question, I think you are having an issue with the bind user not accessing AD through the LDAP authentication module. In the in Distinguished Name field, you will need to put the entire tree to the bind user (i.e. CN=binduseraccount,OU=org unit,DC=domain,DC=domain). LDP.exe will give this to you by browsing to the bind user, right click and Copy DN - then paste that in the Distinguished Name field on the LDAP Auth settings page in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Basic Auth-Plugin question
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is an extract of some code of mine that sets some of the fields (such as city) that you want to set. There are many fields in the user table that store the data you wish to store, so this example can be expanded. Obviously you need to change the $_POST array elements to the correct data for you. Note country is a two letter code. You will need a specific password instead of the lower case random number I generate. The code below is sufficient to fully register a user and even set some profile data. It is even possible to add custom profile data (if setup properly). This code is extracted and modified from existing Moodle code... $user->username    = $_POST['username']; $user->password    = strtolower(random_string(6)); $user->lastname    = $_POST['lastname']; $user->firstname   = $_POST['firstname']; $user->email       = $_POST['email']; $user->city        = $_POST['city']; $user->country     = $_POST['country']; $user->lang        = 'en_utf8'; $user->confirmed   = 1; $user->deleted     = 0; $user->timemodified = time(); $user->mnethostid  = $CFG->mnet_localhost_id; $user->auth        = 'manual'; require_once($CFG-> dirroot .'/user/profile/lib.php'); $user->password = hash_internal_user_password($user->password); $ur = get_record('user', 'username', $user->username); if (!empty($ur)) { // For some reason this Moodle Username ALREADY EXISTS and CANNOT BE CREATED! die(); } if (!($user->id = insert_record('user', $user))) { // User FAILED to be Registered (BAD insert_record())! die(); } $pref->name = 'auth_forcepasswordchange'; $pref->value = 0; // 1 Would force a change on first login! $pref->userid = $user->id; insert_record('user_preferences',$pref, false); $pref->name = 'email_bounce_count'; $pref->value = 1; $pref->userid = $user->id; insert_record('user_preferences',$pref, false); $pref->name = 'email_send_count'; $pref->value = 1; $pref->userid = $user->id; insert_record('user_preferences',$pref, false); // There are currently no custom fields in Peoples Uni. Also there is no mechanism (e.g. form or db) here to set them // I am leaving this in so that defaults might be set correctly? profile_save_data($user); $user = get_record('user', 'id', $user->id); events_trigger('user_created', $user); Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Guest users - only allowed to see course they are enrolled in
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not sure what you mean by "converting the guest account to a student" account. The guest role is assigned to visitors who have not logged in with their own account. Usually someone who is just browsing a Moodle site without logging in is assigned this role and can see course titles and things on the front page , but little else, unless there are courses that explicitly allow guest in. Allowing guests into a course will put them in browsing mode, where they can see content but can not participate in any of the activities . Moodle does not allow a "guest" to participate in course activities. All this is behavior is somewhat determined by the user policy settings and the version of Moodle you're using. All that said - it sounds like you don't want guests to be allowed in courses. Your course settings seem correct for accomplishing that. It seems the problem is in enrolling these two types of users: "internal" and "partners." In both cases, all of these users will have to have their own unique account that they need to use to login to Moodle. I'm not sure how you are handling account creation, but in your case I think it would be typical to create accounts using email-based self registration or having an admin set up accounts manually. The enrollment step can either be done using an enrollment key, or a teacher can enroll students using "assign roles" in the course administration block, or an admin can do this by uploading users in bulk (this method can be used to create accounts and enroll users in courses in the same step). So the "partners" would only be enrolled in the courses they have paid for. In order to allow your "internal" users to have access to all courses, you would either have to enroll them in all courses, or you could handle these multiple enrollments using a metacourse.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Guest users - only allowed to see course they are enrolled in
ResponsesInList.Text: You might try using groups. Since guest users aren't placed in a group, they can see but not interact. You can give those guests that you do want to be interactive a key for the class that puts them into a group thus allowing them to participate fully. When you form groups for a class, you can create a key that will not only enroll the person in the class but also put them into the group. Using the course key only puts them in the course. You only need to create one group per class. \You then set the default for the course to groups. For every activity, you have to be in a group to participate. I hope this helps. Bonnie

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP requires two logins to pull email address
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I figured out a fix..... in the moodlelib.php file I found this these lines: if (!$authplugin->is_internal()) { // update user record from external DB $user = update_user_record($username, get_auth_plugin($user->auth)); } } else { // if user not found, create him $user = create_user_record($username, $password, $auth); From what I can tell these lines control what moodle does when a user logs in. The first part says if the user has external data, update it. The second part is if the user is not in the database create it. So, cheating a little bit, I copied what moodle is told to do when the user exists $user = update_user_record($username, get_auth_plugin($user->auth)); and added it to just below what moodle does after it creates the new user... so the end result seems to be when a new user logs in it checks LDAP, creates the user record in the data base then it updates it. The email address then comes over. Here is the fixed section of the moodlelib.php file: // successful authentication if ($user->id) { // User already exists in database if (empty($user->auth)) { // For some reason auth isn't set yet set_field('user', 'auth', $auth, 'username', $username); $user->auth = $auth; } update_internal_user_password($user, $password); // just in case salt or encoding were changed (magic quotes too one day) if (!$authplugin->is_internal()) { // update user record from external DB $user = update_user_record($username, get_auth_plugin($user->auth)); } } else { // if user not found, create him $user = create_user_record($username, $password, $auth); $user = update_user_record($username, get_auth_plugin($user->auth)); } $authplugin->sync_roles($user); foreach ($authsenabled as $hau) { $hauth = get_auth_plugin($hau); $hauth->user_authenticated_hook($user, $username, $password); }

In order to prevent passwords from being hashed for PAM logins, you need to edit /usr/moodle/moodle/auth/pam/auth.php Specifically, you need to add a line in the auth_plugin_pam() function. That function should end up looking like this: /** * Constructor. */ function auth_plugin_pam() { $this->authtype = 'pam'; $this->config = get_config('auth/pam');
