ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add _password_ expiration support for Active Directory
ResponsesInList.Text: What does the LDAP password expiration code do? Every time a user logs into Moodle, it checks when the password is going to expire. If the expiration time is below a given threshold expressed in days (configurable via LDAP settings screen), the user is shown a little message (no pop-ups, just a plain text message) telling him/her so, and allowing him/her to change it from Moodle at that moment. For the last thing, you need use a bind user with password reset right and establish a LDAP+SSL connection to your Active Directory LDAP server(s). Otherwise, the password change function won't work. But you always get the expiration notice. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add _password_ expiration support for Active Directory
ResponsesInList.Text: The couple of times that I have done it (on linux machines), I followed the instructions given here: http://www.php.net/manual/en/function.ldap-connect.php#36156 with a couple of minor modifications: - I placed the Root CA certificate in /etc/ssl/certs instead of /usr/local/ssl/certs (it doesn't really matters, but I wanted to keep all of them at the same place) and used the openldap configuration files places at /etc/ldap (the ones from the official Debian package). - I didn't do any of the apache .ldaprc things (the openldap version of Debian Sarge -and now Etch- pick settings from /etc/ldap/ldap.conf, so I just put the mods there). I had a hard time to make it work, as I got lots of timeouts (and PHP simply killed the scripts). To make a long story short, the reason was that openldap was checking each and every CA certificate I had in /etc/ssl/certs to verify the server certificate, which took too long (around a minute and a half or so). So I simply deleted the rest of the CA certificates from /etc/ssl and bingo! Of course, instead of deleting them, you can simply put the AD Root CA certificate in a different place and point your openldap configuration to that place (which is probably a wiser thing to do, but I just wanted to make it work as soon as possible in my test environment and never went back to fix things ) Saludos. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ERROR: Could not instantiate mail function
ResponsesInList.Text: I debugged and solved a similar problem. Some SMTP servers do not support headers (e.g. Subjects) outside the ASCII range properly. I describe a solution to this in the following post:- http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=102227#p452859 You seem to be having a similar problem (in that the problem only occurs when using a non English language). Alan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ERROR: Could not instantiate mail function
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to clarify, if you have the same SMTP server problem with UTF-8 subject headers, then just make the following change... In textlib.class.php, in encode_mimeheader, CHANGE LINE:    for ($i=0; $i <= $multilength; $i+=$magic) { TO:                   $i=0; if ($i <= $multilength) { This will truncate subject and other headers that will cause the SMTP server to fail (assuming you have the same problem). This patch should not cause any serious functionality issues, although subject lines will obviously be smaller (if they contain non English characters). Any idea of the type (brand) and version of your SMTP server? Alan.

Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> User policies -> Default role for all users should be Authenticated user, Role for visitors -> Guest and Role for guest -> Guest Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Assign system roles -> No students should be assigned to student role or any other role. We have a sizable Adult Education program of which the student's do not necessarily have a college e-mail address or require it to be in their SIS and therefore AD record. On Thursday, July 31, I was contacted by a faculty member who alerted me to the fact that some of the e-mail addresses for users were not correct (her 2 kids)... At that time, I logged in as the Admin and looked under the Users -> Authentication -> LDAP Server settings and saw the following in the Data Mappings area, Email address Update local  On creation On every login Update external  Never On update Lock value  Unlocked Unlocked if empty Locked At that point, I changed the 'Update local' setting to 'On Every Login' and ran the synchronization script... I checked the addresses for the 2 users that I knew had incorrect addresses and saw that they were correct... I thought that everything was golden.... Later that evening, I was contacted by a faculty member who had been dropped from 3 of 4 of his courses... I added him back into the 3 courses and checked to make sure that everything looked OK and it did. At the time, I didn't think that the 2 events had anything to do with each other... On Sunday, Aug. 3rd, I got an e-mail from a faculty member who had been contacted by one of his students who had been dropped from his course and when logging in had been asked to provide his e-mail address and when he entered it he looked for his posts to discussion boards and they were no longer present and his grades were missing from the Grade book. Now I am not so sure that the setting change didn't have something to do with the issue that I an experiencing with user enrollment... I looked at some of the current courses and found that there were several common elements between the affected people. There are no e-mail addresses in their AD record and in all cases where there was data in the grade book, the user had no e-mail address listed in their record in Moodle... and therefore there would be no e-mail address in AD. If a user had an address in AD, there were no issues with loss of enrollment or grade data. My question is of someone who understands this aspect of Moodle better than I do if this makes sense... Would changing the 'Update local' setting in the Email address Data Mapping area of LDAP cause students with no e-mail address in AD to become unenrolled from their courses? It seems to be caused one SMTP host (relay-hosting.secureserver.net) not fully supporting BASE64 encoding of UTF-8 subject headers. The problem occurs when the subject is long enough to cause a newline to be needed to break up the subject onto two lines. (Maybe, now that I think of it, the SMTP host is expecting CR, LF and not just LF? Although Moodle is using PHP mail() and it should do the correct conversion, if required.) I have put in a temporary patch to limit subject length to one line (only when the subject contains characters outside ASCII)... In textlib.class.php, in encode_mimeheader, CHANGE LINE:    for ($i=0; $i <= $multilength; $i+=$magic) { TO:                   $i=0; if ($i <= $multilength) { The only other header that might be truncated is the user's name part of an e-mail address if is very long and outside the ASCII range. Note that a secondary problem occurs when the Moodle SMTP parameter smtpmaxbulk is set to greater than 1, but direct SMTP is not setup (and the defaults do not work). Moodle tries to do a reset using fputs() in class.smtp.php and gets a Broken pipe error. Note that the Moodle version is 1.9.1 (Build: 20080515). Alan.

I found out that when you change the 'Password Change URL' field on Users->Authentication->Manage Authentication->External Database , it only changes the URL for the 'Change Password' button on Moodle screens where the user is already logged in. To change the 'Lost Password' URL on the front page , I simply went into the Moodle database and changed the 'forgottenpasswordurl' record in the mdl_config table to point to my correct password change URL. I'm sure there's gotta somewhere to set the 'forgottenpasswordurl' variable from the Moodle Admin interface, but I don't know where that is. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Force users to login
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is some feedback to your feedback I think the setting belongs under Front Page -> Front Page Settings rather than Security -> Site Policies The force users to login setting is applied site-wide, not only at the front page (e.g., if you try to directly enter a course from a link and the setting is enabled, you are redirected to the login page). I think the Authentication -> Manage Authentication screen should have a fancy HTML editor for the 'Instructions' field as this is what shows up when Force login is turned on I completely agree. Having Force Login turned on doesn't mean the users already know what credentials they have to use to log in, so I think the sentence makes sense even in that particular case (specially if you allow self-registration, as the instructions you need to perform the self-registration appear there). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: external as well as self-registration
ResponsesInList.Text: We would like to be able to populate moodle with users from an external database , which I see is possible. ...and we would also like a self-registration process for users not covered by this database. I see its possible to turn on a variety of user authentication but i'm interested to know how this would work for the user and if anyone here can see any issues with setting it up this way and perhaps some tips Ali

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: external as well as self-registration
ResponsesInList.Text: When the user tries to log in for the first time, they have the choice to input a username and a password, or register for a new account (if you have self-registration enabled). If they input the username & password, Moodle tries to validate those credentials against the enabled authentication backends (its own internal database, and any other enabled authentication systems). As long as the usernames are unique among all those systems, you'll have no problem at all, as Moodle keeps track of which subsystem should use for each user. If they choose to register a new account, they need to enter the usual details, a confirmation email is sent and when the account is confirmed, they become an 'internal' user, so they are never looked up in external subsystems. All in all it works quite nicely. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Javascript to strip @email.edu from logon
ResponsesInList.Text: Janet: Below is our patch. We made it because username and username@SeattleAcademy.org were being treated is two separate users, but both authenticated against our IMAP server . This was creating multiple accounts. You would not use this in the case of a site that wanted to allow domain names to be part of their usernames. In the file /login/index.php Find: $frm->username = $user->username; Below that, paste: if($atPos = strpos($frm->username,'@')) $frm->username = substr($frm->username,0,$atPos); Below that, we also add: if($atPos = strpos($frm->username,'\\')) $frm->username = substr($frm->username,$atPos+2,strlen($frm->username)); We do the last statement because users can also login as SeattleAcademy\\username, so we just use the last part. Good luck! --Gary

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM authentication in 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jonathan, Hopefully I can help. I've struggled with similar issues over the last day and a half, but have come out the victor today! The issues that faced me were two things that I think pertain to those of us who have used NTLM before. I've added them to the wiki for others to find too. 1. The authentication type held against each users record (auth field) used to be set to ntlm. As it's now merged into ldap Moodle no longer knows what that is and falls through and thinks it's CAS. You need to run a simple query to update all ntlm fields to ldap. This is how it was for me going from 1.7 anyway. 2. I created a .htaccess file for the auth/ntlm folder to allow certain rights to the oncampuslogin.php. I had to move this to the auth/ldap folder and change the file name to ntlmsso_magic.php. If you've done it using the httpd.conf it's the same, but you'll need to change the parent directory too. Hope that gets you going. Then maybe you can help with the error message about No such object on line 1510 that flashes up! Red

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM authentication in 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Red, Thanks for your help. With respect to the issue of authentication type I have queried the postgre sql database and all my user accounts are showing "ldap" in the "auth" field in the mdl_user table (that is all save the guest account and the admin account, these are showing as manual which might explain why I can't login to my admin account using ntlm. So I'm not sure whether I should change the auth type to "ldap" for the admin account ) I ditched the use of .htaccess files in favour of <directory > tags in the httpd.conf file as I read on one of the moodle forums that there was a performance hit in using .htaccess files. However I am guessing that the settings I have made are working as the login is working. The problem seems to be that in IE7 the automated login completes successfully but that moodle fails to recognise this so it persists in displaying a login failure message followed by the login box. As far as I can figure it out 1. login/index.php identifies the authentication options that are configured for the site and calls the function loginpage_hook() in auth/ldap/auth.php 2. Loginpage_hook() redirects to auth/ldap/ntlmsso_attempt.php 3. ntlmsso_attempt.php has a curious (well I'm curious about it anyway) bit of coding that loads a graphic but the source is actually ntlmsso_magic.php 4. The function ntlmsso_magic() attempts the login and if successful creates some kind of cookie (see lines 1803 to 1819 in auth/ldap/auth.php) which should be detected by ntlmsso_finish() 5. redirection then takes place to ntlmsso_finish.php 6. ntlmsso_finish.php calls the function ntlmsso_finish() on the assumption that if ntlmsso_finish() is successful (presumably successful in finding the cookie) then program flow will not return to ntlmsso_finish.php. Should program flow return to this page then a redirection takes place back to login/index.php with a flag telling index.php to skip ntlm authentication. I am guessing that the problem lies somewhere with the creation of the cookie or the failure of ntlmsso_finish() to detect the cookie. Either would explain how a successful login could still be treated as a failed login as far as the login sequence goes, leading to the display of a login failure message and default login box at the same time as displaying "You are logged in as user name (logout)". As I am not getting any errors I can't be of much help with your error message - "no such object on line 1510". Have you turned debugging on in the Site Admin Server Debugging, to see if you can get any more information? If you could identify which line it was referring to I might be better able to suggest something. Do you have an ldap test script to ensure that your ldap connection is working? If not let me know and I can post a sample script I use, it may not be perfect, but I use it to ensure that php can successfully query ldap, as until this is OK nothing else is going to work. Kind regards Johnathan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: NTLM authentication in 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a small timeout set in step 3 (ntlmsso_attempt.php) to redirect you to the standard login page if NTLM authentication fails (or is not supported by your browser). If the NTLM authentication takes a little longer than that timeout (3 seconds, hardcoded in the page), then ntlmsso_attempt.php redirects you to the standard login page, while the NTLM authentication process keeps going on!. So it may happen that you land on the login page, but have just been logged in by that time. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 1.9 upgrade - Roles setting
ResponsesInList.Text: When upgrading from 1.8.4 to 1.9+, I noticed that when creating a new user in my external DB used for authentication, as the user logged in, they would find themselves in a loop receiving an error, "You cannot edit your own profile". ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Still having email authentication problems
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All. After spending months on and off of this problem, searching the whole net for help on this and finding no real answer to it, I have finally cracked it. I did the same things that everyone probably did, reinstalled all the components to make Moodle run, upgrade and downgrade everything, did restores and created test environments, move the server in and out of the DMZ, the list just goes on and I am a little bit disappointed that so many people have had this problem but no one has posted the solution. Solution: Moodle needs to authenticate with the exchange server using a user name and password set in the site variables page in Moodle. It may sound obvious but our exchange was set to relay emails from that server and in fact this was working. Emails did get delivered. However Microsoft have embedded a security feature into Exchange that edits hyperlinks which relay anonymously as one of its anti- spam / malicious use protection of the email server. I would suggest creating a domain user account. Make sure the password is set to never expire & add a description note to the account stating “Do Not Delete / Do Not Change Password”. I hope this helps someone out there.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Active Directory Users can't log in
ResponsesInList.Text: I feel like the same information is being repeated again. Anyway... the following assumes that your ldap_host_url. this should be the fully qualified domain name of the server preceeded by 'ldap://'. i am also assuming that PHP LDAP module is correctly working [or at least loaded awaiting configuration]. After that, you will need to test your configuration. the following is the steps i would use when setting up LDAP authentication for the first time: Install the windows server support tools [contains the ldp.exe tool] run this utility. you will need to 'bind' to the domain you are wishing to connect to. once you are bound to the [AD] LDAP server, some information will be displayed in the right-hand window. you are looking for 'rootDomainNamingContext'. currently this line for me reads: '1> rootDomainNamingContext: DC=domain,DC=local;' use this information after selecting 'view' => 'tree'. you should enter the obtained info in the following way: Base DN = DC=domain,DC=local click 'ok' and this you should be shown a collapsed tree in the left-hand window. once expanded [by double-clicking], the tree should look similar to the root object you see when using 'Active Directory Users and Computers' snap-in. once this is visible, simply double-clicking an object in the left-and window will expand its children [this will work until 'no children' is displayed as the child object]. Find the details for the account you will use to 'bind' to the server use the final step in the previous section, drill down initially to where the account that you are going to use within Moodle to 'bind' to the LDAP server is. once you find where that object is within the ldp.exe tool, double click it. this will retrieve all of its information as stored in the AD LDAP server. the first few lines returned for my user object reads: Expanding base 'CN=DENNY. Kieran,OU=InfoTech,OU=Support,OU=Campus1,OU=Staff,OU=School,DC=domain,DC=local'... Result <0>: (null) Matched DNs: Getting 1 entries: >> Dn: CN=DENNY. Kieran,OU=InfoTech,OU=Support,OU=St Pauls,OU=Staff,OU=Lavalla,DC=lavalla,DC=local you will need to copy out the information following '>> DN: ' and paste it into the 'ldap_bind_dn:' section of the LDAP config page in Moodle. you will need to enter the correct password for this account. that should then do for the bind account. find the correct details for the rest of your users similar to the previous step, except you are now looking for the Organizational Unit [OU] containing your users. our AD server is broken down by staff vs. student, then by campus, then department [or in the case of students, by year level]. some of the OUs have around 300-400 students in it, and overall, the users OU has about 2500 objects in it [this does not include any groups as these are stored in a separate OU] as part of the Moodle config, i have used four distinct OU's in the ldap_contexts entry. two for each of our campus', and then broken apart into staff and students. this setup allows me to easily remove access to students by simply modifying the ldap contexts Moodle config entry. currently, on the Moodle LDAP Authentication config page, my ldap_contexts entry reads: "OU=Campus1,OU=Staff,OU=School,DC=domain,DC=local; OU=Campus2,OU=Staff,OU=School,DC=domain,DC=local; OU=Campus1,OU=Students,OU=School,DC=domain,DC=local; OU=Campus2,OU=Students,OU=School,DC=domain,DC=local;" all of this depends on your personal preference and/or AD setup. one restraining factor is that somewhere along the line, you are limited to 1000 entries per context lookup [i think this i correct, though i'm not too sure where the limitation is enforced]. some other things that can affect connecting to the AD LDAP server: SSL requirement being enforced [though i have not seen this in place] incorrect access permissions for the user binding to LDAP [ie. using a disabled user, or one who does not have lookup & password checking rights]. there are prob lost more issues that can occur, but i dont have time to work them out, let alone list them here... well, that took a good half hour to write [and i'm sure that there are a few spelling mistooks in there]. just rambling, but someone may want to add this to the Wiki/help page for LDAP configuration [specific to Active Directory]. i REALLY hope that helps somewhat... regards, Kieran

ResponsesInList.Title: Removed ext user- Which does what
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, Our LDAP server is configured not to hand out account details of expired accounts. Hence Moodle runs its auth_ldap_sync script each night, sees the users are missing, and deletes them from its internal database (using Delete Internal setting for Removed ext user). The problem we've just realised, is when a user is temporarily inactive in LDAP, they are completely removed from Moodle's user database. When they become active again, they are reimported, but given a new database record ID. This has the effect of locking users out of previous objects, such as previous quiz attempts. The solution is to change Removed ext user in the LDAP configuration page. Ideally I'd like to do this directly on our live server, but I just wanted to clarify with everyone before I did this: Delete Internal - Does exactly that, if the external account isn't in LDAP then it will be removed from Moodle. If the account reappears in LDAP, it will be added back into Moodle, but with a new account ID. Keep Internal - Does nothing to the account if it disappears from LDAP. As users authenticate against LDAP, if their account is inactive, their login will fail. Suspend Internal - Suspends the account, preventing them from logging in again until the account is un-suspended. If the account is suspended in Moodle, but active in LDAP, the user cannot log in to Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Removed ext user - Suspended but still present?
ResponsesInList.Text: Bonjour, About processing users having been deleted/deactivated/suspended from LDAP, I think we need 5 different settings, from "do nothing" to "fully delete". 1) Keep internal - does no change in Moodle - however the user cannot log in Moodle because he cannot identify against LDAP 2) Suspend internal - only one change in Moodle : tagged as "suspended" - the user can no longer log in Moodle - he still appears as course participant - he would be be revived in Moodle if he did reappear in LDAP 3) Hide internal (new setting) - the user is tagged as "hidden" in Moodle - he can no longer log in Moodle - he does no longer appear as course participant - he would be revived in Moodle if he did reappear in LDAP (with his previous enrollments) 4) Deactivate internal (new setting, like "delete internal" in Moodle 1.6) - the user is tagged as "deactivated" in Moodle - he is unenrolled from his Moodle courses - he can no longer log in Moodle - of course he does no longer appear as course participant - he would be revived in Moodle if he did reappear in LDAP (without any enrollment) 5) Delete internal - the user is tagged as "deleted" in Moodle - he is unenrolled from his Moodle courses - his email and idnumber are cleared - of course he can no longer log in Moodle - of course he does no longer appear as course participant - of course he won't be revived in Moodle if he did reappear in LDAP What do you think about these different settings? Arnaud

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ldap synch not working
ResponsesInList.Text:
Assuming your PHP installation is at c:\php, and that there is a php.exe file inside that directory, and that your php.ini file is inside that directory too, and that your Moodle installation is at c:\inetpub\moodle, you just need to setup a scheduled task that runs the command: 
```text
c:\\php\\php.exe -c c:\\php\\php.ini -d memory_limit=256M -f c:\\inetpub\\moodle\\auth\\ldap\\auth_ldap_sync_users.hpp
```
 Make sure you use the right paths in you server. And use the schedule you see fit for your setup (running it once a day is quite usual, more than twice a day is overkill in my humble opinion). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ldap synch not working
ResponsesInList.Text: Enable error logging in your database and have a look at it. 'Error inserting user' means the database refused to insert the record because something wasn't ok with the record data in the first place (invalied characters for a given field, strings too long that don't fit inside the field, etc.) With some of that information we can try to track the problem down. Saludos. Iñaki.

HOORAY! I've managed to fix the problem for our installation. I'm not a programmer, so you'll have to forgive my lack of technical description. I managed to track the problem to around line 50 in 'moodle/auth/ldap/auth.php' 
```text
 if (empty($this->config->objectclass)) { // Can't send empty filter
```
 
```text
 $this->config->objectclass='objectClass=*';
```
 
```text
 } else if (strpos($this->config->objectclass, 'objectClass=') !== 0) {
```
 
```text
 $this->config->objectclass = 'objectClass='.$this->config->objectclass;
```
 
```text
 }
```
 For our LDAP setup, objectClass was being set to objectClass=posixAccount, which is correct. However, for some reason, that was causing something to fail when doing any kind of ldap_read() or ldap_get_entries(), etc., through PHP. So the user information would come back empty. I 'fixed' it by taking out the if/else statement and just leaving it as 
```text
$this->config->objectclass='objectClass=*';
```
 I've spoken with our LDAP gurus and have determined exactly what the problem is, given our system. We don't force students to have a university e-mail address, or any other university centralized account. The only one they have to have is our central LDAP login one, called a Passport account. If they never use any other central account, such as e-mail, or a lab account, they will not get a UID. Without a UID they are not considered a 'posixAccount', hence, they don't show up when we query that type in the tree. So, the fix was to stop looking for a posixAccount and just set it to a wildcard. This is fine since Moodle already knows the exact user_dn when it does the lookup. Such a simple answer. Anyway, thanks for your help Inaki, and I hope that this info helps someone else fix their problems. --Mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Active Directory - workaround to the MaxPageSize
ResponsesInList.Text: We have been discussing the issues with AD and MaxPageSize for a while http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=49336 http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=49336 and I've come to believe that PHP will not support it anytime soon. Iñaki's patch never got much review or feedback, and the reason for that is that, AFAICS, there is no maintainer for the LDAP extension. It is a shame, and a waste of Iñaki's time and code, but well. Discussing an AD plan recently, I came up with a nice workaround that I don't think we had considered before, and would only take a couple of days to get together. The idea is to read from the AD server with a simple Perl script, invoked so that it prints the records to stdout while PHP reads them in. There's a bit of work involved in getting all the parameter passing working, data escaped correctly and encodings set properly, but it would work like a charm. For admins, there is a bit of additional work in getting Perl and a couple of modules installed on MSWindows.

I duly went to pear and attempted to install Auth_RADIUS as suggested. First problem, pear needed to be updated, given that one of their download servers had been turned off. Several other loadloads and updates later, I managed to get to the stage of running pear install --alldeps Auth_RADIUS only to find that it wanted pear/radius 1.2.4 (not available for download). Eventually found out that pecl install http://pecl.php.net/get/radius-1.2.4.tgz (not sure about the link) allowed me to go back and install Auth_RADIUS. Put the requisite extension=radius.so in php.ini, but no joy, moodle still said that Auth_RAIDUS was not present. Uninstalled and reinstalled several times over, installed everything I could from pear, still the message remained. pear told me that radius and Auth_RADIUS were present, the httpd had be restarted about 20 times, but still the accursed message remained. Eventally decided I would see what happend when I knocked out the code that checks for AUTH_RADIUS_PAP in /auth/radius/config.html ie the first three line stanza, I did, and everything worked as it should. Not sure what has happened, but the fact that one can't get pear/radius directly (ie need to go via pecl) may mean that Moodle doesn't pick up that Auth_RADIUS is there, when it is. Hope this is of some use to someone. I am very grateful to the gentleman in Bromley who set up the Radius plugin, much easier to use with an AD controller than LDAP , which seems hideously complex.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and eMinerva
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'll be honest and up front - I've been working for MXL for almost four years and seen both eMinerva and MXL through many phases of development. I'm not going to pretend that anything from me isn't going to be biased so I'll leave it you to judge whether or not my comments hold water. However, I do need to respond to some of the comments posted in this forum. First of all, since the original posts in October 2005 there have been many developments at MXL and changes within eMinerva that render many of these comments out-of-date or irrelevant. I'll describe these later. Secondly, lost results and inaccurate financial data is definitely not the typical experience of 99% of our clients - we would be out of business if that were the case. A few clients using some eMinerva configurations have experienced issues in the past, and one or two clients have felt they needed to pursue other SMS providers. All of these issues have now been addressed. The reality is that no software ships without bugs despite extensive testing, and even Microsoft products ship with bugs. However, when we find issues we've always taken them seriously and addressed them ASAP (at our expense) on all client databases. Having a web-based system gives us the flexibility, speed and ability to update all clients remotely. In response to the below comment: " Whatever the reason, this is was not forgivable and had created a very serious situation where quick action and great expense was required by our institution to contain the damage" MXL fixes issues on all client databases at our own expense. We take responsibility for any issues if they are our fault and fix them ASAP on the client's behalf. While we obviously regret the inconvenience caused, the comment about 'action and great expense required by our institution' is misleading, suggesting that MXL didn't do everything it could to fix the problem on the client's behalf, and it suggests that MXL made the client foot the bill for our mistake. This was definitely not the case. The third issue I want to address is eMinerva's speed and access times. Unfortunately Internet conditions is one area where we don't always have full control. However, we do have strict control over our secure data centre (which is the same data centre that hosts many Internet banking sites). Over the last four years there have been only two unscheduled outages - one for an hour and the other for 15 minutes. Recently we experienced a hardware fault with one of our servers which slowed down access times for a few days. But these are the exception and our data centre is very fast and reliable. Internet conditions between the data centre and the client's PC are often extremely variable and slow speed/outages can be caused by any number of factors — the client ISP, general Internet traffic, the local client network, the local PC hardware, or the number of concurrent Internet users at the client organisation. We understand that this is one area we can't control, and realise why some clients often blame eMinerva for being slow. We try to negate these problems by recommending appropriate bandwidth, ISP choice and network configurations during initial setup. Since the original posts in October 2005, there have been many developments at MXL and within eMinerva that render many of these comments out-of-date or irrelevant. Some changes include: a new Product Development manager and enhanced development team. Our development team has trebled since October last year and MXL's new Product Development manager has instituted very strict quality assurance measures for delivering eMinerva
moves away from the existing eMinerva framework. All software products use an underlying framework, and eMinerva's old framework has been the source of some issues in the past. This framework is now being phased out and replaced with one that is faster, more efficient, easier to test and more robust. The new framework also introduces many new usability enhancements and allows integration with newer, faster Internet access technologies
MXL winning government contracts and tenders to supply eMinerva to schools in New Zealand and Tasmania, winning over many competing SMS products. The NZ Ministry of Education and Tasmanian Department of Education have performed intensive and rigorous testing on eMinerva, independently proving that it is free from any defects that could cause issues such as those described in the original posts. It would be arrogant to suggest that the original posts are factually incorrect (they were essentially true when posted), or that people shouldn't be allowed to express opinions about MXL's software. But by putting these comments into perspective I hope I've provided both sides of the story. And yes, eMinerva does integrate with Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP: ID Number changed, what happens to account?
ResponsesInList.Text: We currently use LDAP authentication with our MS AD. The student ID Numbers are linked to their LDAP/AD sAMAccountName. It's set to update local on every login. We've had a few students get married and so Jessica Smith (jsmith) becomes Jessica Schmoe (jschmoe). Does Moodle treat the new jschmoe as a completely new user? Should I change the update local to never? Or is there a better way to avoid complications? Thanks in advance - JD

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP: ID Number changed, what happens to account?
ResponsesInList.Text: Does Moodle treat the new jschmoe as a completely new user? Yes, it does. If they have a different username (and if you are using sAMAccountName as the username attribute they will), they are different users. Should I change the update local to never? That's one option, though I would't recommend doing it. Or is there a better way to avoid complications? You can change user accounts in Moodle first and then in your LDAP directory. This way the username <-> id mapping inside Moodle remains the same. Also, using something that can vary over the time is not a good candidate for ID Number. We use an internal student number for this, and we store it inside employeeNumber attribute. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP: ID Number changed, what happens to account?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you very much for you reply. I'm wondering, then, how we might fix the problem?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP: ID Number changed, what happens to account?
ResponsesInList.Text: Why is a new account being created? Because of the new username? We just need Moodle to know that it's an updated account and not a new account. The problem is, there's no way Moodle can know it's an updated account. There's nothing[1] in the account (neither in Moodle's nor in AD's) that holds that information, much less a way to retrieve it. So from Moodle's point of view it's another, completely unrelated, user account. That's why I told you to 'teach' Moodle first (by manually changing the username and ID Number to the new values), then change the user account in AD later. This way, when the user logs in with the renamed account Moodle knows it the same user and maintains all the user history. As far as I know, there's no other way to do it. Saludos. Iñaki. [1] In fact, if you want to use the SID of the account as the username, that would be stable across renames, but I doubt your users would remember something like 1-500-1234-5123-12443-12344-1-12321 as their username

ResponsesInList.Text: What fields need to be changed in Moodle? I suspect I'll need to directly modify the MySQL database ? Perhaps w/ phpMyAdmin ? Here's what's linked via LDAP authentication: User attribute - sAMAccountName First name - givenName Last name - sn Email address - mail ID number - sAMAccountName I believe Moodle has another internal ID Number, and this is what we want to remain unchanged. I'd greatly appreciate a step-by-step or checklist of changes from an experienced Moodle admin to aid me in accomplishing our goal here . Supposedly: User has name change Make change to Moodle's database Make change to AD User logs in with new name All Moodle info from old name is present with new name

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP: ID Number changed, what happens to account?
ResponsesInList.Text: 1.- User has name changed. 2.- Go to Moodle database and find the record for the user account, in mdl_user[*] 3.- Change the 'username' field to reflect the (real) user name change. You can change the other fields too, but you don't need to, as they will be automatically updated on next logon. 4.- Make changes to AD. 5.- User logs in with new name. 6.- All moodle info from old name is still present with new name. The key is doing the changes to AD AFTER you've done the changes to Moodle. Saludos. Iñaki. [*] You'll need to do this change directly in the database, as Moodle doesn't allow you to rename LDAP usernames as of now (see MDL-10095 )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SQL code to get list of admins
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, you should not use SQL since admins definition has dramatically changed between Moodle 1.6 and 1.7 .. and may change in future ; use the well crafted API calls described in phpXref Moodle documentation. http://xref.moodle.org In your case you have the function get_admins(), defined in lib/datalib.php that returns an array of admin users objects : if ($admins = get_admins()) { foreach ($admins as $admin) { print $admin->username ; } } you also have get_admin() that returns the first one. finally here is a "famous piece" of code found in many places in Moodle that send an email to all admins from the first one : $recips=get_admin(); foreach ($recips as $admin) { mtrace('Emailing '. $admin->username .' about '. count($logs) .' failed login attempts'); email_to_user($admin,get_admin(),$subject,$message); } cannot be simpler ) HTH

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quick Question about Users in moodle and AD
ResponsesInList.Text: My understanding of how this works, please someone correct me if im wrong. When a user tries to logon to moodle, with the authentication enabled for ldap, the moodle web server sends a ldap query to your domain controller. The DC tries to service the query within AD and returns results to moodle. If the user exists and credentials are correct, moodle prompts new users to create a moodle profile. If the user allready exists access is permitted. If credentials are wrong or user doesnt exist, you get a username/password error. I would dare say there is a far more technical explanation of what is going on behind the scences but this is my basic understanding from my observations.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quick Question about Users in moodle and AD
ResponsesInList.Text: Would you be willing to provide a detailed posting of your config settings? I'm also trying to auto-populate my user's profiles from ActiveDirectory but no details are showing up after the user successfully logs in. Users are prompted with the Edit Profile which I want to be done automatically for them. I've tried numerous settings with no luck. Any assistance would be appreciated TIA .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quick Question about Users in moodle and AD
ResponsesInList.Text: ldap_host_url: ourserversname (not domain name) ldap_version: 3 ldap_preventpassindb: yes ldap_bind_dn: adusername@domain (you should set up a user specifically for searching active directory) ldap_bind_pw: ourpassword ldap_user_type: MSActiveDirectory ldap_contexts: OU=Our Users,DC=ourdomain,DC=co,DC=uk ldap_search_sub: yes ldap_opt_deref: no ldap_user_attribute: sAMAccountName I found that the sAMAccountName bit is really important otherwise it doesn't always use the network login name to do the authentication Also, ldap_contexts should refer to at least one branch of your AD tree The branch works its way up, so 'OU=Our Users' is the point at which we want LDAP to start looking and the parent to 'OU=Our Users' is ourdomain.co.uk - notice that you need to have 3 DCs for ourdomain.co.uk *Your AD might not have a .co .uk on the domain name - if this is the case then you will get away with simply DC=yourdomain ldap_search_sub: yes - this is important because it tells LDAP to search for subitems of 'OU=Our Users'. If we didn't use this then we would need lots of ldap_contexts to cover each branch - one for staff, and one for each student year group. Its easier to search sub branches and its just as fast.

domain

When we fixed that bug in 1.7 (I think we fixed it in 1.7, but don't have the data here to confirm it), the real underlying bug surfaced. But I haven't been able to reproduce it so far (much less fix it). I'll have a look at it in a more detailed way in the following days and see if I can reproduce it in my test environment, now that I know it's related to posixAccount and OpenLDAP. If you find anything with your LDAP admin, please publish your findings here Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Mass Deleting Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All, I have attached a simple script to mass delete (set delete flag in users table) users who have been inactive for a specified number of days. (A simple modification would allow deletion of users based on first access, i.e. delete users who enrolled in a given year). This is a stand alone script which does not require alteration of Moodle source files. It creates log files of deleted users (in sub directory of moodledata) so actions can be undone / reversed from within the script. I wrote this as an alternative to the more advanced modification detailed here: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=72880

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mass Deleting Users
ResponsesInList.Text: I have attached another version of the script which contains some corrections / improvements.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mass Deleting Users
ResponsesInList.Text: just out of interest. Is it a bad idea to delete users en mass from the user table directly?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mass Deleting Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes it is. There are multiple data in other tables that relate to the record in the user table, and there could be files linked to that user that will never be deleted. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mass Deleting Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, as Inaki says there are lots of tables that reference the data in the users table, if you delete users you will "orphan" these records which can cause problems on upgrade. *** Within Moodle there is no way to delete a row from the mdl_user table, instead the "deleted" flag is set to "1". Thus, when you delete users in Moodle the records remain in the users table. This is a bit of a problem in the long term as it means your database keeps growing.... The script I wrote does not delete rows, it just sets the "deleted" flag, and logs the affected users in files, so, it is possible to restore users from the same script. *** There is one place in Moodle where records are deleted, this is in the cron job which runs every few minutes. This will delete incomplete / un-confirmed accounts.

So, one day, I disabled it under authentication and all of a sudden nobody could log in who was registered using the external database. It was if their passwords didn't work. No error message, no nothing, just the passwords acted as if they were invalid. The system would even allow a password reset, but even that password didn't act like it worked (ie. Password invalid). So, I think the problem is that all of the users that were registered with the external database have their user authentication method under their profile set to External Database . So, each time the user logs in, it's trying to check the fields of an external database that is no longer active (eye closed under authentication methods). So, to keep the system running, I re-enabled the external database (eye open). If I want to get rid of the external database, is all the data stored in Moodle? I thought it was. Is the only thing left to do is go through each user profile and change the authentication from external database to manual and then it will work? This is going to be a pain, is there a faster way to do this vs edit each user profile? Am I on the right track? Thanks! Aaron G. (Moodle 1.8.2)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Database  No Longer Needed
ResponsesInList.Text:
This is going to be a pain, is there a faster way to do this vs edit each user profile? Yes there is. You can go to the database and issue a query like this (be sure to make a full backup of your database before doing this, just it case ): 
```text
UPDATE mdl_user SET auth='manual' WHERE auth='db';
```
 Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Database  No Longer Needed
ResponsesInList.Text: Am I on the right track as to what is causing the problem? Yes you are . If a user profile states that the authentication to use is an external database, Moodle will use that external db even if the data is replicated internally. You need to flag the user as 'manually authenticated' explicitly. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can Moodle authenticate against more than one LDAP domain?
ResponsesInList.Text: I was asked the following question about the LDAP authentication: Can Moodle authenticate users against an LDAP server with multiple domains? . I asked the person: Do you mean different contexts? He answered: No, different domains! I have to admit I have little knowledge of Active Directory and LDAP (I am not a systems administror).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can Moodle authenticate against more than one LDAP domain?
ResponsesInList.Text: What is the correct answer to give to this person? If we are talking about Active Directory domains, the correct answer is: it depends. If they are part of the same AD forest, then querying the Global Catalog server(s) you can. The Global Catalog (GC) stores a limited replica of the data of all the AD domains that make part of the forest. By default the first DC of the first domain of the forest is the GC (if I'm not mistaken), but you can activate this role on any DC (see http://docs.moodle.org/en/LDAP_Authentication for the details on how to do it). Then you just need to specify the contexts of all the domains you want to uses as the source of authentication. If the domains are not part of the same forest, things get complicated. There is no single point that holds a unified view of all of the domains and Moodle is not designed to cope with this situation. However, you can build a meta-directory that presents a 'unified' view of all those independent directories (domains). We've done it by using OpenLDAP running on Linux, with the 'meta' backend and it's been working for 24 months now. If you are interested in this kind of solution, you can have a look at http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=55143#p288946 Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can Moodle authenticate against more than one LDAP domain?

ResponsesInList.Title: Upload users -- type?
ResponsesInList.Text: When uploading users from a flat file, what do the optional type1-type5 fields mean? Sorry if this is obvious, but I am just setting up Moodle for the first time. Jan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upload users -- type?
ResponsesInList.Text: I would say that the type1 to type5 fields are for backward compatibility. Prior to Moodle 1.7, roles were fixed (Editing Teacher, Student, Non-editing teacher), so they could have numeric codes (1, 2, 3). Sarting with Moodle 1.7, the aforementioned roles were still there (they consititute "predefined" roles) but you could also define new roles -- in fact, an open-ended number of new roles like Parent. It would be impossible to assign universal numeric codes to such roles. Instead, he role names themselves must be used (use the roles' "short name"). The upload format lets you upload up to five roles for each user (role1 in course1, role2 in course2, etc.) and possibly even in a group context (role1 in group1 of course1, role2 in group2 of course2). If you have not defined any new roles and are only using the predefined roles, go ahead and use the type fields. If I were you I would experiment. Create a short sample upload file, login to demo.moodle.org as admin, upload your file and see how it works.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: where login/signup.php includes auth/email/auth.php ?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Where does login/signup.php include auth/email/auth.php ? In the line that reads (in 1.8.x): 
```text
$authplugin = get_auth_plugin($CFG->registerauth);
```
 $CFG->registerauth is the name of the selected signup plugin, which by default is the email plugin. get_auth_plugin requires the needed files and creates an auth plugin object that you can later use to whatever authentication operations you need. Saludos. Iñaki.

This may be of your help. LDAP server This method provides authentication against an external LDAP server. If the given username and password are valid, Moodle creates a new user entry in its database . This module can read user attributes from LDAP and prefill wanted fields in Moodle. For following logins only the username and password are checked. LDAP server settings Host URL Specify LDAP host in URL-form like 'ldap://ldap.myorg.com/' or 'ldaps://ldap.myorg.com/' Separate multipleservers with ';' to get failover support. Version 2 3 The version of the LDAP protocol your server is using. LDAP encoding Specify encoding used by LDAP server. Most probably utf-8, MS AD v2 uses default platform encoding such as cp1252, cp1250, etc. Bind settings Hide passwords No Yes Select yes to prevent passwords from being stored in Moodle's DB. Distinguished Name If you want to use bind-user to search users, specify it here. Something like 'cn=ldapuser,ou=public,o=org' Password Password for bind-user. User lookup settings User type Novell Edirectory posixAccount (rfc2307) posixAccount (rfc2307bis) sambaSamAccount (v.3.0.7) MS ActiveDirectory Default Select how users are stored in LDAP. This setting also specifies how login expiration, grace logins and user creation will work. Contexts List of contexts where users are located. Separate different contexts with ';'. For example: 'ou=users,o=org; ou=others,o=org' Search subcontexts No Yes Search users from subcontexts. Dereference aliases Choose... No Yes Determines how aliases are handled during search. Select one of the following values: "No" (LDAP_DEREF_NEVER) or "Yes" (LDAP_DEREF_ALWAYS) User attribute Optional: Overrides the attribute used to name/search users. Usually 'cn'. Member attribute Optional: Overrides user member attribute, when users belongs to a group. Usually 'member' Member attribute uses dn Optional: Overrides handling of member attribute values, either 0 or 1 Object class Optional: Overrides objectClass used to name/search users on ldap_user_type. Usually you dont need to chage this. Force change password Force change password No Yes Force users to change password on their first login to Moodle. Use standard Change Password Page No Yes If the external authentication system allows password changes through Moodle, switch this to Yes. This setting overrides 'Change Password URL'. NOTE: It is recommended that you use LDAP over an SSL encrypted tunnel (ldaps://) if the LDAP server is remote. Password-change URL Here you can specify a location at which your users can recover or change their username/password if they've forgotten it. This will be provided to users as a button on the login page and their user page. if you leave this blank the button will not be printed. LDAP password expiration settings. Expiration no LDAP Select No to disable expired password checking or LDAP to read passwordexpiration time directly from LDAP Expiration warning Number of days before password expiration warning is issued. Expiration attribute Optional: overrides ldap-attribute that stores password expiration time Grace logins No Yes Enable LDAP gracelogin support. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: FirstClass Authentication allows anyone with a correct fc UserID access
ResponsesInList.Text: FirstClass's FPP function returns "Sorry. You are not allowed to login with the FPP interface" ONLY if the username and password are correct - a mis-matched combination returns "Could not login. Bad user name or password." Moodle's auth/fc module treats the "Sorry..." message as proof that the user information is accurate and doesn't care beyond that. Now, if the username you provided for the module ISN'T a subadministrator then you'll have issues because the module will fail when trying to pull user data. I'm now using 1.8.2 but the auth module that came with 1.4.3 (I just upgraded last week) uses the same method. ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 1.8: admin notice about new user registration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, We allow self-registration to our Moodle website users. How can the website admin get noticed about a new user registration? This is necessary to enrol the new student into the courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.8: admin notice about new user registration
ResponsesInList.Text:
In file .../lib/moodlelib.php, around line 3614 (for 1.8.1+, version 2007021511), you'll see a line that reads: 
```text
return email_to_user($user, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 Just add a line above that one with the following text: 
```text
email_to_user($from, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 This way, the site admin will get the same registration email that the registering user. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Edit confirmation e-mail content
ResponsesInList.Text: If you mean the email which is sent out to people when they create their own accounts, which contains the link to activate the account, the text is in your lang/en_utf-8/moodle.php file, and is in the section beginning $string['emailconfirmation'] = " If you edit that file with a text editor (eg Notepad), you can change the text that gets emailed out. If you're referring to a different email, the chances are that it's another string in the same file.  If you load moodle.php into your text editor and then do a search for a word or phrase in the existing email it should find it for you.  Make sure you make a backup copy of moodle.php first so you can restore it if you break it - you're actually editing a PHP script, so one full stop or comma out of place and it'll all go horribly wrong! HTH Chris

Any help would be grate. Rich.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Auto Authentication With MS Server 2003 step by step guide?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rich, I think what you want is something called LDAP - this will allow Moodle to authenticate users to against the domain, so they'll use the same username and password to log on to Moodle as they used to log on to the computer. There's pretty full instructions here: http://docs.moodle.org/en/LDAP_authentication You may need to talk to your school's IT techies for them to set it up on the domain controller, then you should be able to point Moodle at it and authenticate your users. HTH Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Auto Authentication With MS Server 2003 step by step guide?
ResponsesInList.Text: Rich, There is a third party plugin for NTLM (NT Lan Manager).  This uses the MS protocol to log folks into Moodle based on thier AD usernames and passwords. How much do you know about Moodle admining? NTLM is very similar to LDAP authentication, but it allows for the browser to send the user data without sending the user to a log in screen.  See this thread about the settings for LDAP. Internet Explorer is compatible with NTLM, to make Firefox compatible you need to edit the configs.  Type about:config into the address bar in FireFox then set the value of network.automatic-ntlm-auth.trusted-uris to the name of the moodle server you want to use ntlm. Hope that gets you started. Good luck, Miguel

Anyway, if you need to add an admin account and you have access to your Moodle database, this is what you can do: 1.- Get the user 'id' of a normal user you can login with: SELECT id FROM mdl_user WHERE username='your-username'; Let's suppose you got a user id of '123'; 2.- Insert a new rol assignment with roleid=1 (admin) and contextid=1 (site) for you user id: 
```text
INSERT INTO into mdl_role_assignments (roleid, contextid, userid, enrol) VALUES ('1', '1', '123', 'manual');
```
 (the primary admin should always have an enrolment value of 'manual', that's why I specified it above). Your user should no be a site administrator. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Search Engine - How to grant access by IP address?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks so much for your repley! What you suggested is over my ability though. The search engine does handle cookies. Could you please read the following Zoom tech support to see anything helps?  I tried the first one, it doesn't work. The 2nd and 4th are not for us either. My only hope is # 3. Zoom search is a really excellent search engine. It offers Google like text based search, scans MS word, PDF and many other type of files, and offers lots of nice features. And it's real cheap. I think it really worth a try in Moodle if we get the authantication solved. Cookie-based or session-based authentication Cookie-based authentication however, usually appears as a form on a page, and is implemented by server -side scripts (such as PHP or ASP or Cold Fusion). Because there is no standard method as to how this can be implemented, Zoom is unable to automatically login to access the protected web page. However, there are alternative methods to bypass this. If your website uses cookie or session-based authentication, try the following: You can login to the site via Internet Explorer, then immediately afterwards (do not close IE ), start indexing from Zoom (making sure it starts spidering from a page within the site rather than visiting the login page again). The cookie set in Internet Explorer should carry across to Zoom (make sure to check the option "Use cookies from Windows and IE" under the "Authentication" tab of the Configuration window). Note that this method will not work with per session cookies (see notes below). If your login page can receive username and password information via the URL , then you can use a spider start point / URL with this information specified as GET parameters (for example, " http://www.mysite.com/login.asp?username=george&password=ringo "). If you can modify the server-side script that does the authentication, you could change it so that it allows a user-agent containing the word "ZoomSpider" to bypass the login process. Similarly, you could also allow the IP address of the indexing computer to bypass the login process. If possible, consider using Offline mode to index your website. This requires a copy of the website to be accessible on your local hard disk, allowing Zoom to simply scan all the files without having to get pass the security restrictions on your live site. Note however that offline mode is not suited for websites which depend heavily on server-side scripting to deliver content (eg. PHP or ASP driven websites). See the Users Guide for more information on Spider mode and Offline mode . Important : If you are using one of the above methods to allow the spider to login to your cookie or session-based authenticated site, you need to make sure that the spider does not follow a link to the "logout" page, subsequently logging itself out of your website. You can prevent this by simply specifying the logout page in the "Skip pages and folder list" (in the Configuration window, under the "Skip options" tab), eg. "logout.asp" or "&logout=1", etc. Notes regarding persistent and session cookies If your website uses cookies for authentication, you should check whether the cookies are persistent or session based. Persistent cookies are stored for a specified length of time. These cookies can retain information between visits to a site, and is typically implemented with a "Remember my login information" option on your login page. Session cookies are used to only store information within a session or single browser window. These cookies will be deleted and invalid when a session is terminated (eg. when you close your browser window). If your site uses session cookies, note that some of the methods listed above (namely #1) will not work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ldap Authenication Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All, I am trying to set up the authentication process for our Moodle application for our college. I have to admit that PHP and LDAP is not my area of expertise and have minimal knowledge of either technology. Our network team have informed me that the ldap connection string is ldap://bbldapt1 I have then entered a user account (Cn=nldapuser) and password so that I can bind to that account to perform a search for the user when they try to login to Moodle. The users are located (as I have been told) in a tree structure which has a main node of "o=SC_Admin" under this node are located the college administrators and they appear in the format (CN=AdministratorId). There is another node under "o=SC_Admin"  labelled "OU=lecturers" which contain the college lectuers and they also appear in the format "CN=LecturerId). Therefore, I have set up the ldap authentication page as follows: ldap_host_url: ldap://bbldapt1 ldap_bind_dn - "nldapuser" ldap_bind_pw - "nldapuser" ldap_user_type - "Novel Edirectory" ldap_contexts - "o=SC_Admin;o=SC_Admin, OU=lectuerers" When I  try to login to Moodle I receive the following error messages "LDAP-module cannot connect any LDAP servers : Server : 'ldap://bbldapt1' Connection: 'Resource id #29' Bind result: '' or LDAP-module cannot connect any LDAP servers : Server: 'ldap://bbldapt1 Connection: 'Resource id #43' Bind result: '' Does anyone know where I am going wrong? Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ldap Authenication Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: The problem is with your bind user credentials. You need to use the full distinguished name (DN for short) of the user. Most probably is something similar to this: cn=ldapuser,o=SC_admin but to be really sure, ask your network admins for the full distinguished name of that user. Then, the LDAP contexts is not right. In LDAP, you write thing from the leafs to the root of the tree, so if ou=SC_Lecturers is under the root o=SC_Admin, the you need to write it like: ou=SC_Lecturers,o=SC_Admin I hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single Sign On with Novell eDirectory.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi These are our settings, for LDAP Settings LDAP server settings ldap_host_url: Specify LDAP host in URL -form like 'ldap://ldap.myorg.com/' or 'ldaps://ldap.myorg.com/' Separate multipleservers with ';' to get failover support. ldap_version: 2 3 The version of the LDAP protocol your server is using. Bind settings ldap_preventpassindb: No Yes Select yes to prevent passwords from being stored in Moodle's DB. ldap_bind_dn: If you want to use bind-user to search users, specify it here. Someting like 'cn=ldapuser,ou=public,o=org' ldap_bind_pw: Password for bind-user. User lookup settings ldap_user_type: Novell Edirectory posixAccount (rfc2307) posixAccount (rfc2307bis) sambaSamAccount (v.3.0.7) MS ActiveDirectory Select how users are stored in LDAP. This setting also specifies how login expiration, grace logins and user creation will work. ldap_contexts: List of contexts where users are located. Separate different contexts with ';'. For example: 'ou=users,o=org; ou=others,o=org' ldap_search_sub: No Yes Search users from subcontexts. ldap_opt_deref: Choose... No Yes Determines how aliases are handled during search. Select one of the following values: "No" (LDAP_DEREF_NEVER) or "Yes" (LDAP_DEREF_ALWAYS) ldap_user_attribute: Optional: Overrides the attribute used to name/search users. Usually 'cn'. ldap_memberattribute: Optional: Overrides user member attribute, when users belongs to a group. Usually 'member' ldap_objectclass: Optional: Overrides objectClass used to name/search users on ldap_user_type. Usually you dont need to chage this. Force change password Force change password: No Yes Force users to change password on their first login to Moodle. Use standard Change Password Page: No Yes If the external authentication system allows password changes through Moodle, switch this to Yes. This setting overrides 'Change Password URL'. NOTE: It is recommended that you use LDAP over an SSL encrypted tunnel (ldaps://) if the LDAP server is remote. LDAP password expiration settings. ldap_expiration: No LDAP Select No to disable expired password checking or LDAP to read passwordexpiration time directly from LDAP ldap_expiration_warning: Number of days before password expiration warning is issued. ldap_exprireattr: Optional: overrides ldap-attribute what stores password expiration time passwordExpirationTime ldap_gracelogins: No Yes Enable LDAP gracelogin support. After password has expired user can login until gracelogin count is 0. Enabling this setting displays grace login message if password is exprired. We couldn't have got working without help in these forums - I know it has been discussed. Works very well for us. Andy D

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single Sign On with Novell eDirectory.
ResponsesInList.Text: If I recall correctly, the NN client includes a service that behaves like an oldstyle unix ident service. We read login info from it via tcp, and then made the corresponding LDAP lookups. You have to trust your network security though It is a pretty weak scheme unless you are prepared to glue the RJ45 sockets and prevent your users from running any non-sanctioned software. What we could do is (a) check that this approach will work in your network, (b) tell you all you need to know about the level of security it provides (so we can sleep at night) and (c) extract the the code we have from an old custom moodle and port it to 1.7 or whatever it is you are using

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP and sync users
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'm really sorry Alfons. I lost most of my Moodle unaswered forum posts, and your question was one of them. Let's have a look at it. In Users - Authentication - ldap_user_attribute = CN
in Courses - Enrolment LDAP - ldap_member_attribute = memberUid
I had to set "ID number = uid" in Users - Authentication in moodle and create a field uid for every person in ldap with the content of memberuid. Now, I think your problem is using a different LDAP attribute for ldap_user_attribute and 'ID Number' in Users - Authentication. The current sync code tries to match ldap_user_attribute values in the LDAP server with the ID Number values inside Moodle. If they don't match (and unless cn == uid in your setup, they won't match), every (ldap) user is deleted in Moodle and a new one is created from LDAP values (but having a differente id number, which breaks enrolments, as you've seen). So you need to use an ID Number value that: matches the value of ldap_user_attribute in LDAP authentication, and matches the values you get for your LDAP groups when you query the ldap_member_attribute on them. So I would use the 'uid' attribute for ldap_user_attribute and 'ID number' (as long as uid has a unique value for all the users in your LDAP tree), and make sure the LDAP groups store 'uid'[1] values for all of their member users. [1] Active Directory stores full distinguished names, for example. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A couple of questions about MNet
ResponsesInList.Text:
Great to hear that. Why can't they just go to the other site and
"log in" and have the other server checked
in the background? Several reasons. I'll use the terms IDP (Identity Provider - "your originating moodle") and SP ("Service Provide" - any other moodle you go to): User education! Reinforce the idea to your users that they should ONLY EVER type their username and password in your instituational Moodle. Not give their username/password to any site that claims to be affiliated. It could very well be a scam. It is actually a security problem. If you can go to any SP moodle in the network, then that SP will see your password. No matter how much we encrypt things, we cannot get around that problem. Currently, you only entrust your IDP with your username/password. By logging in to your IDP, as a user we can offer links for you can jump across from any moodle to any other that is listd in your "hosts" block, and/or across the courses in your "my courses" list. That always happens via your IDP. By logging to your IDP we can do sophisticated session keepalives. That is, you can roam the MNET "network" without your session timing out. (And also logs are transferred back to your IDP - the admin there can see your activity). By the way, did I mention the "my courses" block? Once yoyu have enrolments setup, that's probably the best way to navigate the network. With time and experience we may be able to do those things better, and perhaps even allow logins to remote servers. But there are a lot of social and technical issues to overcome there Edit: and with scams and password theft on the rise, I think that even if we could support it, we shouldn't. User education is really important, and the last thing I'd do is teach users to give their username and password to "other" websites.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A couple of questions about MNet
ResponsesInList.Text: Ah yes, of course. Point taken. I agree you'd never want to enter your username and password into some "other" site. The issue for me is that both sites are "mine". Random thought alert... this is off the top of my head, so no guarantees its workable... This would be true of any institution with faculty Moodles all connected by MNet though, so there may be other people who'd quite like to see login on the "other" site too. It would allow users to browse around with guest access, and use any links to login that they come across - for example at the point where they attempt to post to a forum or self-enrol on a course. It would be annoying if you have to go back to your IDP to log in, then find your way back to wherever you wanted to post/enrol. Maybe you could make it a setting that the admins could control?

ResponsesInList.Text: In that case, require login early in one central location In all scenarios that I can think of, it's always better if each user knows a single unequivocal place where they are expected to login.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A couple of questions about MNet
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jenny - sorry I missed your last post. I can't think of anything else that roaming users are unable to do, apart from having their profiles edited. Otherwise, I think they're full members of the remote site. Your final question - we didn't provide the capability for users to log in directly at the remote site, because it's kind of a trust issue. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Squirrelmail / Moodle / LDAP
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi James, First thing you need to understand is that Squirrelmail is an Email client not a server (the fact that it runs on a web server tends to confuse people). As a client, Squirrelmail needs an email server to run against and the email server is what you'd want to configure to auth. against LDAP. Having clarified that, there's a number of good open source email servers out there that you can use. I personally use Courier MTA . It is a SMTP , POP3 and IMAP Server and can authenticate against LDAP, MySQL , Postgres , Shell accounts, and pretty much anything else you throw at it with a little scripting. It's extremely powerful and works quite well with Squirrelmail. We have both Moodle and Courier-IMAP/Squirrelmail authenticating against our LDAP server and it works quite well. If you have any more questions, feel free to let me know. Jay

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AutoEnrol on Course Using MSSQL
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm fiddling with this now using a mySQL database , and everything should work similarly. Referencing the screen shot below, I'll explain what I have discovered so far. - The server name should be self explainatory. - The user is a user on the database that has read access to the table you need to reference. - The password is this users password - The db_name is the database name that the table which contains student -> course mappings exists. - Table with student -> course mappings. If this information is across several tables, you will have to create a view to reference it all. Field Mapping - localcoursefield is the name of the field in the mdl_course table which you will use to reference the course in the database. Before you can actually autoenrol, you will need to set up the courses and give them an ID number which you pull from something. This is where you will store the id number in the moodle table. Once you create a course, you can peek at the DB and see what the columns are called. - localuserfield is the name of the field in the mdl_user which you will use to reference a student. You can use any field, but I used the special ID field. I've also locked this field so students cannot change it. - remotecoursefield is the name of the field in the external DB that contains the course numbers in the student -> course mappings. - remoteuserfield is the name of the field in the external DB that contains the student id in the student -> course mappings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting LDAP to work (a solution)
ResponsesInList.Text:
If you want all of your currently POP3-authenticated users to use LDAP instead, you can execute the following SQL query in your moodle database (I suppose your moodle users' table is called mdl_user): 
```text
    update mdl_user set auth='ldap' where auth='pop3'
```
 If you just want some of the users instead, execute something like this: 
```text
	update mdl_user set auth='ldap' where username = 'the-username-I-want-to-chage'
```
 Saludos. Iñaki.

I'm going to look into this in the moodle code, but here's a head's up of what the issues are at my company... Large number of people in AD (nothing magic here). AD is organized by geographical location-- many buckets for users. Not  as simple as "Students" and "Teachers". It is unrealistic to enumerate all of the locations in the AD tree where someone could be located. Instead of enumerating all the search bases, the process can be handled in two steps: The first query with the bind user id looks up the person and finds their full DN (will include their location). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting LDAP to work (a solution)
ResponsesInList.Text: Nice write-up, Lou! I had to discover most of this stuff for myself when I integrated our Blackboard site with AD a few years ago, and I had forgotten how frustrating it was. One more tip: The domain controller (DC) servers on our campus change names and IP addresses from time to time as old hardware is replaced, and other things happen. It doesn't happen all that often, but having a hard-coded array of specific server names in my Blackboard or Moodle LDAP configurations would mean updating them every time the AD managers change a DC.
