ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP course creator weirdness
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm having some odd problems with this function. It's all set up and working, or at least was until alittle while ago when I stripped down the course creator role to nothing but moodle/course:create. This was to stop creators showing up in the course participants list, which worked, but now when teachers log on, they are being made into site level teachers instead of course creators. I have a feeling this is to do with this code around line 563 of auth/ldap/lib.php $sitecontext = get_context_instance(CONTEXT_SYSTEM); if ($creatorroles = get_roles_with_capability('moodle/legacy:coursecreator', CAP_ALLOW)) { $creatorrole = array_shift($creatorroles); // We can only use one, let's use the first one so I have changed the legacy course creator role to allow instead of prevent, although I'm not sure this will fix things.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP course creator weirdness
ResponsesInList.Text: I've also just noticed (to my horror) that removing those people from their sitewide role as teacher and making them course creators instead removes them from their own courses entirely. I've has to manually add them all again. What's going on???

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP course creator weirdness
ResponsesInList.Text: Got it! The teacher role had course 'Legacy ROLE:Course Creator' set to 'allow'. Seems that the automatic assignment of course creator role uses the first role with that capability enabled, so if more than one role has it, you'll have problems. Hope that saves someone some hassle. Matt

ResponsesInList.Title: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, Perhaps I had better introduce myself and say "Hi, I'm a guy at Catalyst working on multi-authentication" It is in a state of unfinished-ness, but we have a branch from 1.6 available (for interested developers and testers only at this stage!) here as a git repository: http://git.catalyst.net.nz/gitweb?p=moodle-r2.git;a=shortlog;h=mdl-mnet-multiauth For those not using git/cogito, you can download snapshots from the snapshot link: http://git.catalyst.net.nz/gitweb?p=moodle-r2.git;a=snapshot;h=mdl-mnet-multiauth The major changes are: Refactoring each set of auth functions in auth/foo/lib.php into a plugin class analogous to enrolment plugins. This class is now contained in the file auth/foo/auth.php Adding some supporting functions to moodlelib to retreive and check for existence of plugins Shifting the auth plugin configurations into the config_plugin database table, using 'auth/foo' as the plugin name Changing the admin interface to allow selecting and reordering of multiple plugins (similar to the up/down arrows in admin/filters) Instead of $CFG->auth, we now have $CFG->auth_plugins_enabled Tweaking Moodle code to handle auth plugin classes So, now we can say

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Wohoo! The work started with Howard Miller and Iñaki Arenaza is coming together! We've been talking about multi-auth for a while -- with this code you can actually have several auth plugins enabled at the same time ... you can fake it a bit with the current code, but there are a million little pitfalls in doing that -- this work is supposed to cure them all, and make it a supported mode of operation. That in itself is a useful thing. So there have been quite a few changes in the auth modules -- all of them, and we need testers and review. And comments from from plugin authors, maintainers & users. This whole thing is aimed at 1.8 though we will probably put together an unsupported "at your own risk" patch on top of 1.7 for people who want to play with it. Long term, this is part of a cunning plan to get us doing transparent SSO and a few other things across moodle installations. If you really want to know, I've written some notes at http://docs.moodle.org/en/Community_hub_technotes

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: If there is interest in multi-authentication with multiple instances of the same plugin type (e.g., using several ldap servers with completely different sets of parameters -which is not yet possible with the great work from Jonathan-) I'd be grateful if some knowledged enough about the internals of authentication (that's you MartinL, among others ) would answer some of the remaining questions at http://docs.moodle.org/en/Multi_Authentication so I could design a proper solution to this Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Hola Iñaki! You never ask easy questions do you? I think once the switch to class-based auth is done and all the bugs fixed, it should be easy to make multi-instance by + modifying how we store config data to be per-instance -- perhaps extend mdl_config_plugins a bit to match the table 'auth_instance_settings' you describe + changing admin/auth UI to match + changing how we deal with mdl_user.auth I am interested -- and we were discussing it with Jonathan yesterday -- but it's beyond our immediate goals (we have to get the rest of ' moodlenet ' done!). So I'm hoping we move the ball close enough to the goal so that a top scorer can kick it in. Is that you? BTW , I had forgotten about that Wiki page. We could describe there the implementation as it's happening.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: You never ask easy questions do you? The easy ones were already answered here in the forums... So I went for the rest So I'm hoping we move the ball close enough to the goal so that a top scorer can kick it in. Is that you? Well, I don't play soccer but basketball, so I'm not really sure But the work Jonathan is doing will greatly simplify things like upgrading to the full multi-instance scenario undoubtly. Maybe part of the problem with the questions in the wiki page is that I'm a little bit too ambitious, allowing things like instance removal, which create their own set of problems. But I guess we'll arrive there someday anyway, so the questions will need to be answered sooner or later. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello -- I have some recent experience with multiple-authentication systems. I recently wrote an LDAP server in PHP which had these requirements: - Run as a daemonized socket server and decode LDAP network requests - Authenticate users against a fast local MySQL cache, Apple Password Server, and ActiveDirectory. - Be able to easily extend the code to add additional authentication backends as necessary. - Each authentication backend can accept two operations: Authenticate (bind), Change Password. - Synchronize users' passwords across all systems. - The system must respond with a valid LDAP response. Happily, this worked and the project is being used to authenticate all staff and students on all web-based infrastructure in our school district (~10,000 users). Because of the small number of backend systems that were required up-front, I didn't do much work abstracting them as "plugins", and I'm not sure how much of my code would be valuable here. I can locate the UML for the design, though, and share if there is interest. I CAN share the number-one lesson learned: how does the system respond if one (or more) backend systems become unavailable? Our Apple Password Server installation has had an ongoing issue which causes it to ...not quite give up, but take up to 30 seconds per request for authentication. What should the system do? Should we fork for every authentication request? (that invites its own set of problems, though) ...etc. Worth considering.

You don't have a 'connect' timeout because you don't need it (connect calls ldap_init(), which doesn't really connect the server until an operation is attempted, so no need to have a timeout . ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Authentication
ResponsesInList.Text:
I know this might be rather late in the day but can I ask if the pending multi-authentication will work with multiple plug-ins of the same type? As far as I know, this isn't supported yet. There is some work in progress, but it's far from being complete. To explain, we've got a weird situation at our organisation where we have not just two separate AD domains, but two separate AD forests, so we need to be able to specify a couple LDAP/AD servers in the Moodle config. (we've tried adding a recursive server, but that doesn't work due to the separate forests). In case you are in a hurry, you can build a meta-directory using OpenLDAP and its 'meta' backend. This creates the illusion of a single LDAP tree which incorporates the two (or more) separete LDAP trees. This is what we are currently using at our site. We are using OpenLDAP (on a Linux box, but you should be able to do this in Windows too) to 'glue' toghether two AD domains (in two different forests) and present it as just one single domain. Beware: this breaks if you have users with the same displayName/cn/sAMAccountName in both domains and you are using any of them in Moodle for anything (as the meta backend can't tell them apart) This is our setup: First AD domain (in one of the forests): eteo.mondragon.edu Domain controller: 10.0.0.1 Second AD domain (in the other forets): bidasoa.eteo.mondragon.edu Domain controller: 192.168.0.1 Both domains have a user called 'ldap-user' we use to bind to AD. We create a meta directory called eteo.mondragon.local Each of the real directories appear as leafs of the meta directory, namely onati.eteo.mondragon.local (for the first AD domain) and bidasoa.eteo.mondragon.local (for the second one). We have a bind user (the root user in fact) for the meta directory, called 'ldap-user' aswell. This is the user Moodle needs to bind to the meta-directory. All of this is running in a Linux box with the IP address 172.31.1.1. This is the ldap server Moodle needs to use. Here is our slapd.conf file (have a look at the man pages to see what every line means): ----- [/etc/ldap/slapd.conf] ----- 
```text
database meta
suffix "dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local"
rootdn "cn=ldap-user,ou=moodle-staff,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local"
rootpw {SSHA}12345678901234567890123456789012
lastmod off
dncache-ttl disabled

access to attrs=userPassword
 by dn="cn=ldap-user,ou=moodle-staff,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local" write
 by anonymous auth
 by self write
 by * none
access to dn.base="" by * read
access to *
 by dn="cn=ldap-user,ou=moodle-staff,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local" write
 by * read

uri "ldap://10.0.0.1/ou=moodle-users,dc=onati,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local"
pseudorootdn "cn=ldap-user,ou=moodle-staff,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=edu"
pseudorootpw "ldap-user-password"
rebind-as-user
map objectclass groupOfNames group
suffixmassage "ou=moodle-users,dc=onati,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local" "ou=moodle-users,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=edu"
```
 
```text
uri "ldap://192.168.0.1/ou=moodle-users,dc=bidasoa,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local"
pseudorootdn "cn=ldap-user,ou=moodle-staff,dc=bidasoa,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=edu"
pseudorootpw "ldap-user-password"
rebind-as-user
map objectclass groupOfNames group
suffixmassage "ou=moodle-users,dc=bidasoa,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local" "ou=moodle-users,dc=bidasoa,dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=edu"
```
 ----- [/etc/ldap/slapd.conf] ----- Then in Moodle's LDAP authentication settings we have (I show only the most relevant settings, fill the rest as usual): ldap_host_url: ldap://172.31.3.4 ldap_bind_dn: cn=ldap-user,ou=moodle-staff, dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local ldap_user_type: posixAccount (rfc2307) ldap_contexts: dc=eteo,dc=mondragon,dc=local Notice we set the user type to posixAccount, even if we are using Active Directory for the real users. Remember Moodle is really talking to OpenLDAP, not to AD domain controllers. This is sort of a reverse LDAP proxy. Just a couple of warnings: You can't change users' passwords in AD from Moodle (or any other AD data, for that matter). If one of the AD domain controllers is unreachable (for any reason) the meta directory times out after a long wait (something in the order of a couple of minutes or so), even if the user we were looking for is in the other domain controller. This is a limitation of the OpenLDAP meta backend (at least in the version we are using). We have been using this framework for over 18 months without any side effects (except the ones mentionned above) for LDAP authentication only . We haven't tested LDAP enrollment at all, and we haven't run auth_ldap_sync_users.php at all, so I can't comment on them. Saludos. Iñaki.

That's why I proposed the separation between the authentication types (db, ldap, etc.) and the authentication instances ( this db, that other db, this other ldap server, etc.) in the 'multi-instance' multi-auth "specification" ( http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Multi_authentication ). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Nested Groups with LDAP Auto-Enrollment
ResponsesInList.Text: In order for enrolment to work with AD, there are a couple of 'ugly hacks' you have to do. First, you have to map 'distinguishedName' into ID Number for all of your users (students and teachers). The enrolment code matches user's ID Number with membership information, which in the AD case is the distinguished name of the user(s) belonging to the group. Second, you have to 'widen' the database fields for the ID Number if your distinguished names are longer than 64 chars (otherwise they are trimmed and the enrolment doesn't work). You need to alter the mdl_user table, to make 'idnumber' field as long as your longuest distinguished name (128 should be enough for most cases). But this doesn't stop here (that would be too easy ). There are a couple of places in the Moodle code where ID Number is trimmed to 64 chars too, so you need to 'fix' those places aswell. One is in .../lib/moodlelib.php (around line 2486 in 1.6.1, in fuction truncate_user_info()), other is in .../auth/ldap/lib.php (around line 404 and 407 in function auth_sync_users()), and the last on in in .../lib/db/migrate2utf8. xml (around line 424). Does anyone know if the openldap patch is available for php in a win32 environment, specifically Windows 2000 Server with IIS5 The patch is platform independent (doesn't depend on operating system or web server). You just need to recompile PHP yourself after patching the relevant files. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Nested Groups with LDAP Auto-Enrollment
ResponsesInList.Text: But how can we allow moodle to read from sub groups too? You need to modify the code. Right now Moodle assumes groups members are just plain users, and treats them so. If any of the members are groups themselves, Moodle doesn't notice and treats them as regular users. Note that you can eventually have groups inside grupos inside grupos inside grupos... You get the picture: you need to expand the search recursively until you don't get any new groups. This is feasible, but nobody has done it yet Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP AUTH aNd Batch Upload Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Stuart I have the MySQL addition loaded and using this I selected the mdl_users table (to check the values) and the SQL Tab to enter the code. I then typed in: UPDATE mdl_user SET auth = 'ldap' WHERE auth = 'manual' AND password = '' The check for the blank password picked out accounts which either had been LDAP prior to my upload or which were uploaded with a blank password. It excluded accounts such as guest and admin which need to remain manual. WARNING Take a backup of the database before running an UPDATE query like this. Unless you are certain of the command it may not select the rows you were after You can check with the following code: SELECT * FROM mdl_user WHERE auth = 'manual' AND password = '' Hope this helps Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling 'No Authentication'

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Controlling 'No Authentication'
ResponsesInList.Text:
I guess I need to change my signature, you are the third person to call me 'Saludos' ('saludos' is the Spanish word for 'greetings'). My real name is Iñaki Now to the real question. You can edit .../lib/moodlelib.php, function send_confirmation_email() (around line 7119 in 1.6.3+) and search for the line that reads: 
```text
return email_to_user($user, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 and change it to: 
```text
return email_to_user($from, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 The message will be sent from the primary admin address to the primary admin address, so make sure it's a valid address Saludos. Iñaki.

return email_to_user($user, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email-based authentication but with Admin authorisation
ResponsesInList.Text:
Got this answer from another post. You can edit .../lib/moodlelib.php, function send_confirmation_email() (around line 7119 in 1.6.3+) and search for the line that reads: 
```text
return email_to_user($user, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 and change it to: 
```text
return email_to_user($from, $from, $subject, $message, $messagehtml);
```
 The message will be sent from the primary admin address to the primary admin address, so make sure it's a valid address Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: OpenLDAP on Fedora Core 4
ResponsesInList.Text: This is fairly stock, but I remember going through a bunk of tutorials before I got it running. I already had a bunch of unix users so I used the migration scripts to seed the ldap. But you can also enter into the phpldap admin. Note that when logging into web console use the matching info as specified in the slapd.conf for the rootdn I have my password set to clear text, but there is a procedure to change that to a hashed password. This is from a debian system. # Allow LDAPv2 binds allow bind_v2 # This is the main slapd configuration file. See slapd.conf(5) for more # info on the configuration options. ####################################################################### # Global Directives: # Features to permit #allow bind_v2 # Schema and objectClass definitions include /etc/ldap/schema/core.schema include /etc/ldap/schema/cosine.schema include /etc/ldap/schema/nis.schema include /etc/ldap/schema/inetorgperson.schema # Schema check allows for forcing entries to # match schemas for their objectClasses's schemacheck on # Where the pid file is put. The init.d script # will not stop the server if you change this. pidfile /var/run/slapd/slapd.pid # List of arguments that were passed to the server argsfile /var/run/slapd.args # Read slapd.conf(5) for possible values loglevel 1 # Where the dynamically loaded modules are stored modulepath /usr/lib/ldap moduleload back_bdb ####################################################################### # Specific Backend Directives for bdb: # Backend specific directives apply to this backend until another # 'backend' directive occurs backend bdb checkpoint 512 30 ####################################################################### # Specific Backend Directives for 'other': # Backend specific directives apply to this backend until another # 'backend' directive occurs #backend ####################################################################### # Specific Directives for database #1, of type bdb: # Database specific directives apply to this databasse until another # 'database' directive occurs database bdb # The base of your directory in database #1 suffix "dc=usd465,dc=com" rootdn "cn=admin,dc=usd465,dc=com" rootpw yourpasscode # Where the database file are physically stored for database #1 directory "/var/lib/ldap" # Indexing options for database #1 index objectClass eq # Save the time that the entry gets modified, for database #1 lastmod on # Where to store the replica logs for database #1 # replogfile /var/lib/ldap/replog # The userPassword by default can be changed # by the entry owning it if they are authenticated. # Others should not be able to see it, except the # admin entry below # These access lines apply to database #1 only access to attrs=userPassword by dn="cn=admin,dc=usd465,dc=com" write by anonymous auth by self write # by * read # Ensure read access to the base for things like # supportedSASLMechanisms. Without this you may # have problems with SASL not knowing what # mechanisms are available and the like. # Note that this is covered by the 'access to *' # ACL below too but if you change that as people # are wont to do you'll still need this if you # want SASL (and possible other things) to work # happily. access to dn.base="" by * read # The admin dn has full write access, everyone else # can read everything. access to * by dn="cn=admin,dc=usd465,dc=com" write by * read

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error: could not bind ldap anonymously
ResponsesInList.Text: Whoever runs your LDAP system needs to supply you with the credentials of a user that has permission to query the LDAP database. You just enter the DN (ldap_bind_dn) and the password (ldap_bind_pw). Then Moodle can 'pretend' to be this user and your LDAP server will talk to Moodle. The DN would look something similar to this: cn=moodle,ou=Users,dc=mycollege,dc=ac,dc=uk

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP connected, but users not allowed in
ResponsesInList.Text: Humm, the settings look OK at first sight. What puzzles me is that using a regular user to bind to the AD results in 'invalid credentials'. Any regular user should be able to bind to the AD. Otherwise, they won't be able to log into Windows itself, or retrieve their own data, change their passwords, etc. Unless you AD admin has secured the AD access for the default, non-encrypted, connection type (LDAP). If you can't bind as a regular user to AD, no user will be able to log into Moodle, as the username/password verification against AD is done trying to bind to AD with that username+password. Maybe you should ask your domain admin if there are additional requirements for binding to AD (like using encrypted LDAP or such). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Using onsite Active Directory to authenticate with offsite webhost
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi fellow moodlers. I am researching the best way for my students to access moodle. First I set up my own webserver as an intranet and authenticated with our Windows 2003 Server Active Directory using LDAP . However students could not log in from home because it was all local. We do not have the infrastructure to host a webserver on our internet connection so I set up moodle on our externally hosted website which allowed students to access from home and school but I have to maintain all their authentication details manually What I would like to know is if it is possible to authenticate using AD over the Internet? Our AD is on site and behind a firewall and our moodle is hosted externally on a subscribed webserver. Thanks, pburney

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using onsite Active Directory to authenticate with offsite webhost
ResponsesInList.Text: I think it is possible, though I've not done it - I'd imagine you have to allow access through your firewall to the domain controller.  However, I'd be extremely reluctant to do it, because you're opening up a huge hole in your security - there will be a route into your domain controller, and thence to your entire network, from the whole world. A better solution for you might be to do what I've done with our Moodle-based Staff Intranet.  It's set up for email authentication, but it will only accept our college email addresses when they set up their Moodle account, so only people with college email addresses will get the authentication email to which they have to reply to enable the account.  It's not as convenient as LDAP, but it would save you having to allow the whole world access to your domain controller. HTH Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using onsite Active Directory to authenticate with offsite webhost
ResponsesInList.Text: you should use Secure LDAP as you are communicating via servers over the www - so make sure you specify LDAPS://yourinternalserver.com rather than ldap://yourinternalserver.com you will need to open up TCP port 636 to the fixed IP address of your externally hosted webserver in your firewall so that the webserver can communicate with your Domain server. NOTE: if you are using a shared webserver, all the applications/websites on that server will have the ability to get through your firewall to see your domain, so make sure you are forcing an Authenticated Bind. - eg make sure that anonymous access via LDAP to AD is disabled, and in the ldap settings for moodle enter a user to Bind the LDAP connection with. hopefully that gives you somewhere to start! (and isn't too cryptic!) good luck!

Moodle is however at it's best when used as a tool to have students construct knowledge collaboratively. That's why forums play such a vital role in Moodle. I think you may be missing out on one a lot of Moodle's functionality when you don't try to make the user part of some kind of community. You can still allow people guest access to courses for convenience sake.

ResponsesInList.Text: My Pre K-12 school is seriously considering adapting Moodle as a way of delivering online learning in the High School. However, the IT department head wanted to know if there were a way for parents to view their child's work other than logging in with the child's password. If anyone knows  how a parent account can be directed toward's viewing the child's account, please let me know. It would be greatly appreciated. Thanks, Allen A. Buchanan Shorecrest Preparatory School

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating a Parents' View in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: We were hearing lots at the Moodlemoot from both Martin and the OU team about the new roles and permissions architecture , which will be able to give parents some degree of access. I'm not clear from what we heard that linking two (or three) accounts together is part of the plan, so that eg Amy's parents get to see her work and not other people's, but I think this is so central to the school-age requirements that this will have to be on the spec. There are other privacy issues too: it's possible that some students will feel constrained in their forum contributions if they know their parents are going to be reading them: it's one thing to tell parents how a child is getting on, it's quite another to have them sitting in and observing every lesson .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating a Parents' View in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for your response Miles. It is well taken indeed. I would not feel comfortable with parents having access to some of the forum discussions because the whole idea is to get the middle schoolers to open up. Maybe there should be flexibility to select the modules the parents do have access to. In rare situations, a parent may need access to Johnny's forum discussion because it was inappropriate. This kind of linking would definitely help. I'm thinking that a PHP programmer could design a plug-in with the forementioned capabilities.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating a Parents' View in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Miles gthat the linking together of accounts a number of child accounts to a parent id is vital for implementation in schools. I also agree that the cildren may need spaces to njoin in without parents watching. However, we do have to realise that the Data Protection and Freedom of Information acts will impinge of this. At least in the UK. I guess the human rights act does too. I feel quite torn at times. I will respond in a different way to discussion and debate when I am in forums that my bosses or subordinates (?) are also in rather than just peers. But as a parent I believe I should have the right to monitor anything my child does. Of course I would want to give them the freedom to collaborate without my presence stifling things but we cannot promise confidentiality away from parents willynilly. We need to follow the law in any implementation. Despite it being an ass at times. I think this may be a tip of an iceberg but in a pragmatic sense one that we may never see in day to day stuff. However it will only take one test case to cause us all a lot of grief. Lets hope we can get bthis right (I mean across elearning generally not just Moodle implementations) otherrwise innovation and real benefit may suffer.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle, LDAP and a Radius Server
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle has a plugin architecture for its authentication modules. It is very simple (trivial) to create a new auth plugin that uses Radius for its backend, using http://pecl.php.net/package/radius . If you need an intermediary to restrict what AD info is visible form the DMZ, you can always use an intermediate LDAP server. Properly configured, LDAP servers can act as a gateway to other servers -- you'd have to configure the LDAP server to only know about the parts of the AD tree you want to make available.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle, LDAP and a Radius Server
ResponsesInList.Text: Clive, There isn't a RADIUS plugin at the moment, but creating one isn't too hard. If you're feeling intrepid... Go to your Moodle directory, and create a new directory inside 'auth' called radius. This will be moodle/auth/radius/ . Copy the config.php and lib.php files from moodle/auth/pop3 into your new directory. Now, for the hard part... you will have to replace the contents of the auth_user_login() function in lib.php with whatever you need to do with Auth_RADIUS. You'll need to read the Auth_RADIUS documentation (actually, I think the doco is in the Auth module, Auth_RADIUS hasn't got much doco). The good news is that Auth_RADIUS supports MS-CHAP v1 and v2, and a few other variations. Let us know how it goes -- we'd like to be able to include the plugin in Moodle.

Creating a RADIUS plugin Here is the process I went about to create a RADIUS plugin to work with Moodle 1.4 on a Fedora Core 3 platform: 1) Create a subdirectory of moodle/auth called radius 2) Create the following config.html file within the radius directory:

: 3) Create the following lib.php file in the radius subdirectory: addServer($CFG->auth_radiushost, $CFG->auth_radiusnasport, $CFG->auth_radiussecret); if (!$rauth->start()) { printf("Radius start: %s
", $rauth->getError()); exit; } $result = $rauth->send(); if (PEAR::isError($result)) { printf("Radius send failed: %s
", $result->getMessage()); exit; } else if ($result === true) { //       printf("Radius Auth succeeded
"); return true; } else { //       printf("Radius Auth rejected
"); return false; } // get attributes, even if auth failed if (!$rauth->getAttributes()) { printf("Radius getAttributes: %s
", $rauth->getError()); } else { $rauth->dumpAttributes(); } $rauth->close(); } ?> 4) Add the following lines to the end of moodle/lang/en/auth.php : $string['auth_radiustitle'] = 'Use a RADIUS server'; $string['auth_radiusdescription'] = 'This method uses a RADIUS server to check whether a given username and password is valid.'; $string['auth_radiushost'] = 'The RADIUS server address. Use the IP number, not DNS name.'; $string['auth_radiussecret'] = 'The shared secret for this client
(The radius server admin will know this)'; $string['auth_radiusnasport'] = 'The  value  of  the NAS-Port attribute (0 will do fine)'; 5) Install the PHP modules associated with RADIUS using the following Linux BASH commands as root: pear install RADIUS pear install Auth_RADIUS 6) Moodle will now authenticate a RADIUS user successfully

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle, LDAP and a Radius Server
ResponsesInList.Text: Turning this into a PEAR::Auth plugin does not seem straightforward. Also I cannot clearly see how creating such a plugin would fit in with the existing set of authentication plugins. The PEAR::Auth package provides methods for creating an authentication system using PHP. Currently it supports the following storage containers to read/write the login data: * All databases supported by the PEAR database layer * All databases supported by the MDB database layer * All databases supported by the MDB2 database layer * Plaintext files * LDAP servers * POP3 servers * IMAP servers * vpopmail accounts * RADIUS * SAMBA password files * SOAP It seems to me that the above list encompasses many of the existing separate authentication schemes already embodied within Moodle. Consequently, unless the existing schemes are to be ported over to PEAR::Auth a separate Auth::RADIUS plugin fits in much better.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle, LDAP and a Radius Server
ResponsesInList.Text: This is looking good! I have some minor requests that have to do with tidyness really. 1.5 is XHTML compliant, and to keep that compliance, we need the tags in lowercase, and attribute values quoted. And tags that don't have a matching closing tag need to end in "/>". The warning you print when Radius isn't there should be in a <tr><td> set -- I did it wrong in auth/ldap (just fixed it!) and you've based your work on it. Should know better than to follow my example ;) And there's been another change that affects all auth modules. You'll need to add a call to print_auth_lock_options() in config.html, like auth/email and others do. Don't follow auth/ldap or auth/db for this. You may want to consider using the new config_plugins table to store some of your settings, but that's completely optional at this stage.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Filemaker and moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: "You can use this, for example, to create a link to Google that is different for each user, a search on their surname for example." how do i go about this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Filemaker and moodle
ResponsesInList.Text:
If you go to Google and search for "test" you'll see the url looks something like this: 
```text
http://www.google.co.uk/search?hl=en&safe=off&q=test&btnG=Search&meta=
```
 Optionally, you can get rid of the useless bits to leave: 
```text
http://www.google.co.uk/search?q=test
```
 So what you've got is a call to a program called `search` with a parameter called `q` which tells it what to search for. If you choose Link to a file or website from the Add Resource menu then you can put the url in the location field as: 
```text
http://www.google.co.uk/search
```
 and then hit the show settings button next to parameters , and from the dropdown menu choose (e.g.) surname and in the variable name box next to it put `q` . When a user accessesses this resource they will not go to the url you typed in but instead be sent to a slightly longer, Moodle-generated url based on their own user details, for example: 
```text
http://www.google.co.uk/search?q=Redmond
```
 I hope that helps, it's a bit complex if you're not used to messing with URLs but it's a relatively simple yet very powerful way of connecting two web applications together, once you get the hang of it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Email accounts at one POP3 server
ResponsesInList.Text: IMHO this should not be submitted as a fix but as an alternate auth plugin. That is you should duplicate the pop3 folder in the auth folder and rename it to, for example, pop3subdomain or pop3sub. You also need to add new strings to language file, defining the new plugin. Then, when you visit the auth admin page or edit user profile, you will have that new plugin showing among the authentication options independently from the standard pop3 plugin. You might find it yourself handy to have the standard plugin further available as well. To switch all or select users on your site to the new plugin, edit the database using myPhpAdmin or similar and run SQL UPDATE command to change pop3 to pop3subdomain (or whatever you called it). Finally, let me repeat the security warning I mentioned earlier. If your pop3 server supports users from multiple domains, lets say, school1.edu and school2.edu, depending on the server setup, you have two possible scenerios: 1. the server requires only username part for login; that is it does not distinguish whether user belongs to school1 or school2. 2. the server requires username%domain or user@domain for login (I have seen servers using both variants); that is it recognizes users within their domains only. Your code will work fine for case 2 and it will be secure. But... in this case, you could simply modify the pop3 plugin to automatically include the domain after username (assuming that all your users use the same domain -- exactly a case where having this as an extra plugin may come handy -- one can even have multiple variants if they support more than one domain) to accomplish the same. In case 1, such a plugin does not provide full protection: If I have an email address myusername@school2.edu, I can login to your site by entering myusername@school1.edu -- your domain verification will pass and the server will not know a difference. Granted, as supplied, your code will actually always fail to authenticate in this case since it does not strip the domain part, which is good here, but this security hole should be stated clearly so nobody tries to modify this code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple Email accounts at one POP3 server
ResponsesInList.Text: I have focused above on the interaction with the pop server only, but, of course, there is also a match needed for Moodle username, so in case 1, if username stored in Moodle includes full domain, the code can be secure as well. In that case, instead of checking the domain, the lib.php needs to strip the domain part before passing it to pop server. Actually, if domain is part of username, the check should not be needed in case 2 either.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Authentication: This is probably a stupid idea, but...
ResponsesInList.Text: I think I understand your reasoning. It's not a half-bad idea. Let me just throw you another idea just for your consideration. I don't know your situation, so I don't know if this is better than your idea would be or not. What you could do is create a list of students' names and e-mail addresses in a program like Microsoft Excel. Then, you could have Excel generate a user name and a password for each student. For example: firstname lastname email username password John Doe jdoe@example.com jdoe john Jane Roe jane@example.com jroe jane If you put in the formula "=LOWER(LEFT(A2,1) + B2)" under "username" and "=LOWER(B2)" under "password," you could use Excel's AutoFill feature to create user names and passwords. (Just drag the little box in the lower-right corner of the cell down until you reach the end of your names.) Then, all you'd do is export the file as a "Comma-Separated Values (.csv)" file and use Moodle's import feature to create the new usernames. Then, just let the students know that their username is their first initial and their last name, and their password is their first name in lowercase. (You'd have to tell them to change their password immediately.) I know this seems a little complex, but it might work for your situation right now. The import feature is documented at http://moodle.org/help.php?file=uploadusers.html . Of course, your idea might work better for your situation. But I hope this helps. -Todd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I print a list of user names and passwords for a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Tammy, Printing the usernames would be pretty easy...you could just export the information from the users table in the database . The passwords is another matter since they are encrypted in the database. I don't think there is a way for you (teacher or admin) to see the user passwords unencrypted. However, you really don't need to see the passwords. If a student forgets their password, you (site admin) can open their profile and type changeme in their password field, then just contact them and let them know the new password and that they will be forced to reset it when they login. Even if you could see their passwords, you would have to contact them and let them know what it is...so, it's just as easy to just change it and communicate the new password to them. It will also be reassuring to some users that even the site admin can't get their password. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can I print a list of user names and passwords for a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: No. Moodle does not store the passwords in plain form. The passwords are encrypted into a string of numbers and letters 32 digits long. When the student logs in, what they typed is then encrypted, and the encryptions are compared. You could change their password from your account and tell them the new passwords, but unless you had this list from the beginning, you cannot create a list of passwords.

ResponsesInList.Title: Prefilled login form -> not good for Shibboleth
ResponsesInList.Text: Today I was pointed at something concerning the Moodle login page. Apparently Moodle uses a longterm cookie that contains the encrypted username to "prefill" a users loginname on the login page. This may or may not be good feature (I won't talk about security considerations at this place) but in the case of Shibboleth authentication this is definetly not a very good thing (the same may be true for CAS), because it confuses Shibboleth users when they see that the manual login field already contains a username. They could be tempted to submit their Shibboleth password to Moodle, which for security reasons should not be submitted to Moodle. This is not necessary because the user provides the password only at this home institution, Moodle trusts this institution and therefore never should need a users password. I haven't noticed that myself because my webbrowser overwrote that field with a manual login username and apparently everyone else uses Moodle in Shibboleth-only login mode Therefore I would like to submit the attached patch for the file moodle/login/index.php that prevents that a username is shown on the login page if the authentication method is set to shibboleth. Alternatively, I would suggest that there should be an option in the Moodle Variable settings (probably under the security options) that allows to deactivate the prefilling of the username field.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ldap Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Having had the same troubles as many of the others in this thread, I wanted to let you know how I solved the PHP ldap module problem. I am running Windows 2003 and am using the Windows Moodle Quick Installer 1. I had to put the php path in my environment path variable in windows 2003. To check to see if yours works before beginning, do start, run, cmd and enter Type php -m, you should see output, if not you need to set the path To see what your path currently is, type path and hit enter To set the path on Windows 2003, go to the control panel and click on System.  Then click on the advanced tab and you should see at the bottom a button for environment variables, click that. You now have a box where you can edit several things including your path. (Keep in mind that if you use %SystemRoot% in you php path that it does NOT point to c:\, instead to c:\Windows\) 2. I had to alter the PHP.ini file. Interestingly enough, I kept thinking I had done this. It turns out that at least on my system, I have two php.ini files and one php5.ini.  To find out which one your system is actually using, login to moodle as the administrator, go to the admin page and at the very bottom press the php Info button. About the seventh line down you should see something like this: Configuration File (php.ini) Path  C:\moodle\apache\bin\php.ini Open and edit that file and remove the semicolon (;) in front of the line : extension=php_ldap.dll 3. After these two things restart apache and you should no longer receive the red error message. Scott

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Turning off guest
ResponsesInList.Text: I've done something very similar, although I need to add each person manually. Log on to your site and click "Users," then "Authentication." At the top, choose "Manual accounts only" from the dropdown box labeled "Choose an authentication method." The page will refresh. Then, scroll down and choose "Hide" from "Guest login button." ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing to Email Authentication Method - a few questions
ResponsesInList.Text: First, if you plan to restrict emails to certain domain or domains only, this means that your users all have email accounts there. If so, consider pop3 authentication instead of email. This way, they use the same password as they use for email. No need to deal with lost/forgotten passwords, for example. Second, the default (site) authentication is what is used for new users. However, authentication is set on per user basis and whateverwas set at registration stays for ever (only admin can change it by editing user profile or massaging database directly). So all students that registered under manual will stay manual unless you change them all to something else. 1. not that I know off. But you can manually set a few people to using it and see how it works for existing users. 2. no, all stays unchanged. 3. yes. 4. yes. 5. You will probably need to preregister users that will be expected to use paypal until multi-auth is in Moodle release.

ResponsesInList.Title: LDAP Concerns
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a few concerns with the ldap implementation. First: the ldap bind password fields in both the authentication and enrollment pages is returned to the browser, and the enrollment page is in a text box not even a password box. Some may argue this is unimportant as you can simply use a non priviledged user for your queries.  but what if you want to provide the ability for users to update personal information and have it reflected in in ldap.  I am infinatly familiar with both active directory as well as NDS and their respective implementations of LDAP and in both cases this requires and administrative login to accomplish updates to user accounts. This poses a huge security hole for those of us using ldap.  Can someone tell me where these usernames and passwords are stored? can they be encrypted(even a syncronous hash would be better than none)?  Can the passwords be removed from the query that populates the enrollment and authentication forms(i.e. if blank dont change password)? As those passwords are easily read by viewing the soruce html. Second: in an ldap implementation the user idnumber is used to compare to group membership for the purposes of enrollment. this field is limited to 64 characters, anyone with an ldap tree more than one level deep can easily exceed 64 characters.  I increased mine to 128 and I'm not 100% sure if that is enough.  When you start adding in all the cn=, ou=,dc=, and ',' it doesnt take much to fill it up.  To make this change the database table had to be altered and two php files had to be modified.  Now I'm not one who likes to create unused space in a database but that is the advantage of varchar fields.  as for the arrays how about we dont limit them at all. and lastly who cares about temp tables they are flushed when finished.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP sync unenrols users from classes
ResponsesInList.Text:
I think I have the answer, but I'm not sure whether this is a bug in
the code or a configuration error on your part (if I've read the code
correctly). The problem is, the code uses 'ldap_user_attribute' to search for
users, when running the sync code. And then creates a temporary table
where it stores all the values it get from LDAP. In your config, this
is the sAMAccountName. So you only have sAMAccountName's in your temporary table. But then, when comparing existing Moodle users when the users in the temporary table, it uses the idnumber field for the existing Moodle users. And then, unless you have mapped sAMAccountName onto the ID Number field for users, kaboom!, all your Moodle users are no longer found in the temporary table and are marked for deletion (and subsequently deleted). As I say, I'm not sure if this in an error in the code, or in your configuration (that doesn't match what the sync code is doing/expecting). Saludos. Iñaki.

It allows (or should allow) username to be mapped from another LDAP field, something that in practice isn't very useful. At least the use of idnumber as the main key should be optional. Long term the use of idnumber vs username needs to be reviewed. I suspect we went astray at some point, and things aren't 100% consistent. With the current code, as long as idnumber is populated everything works correctly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle, LDAP, and a firewall
ResponsesInList.Text: I am working on this right now. I have an offsite web server trying to authenticate back to an active directory server behind a Sonicwall firewall. The first thing you need to do is make sure that you can bind to LDAP from inside your firewall. To do this, download a free LDAP browsing tool such as LDAP Browser/Editor 2.81 ( JAVA client - click on browser.jar to run program).  If you are able to bind to your ldap server from inside, then the next step is to configure your firewall to port forward your LDAP traffic to the correct server. The configuration will depend on your server, but you must forward the applicable ports below to the LDAP server's local ip address (inside firewall).  This way, any traffic that hits your firewall on those ports (i.e. Moodle authentication) gets to the right place inside your firewall. You may not need all of the ports below. The basics are the following: port 389 (LDAP) port 636 (LDAP over SSL) port 3268 (Global catalog server for Microsoft Active Directory) port 3269 (Global catalog server for Microsoft Active Directory w SSL) If you need some clarification, let me know. I am actually still having some binding issues with mine, but I can see the LDAP server from outside, so I know it is simply a mattery of tweaking my Moodle settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: ldap auth and sync with 250,000 user objects
ResponsesInList.Text: We have a fairly large flat ldap tree with close to 250,000 user objects. I had a need to sync some of the users so that the database enrollment module can do it's things (haven't gotten that far yet; though)... Given the way our tree is structured the only way I could pick and choose was to do a fairly advanced search and just work with those objects.. So I added some code to allow for this. As an example, here is the search I need to use. Though I do believe any search that limits results based on specified critera will work. (&(objectclass=Person)(uid=*)(|(eduPersonAffiliation=student academic)(eduPersonPrimaryAffiliation=employee))) I'd appreciate any feedback. You also need to add an entry to your auth.php lang file such as: $string['auth_ldap_advanced_search'] = 'This setting overrides the ldap_objectclass and provides advanced search capability for filtering user objects. Particularly useful for sync operations if you have a large flat tree. This should be set to a valid ldap search query. Test the query first! Since ldap_objectclass is no longer used the search specified here should include it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing the creation of new accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: You can also modify Moodle to not accept logins for users who are not in the database . This is a hack but it will work for any authentication mode, so in some way it is a cleaner solution for you. To accomplish this, open the moodle/lib/moodlelib.php file and find function authenticate_user_login(). There, after the first "if" block, insert the following: if (! $user->id) { return false; // no go for new users } Then in file moodle/lang/en/moodle.php find string 'invalidlogin' and modify it accordingly. For example: Invalid login, please try again. Note: if you are not a registered user on this site, you must contact Moodle Administrator to create a new signup. Of course, you need to do this in every language pack you use.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal - Implement basic multiple authentication (1.6)
ResponsesInList.Text: Howard, Cool -- I'm happy to set up the branch for you, well tagged and tidy, if you want. Then all you need to do is a checkout to a separate dirrectory or "switch" an existing checkout to the branch. Both trivial operations. Let me know if you want me to do this (and then I'll later be better prepared to help you to merge it into HEAD). (edit: I see you've got it done) Now, with regards to the stuff we're discussing... Classes If you're after self-documenting code, we can have manual auth be the 'reference' and make sure it has all the API methods, even if commented out, with generous comment blocks. Using base classes + inheritance backfires often, and this is a textbook scenario. This is an API that grows organically, and that tolerates (and even encourages) people to maintain their private plugins, like those that interoperate with UglyLegacyStudentMgmtSystem. I maintain a few of them. So, we define the API today, and provide 'default' methods in the base class, which doubles up as 'manual/internal enrolment'. So 100 plugins are written against it, that count on the current API behaviour, 20 of those are official, 80 'private', local customizations. Now, in 1.8, we decide to grow the API adding a new series of methods. Normally, when you're growing an API like this, you add methods that are optional so it's backwards-compatible (or forward-compatible, depending on where you are standing). But with a strategy of "it's always in the base class" we're fsck'ed. We will add them to the base class, because (a) the code expects them, (b) for self-documentation, and (c) because it implements 'manual auth' which can truly make good use of them. And as soon as we do that, all the plugins will magically do the same thing that the base class does even if it doesn't make any sense at all and breaks them badly . The workaround usually involves adding more methods to the API, where each module reports what it knows how to do, or what 'features' it has, and is generally awful, because you check whether you should call the method before you call it, lest inheritance does its job. Oh my!. So, the best way is to have manual as a normal class, have no base class, and wrap calls to methods that are optional in the API with method-exists(). This is important, and is something I'll have to get around to fixing in the enrolment plugin architecture, but it hasn't been a problem so far (because we haven't changed the API... but we're about to ) Inheritance is tricky business, and defines an 'internal' API between base class and subclass that is full of funny interactions. All good for an in-house project, but hell for this loosely organized tribe. (In other words, inheritance is too tighly coupled, we need loose coupling for a plugin API). Edited for clarity and typos.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal - Implement basic multiple authentication (1.6)
ResponsesInList.Text:
hi Howard, I would still prefer - as I always do - to implement an abstract
bass class. This can be completely non-functional (ie, even the
manual auth inherits from it). Cool. An 'empty' base class is better than a functional one, but let me try to explain why no base class for the plugin API is even better . I am not against inheritance at all. In fact, I think some classes (manual, for instance) should be written so that other classes can inherit from them if they want. But that is an option of the 'new' plugin author. APIs are the point where we provide for loose coupling and inheritance is way too tight. We end up with a brittle API. Using an empty base class only buys you not having to call method-exists() , but that also means not being able to call method-exists() and get a meaningful answer . The short version is that inheritance is not for that, and we would be misusing it. The long version goes... Imagine you want to offer an option in user/edit.php only if the auth supports it. Impossible to tell because method-exists() isn't useful. Of course, you can start implementing methods that report back what the object knows how to do, a poor man's substitute for method-exists(). Yuck. And having 
```text
   if (method-exists($obj, 'danceforme')) {
```
 for optional methods is good because it is self-documenting. No-one has to guess whether 
```text
   if ($obj->danceforme()) {
```
 Returned true because it's implemented and did dance correctly, or because it's not implemented and we hit a dummy method. If knowing this is important (and often is) we're fsck'ed The base class method would either say "ignore this if you
don't want the functionality" or "you must override this
method" which is surely clearer and more elegant? That approach is valid for in-house development (and still doesn't scale very well along code size and team size) of a few tightly controlled classes. But it's not elegant in an API where you don't have any control on your plugin implementors and want to offer backwards compat. I started doing OOP about 9 years ago now, and used it in 4 languages with different approaches and teams (and specially, team sizes of up to ~25). Inheritance is tightly bound, and brittle, and you can see things go wrong with large codebases, large teams and long project history. Large FOSS projects using OO this way spend a lot of time and effort coordinating the smallest changes in their base classes, partly because backwards compat is almost impossible unless you version your class names. Sorry for the rant, as you can surely tell, I don't want to go that way -- and I'll probably be stuck maintaining ext auth plugins for a few seasons to come, too

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal - Implement basic multiple authentication (1.6)
ResponsesInList.Text: Promise! no inheritance bashing in this post! ;) I had forgotten about one important API change that we'll need to have multi-auth working well. I've worked/programmed a lot with other systems that implement multi-auth, namely PAM and Apache 's internal auth system (which is pretty sophisticated and it's a crying hsmae that PHP doesn't hook into it at all). These systems both implement an Auth API very much like Moodle, and you can configure each module and put them in order. Man, they were reading our minds. And through a time-machine too! ;) The difference, though, is that for the auth handler (in our case, `auth-user-login()` ) they accept 3 return codes, rather than just boolean. They are usually constants defined like: AUTH_OK - user/password verified AUTH_DENIED - an authoritative "we don't like the user", stronger than just user/pw don't match (perhaps they don't match and this plugin is authoritative with regards to this user acct) AUTH_DECLINED - non-authoritative "no". Means that user/pw didn't match, or I don't know about this user. Try the next plugin. and sometimes AUTH_ERROR - something went wrong (ext auth server not there?) The control loop is still simple, but becomes much more powerful. You breakout with a 'true' on thefirst OK you see, and with a 'false' on the first DENIED you see. If you get to the end of the foreach and all you've seen are DECLINED, then it's 'false'. Examples (taken from Apache and PAM plugins): As auth/plugins are 'stackable' you can implement a 'blacklist' plugin, and put it 'on top'. Plugin modules that actually can read the password can choose to issue a DENIED if the user matches, but the pw doesn't. What do you reckon?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External database authentication question
ResponsesInList.Text: It depends. If you plan to update external records from Moodle (i.e., update external database data with Moodle's data), then the user will need write access. If you don't plan to do any updates, then read-only access will do it. I guess the help text tries to be conservative: require write access in case you decide to do external updates (so you don't get errors later). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ldap_creators not drawing from Mac OS X Open Directory
ResponsesInList.Text: ldap_user_attribute is the attribute you use to name/search users in your directory. It's usually 'cn', but you can, for examplo, use 'sAMAccountName' if you are using MS Active Directory. ldap_memberattribute is the attribute name you use to list membership of a certain group, i.e., to get the list of users in a given group. Unless OSX OpenDirectory is quite different from the rest of directory servers, 'member' should do the trick. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Database Authentication - LAMP

So, to properly integrate authentication you will have to do something like the following in root/auth/lib.php: $queryfirst = $authdb->Execute("SELECT * FROM $CFG->auth_dbtable WHERE $CFG->auth_dbfielduser = '$username'"); switch ($CFG->auth_dbpasstype) {   // Re-format password accordingly case "md5": $md5pass = md5($password); $password = md5($md5pass . $queryfirst->fields['salt']); break; } Hope this helps somebody!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Redirect to a Course on Login
ResponsesInList.Text: Peter First please bear in mind that in a sense the site course, the front page of moodle, (course id=1) is the course that everyone sees when they log in. But, taking your request at face value, the most direct way, is to hack moodle/login/index.php at around line 188 (moodle 1.5.3)  make the changes shown in red, but changing the number in blue ("11" below) to the course that you wish users to be directed to. /// First, let's remember where the user was trying to get to before they got here ///Takemoto: and set up a default course to enter when they arrive. $defaultcourse = $CFG-> wwwroot ."/course/view.php?id= 11 "; if (empty($SESSION->wantsurl)) { $SESSION->wantsurl = array_key_exists('HTTP_REFERER',$_SERVER) ? $_SERVER["HTTP_REFERER"] : $defaultcourse ; } But I am not sure why you would want to always make users enter this default course, when the site course could provide the same look, feel, and functionality. If you mean when users log in for the first time (i.e. when they register), then you could add a link to the welcome email, the text of which is in lang/en_or_whatever/moodle.php This will not redirect users, but merely give them a link. Alternatively, if you mean when users log in for the first time, you might also make use of the Site policy, which is a page which is shown to users when they first log in (or to guest users every time they log in). You could add a link inside that. You could also hack the site police page so that when people click on the link accepting the site policy they might be taken to a specific course. I will hack that for your too, if you donate $50 to moodle! Timothy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Redirect to a Course on Login
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter The above will take all users to course whether they are a guest or not. By the way to redirect everyone the first time they log in can be achieved by changing line 28 of moodle/user/policy.php from redirect($CFG->wwwroot.'/'); to redirect($CFG->wwwroot.'/course/view.php?id=11'); but this again redirects everyone, because guests log in too, as guests. To take people to a different course depending upon wether they are guests are not then I guess you could use if (isguest()) { $mydefaultcourse = $CFG->wwwroot ; } else { $mydefaultcourse = $CFG->wwwroot.'/course/view.php?id=11'; } or perhaps $mydefaultcourse = isguest() ? $CFG->wwwroot : $CFG->wwwroot.'/course/view.php?id=11' ; In one or both of the above files. Timothy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Redirect to a Course on Login
ResponsesInList.Text: As far as I can tell, the section around line 180 comes in play when user was already using moodle and his session timed out. I don't think thus this is the right place to redirect user to another course. Some 30 lines higher is } else { $urltogo = $CFG->wwwroot.'/'; /// Go to the standard home page unset($SESSION->wantsurl); /// Just in case } You could try to change it following Tim's suggestion to } else if ($frm->username != 'guest') { $urltogo = $CFG->wwwroot.'/course/view.php?id=xx'; // xx is your alt home course unset($SESSION->wantsurl); /// Just in case } else { $urltogo = $CFG->wwwroot.'/'; /// send guest to the standard home page unset($SESSION->wantsurl); /// Just in case } Note: I am not sure how safe it is to use the isguest() at this stage of the game, so I suggest to explicitely test against guest login. Also, to avoid having to modify the code here again should the number of the alt home course changes, I suggest adding to config.php $CFG->nonstandard_homepage = xx; // course number of home for non-guests and use in the code $urltogo = $CFG->wwwroot.'/course/view.php?id='$CFG->nonstandard_homepage; Disclaimer: untested

failover support. ldap_version: 23 The version of the LDAP protocol your server is using. Bind settings ldap_preventpassindb: NoYes Select yes to prevent passwords from being stored in Moodle's DB. ldap_bind_dn: cn=ldap user,ou=full,ou=path to,ou=Users ou,dc=my,dc= domain If you want to use bind-user to search users, specify it here. Someting like 'cn=ldapuser,ou=public,o=org' ldap_bind_pw: Password for bind-user. User lookup settings ldap_user_type: Novell EdirectoryposixAccount (rfc2307)posixAccount (rfc2307bis)sambaSamAccount (v.3.0.7)MS ActiveDirectory Select how users are stored in LDAP. This setting also specifies how
login expiration, grace logins and user creation will work. ldap_contexts: ou=top level container for users,dc=my,dc=domain; List of contexts where users are located. Separate different contexts
with ';'. For example: 'ou=users,o=org; ou=others,o=org' ldap_search_sub: NoYes Search users from subcontexts. ldap_opt_deref: Choose...NoYes Determines how aliases are handled during search. Select one of the
following values: "No" (LDAP_DEREF_NEVER) or "Yes" (LDAP_DEREF_ALWAYS) ldap_user_attribute: Optional: Overrides the attribute used to name/search users. Usually 'cn'. ldap_memberattribute: Optional: Overrides user member attribute, when users belongs to a group. Usually 'member' ldap_objectclass: Optional: Overrides objectClass used to name/search users on ldap_user_type. Usually you dont need to chage this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No email confirmation  when the user signs up
ResponsesInList.Text:
Let's try step by step 1.- Open a console on your Fedora machine (xterm, konsole, whatever). 2.- Execute the following command: 
```text
telnet localhost 25
```
 3.- If you get something similar to this: 
```text
Trying 127.0.0.1...


Connected to localhost.


Escape character is '^]'.


220 bla-bla-bla  more text here ... SMTP maybe more text here
```
 then your local mail server accepts mail via SMTP. Type 'QUIT' and press Enter to close de the connection. 4.- If you get something similar to this: 
```text
Trying 127.0.0.1...


telnet: Unable to connect to remote 
host
: Connection refused
```
 then your mail server doesn't accept mail via SMTP. Maybe it accepts it via the 'sendmail' command (this works even if you are using a mail server other than sendmail, like postfix, exim, etc.) 5.- If your mail server accepted mail via SMTP, let's see if it can deliver it to the rest of the world. You have to type the bold text parts below. The rest is what the server sends you in response to your commands. Please, type it exactly like it's shown below ('<' and '<' included). I will be using the destination address 'elloco_delacolina@yahoo.es' to test this. Please, use an address you can read (to see if the mail arrives there or not 
```text
$ 
telnet localhost 25


Trying 127.0.0.1...


Connected to localhost.


Escape character is '^]'.


220 barad-dur.escomposlinux.org ESMTP Postfix (Debian/GNU)


HELO test.org


250 barad-dur.escomposlinux.org


MAIL FROM:<your-own-mail-address@your-
domain
>


250 Ok


RCPT TO:<elloco_delacolina@yahoo.es>


250 Ok


DATA


354 End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>


This is a test message.


.    
<--------- This is a dot ('.') followed by an ENTER


250 Ok: queued as 1AA9FF8014


QUIT


221 Bye
```
 Wait a few minutes and see if there is a new message for the address you typed above. If yes, you have a perfectly working local SMTP server If not, we have to find out where did the message go. You can use the 'mailq' command to show the mailserver queue. This queue holds the sent emails until they are sent to their final destination. If the mail server cannot send them for a know reason, using 'mailq' shows a little message noting the reason (DNS failure, cannot connect to destination server, address unknow, etc.). 6.- If your server didn't accept mail via SMTP in the first place, you can try to send it with something like this (the sendmail command is located at /usr/sbin in my Debian GNU/Linux, it can be located at /usr/lib on other Unices/Linuxes) 
```text
$ 
/usr/sbin/sendmail elloco_delacolina@yahoo.es


This is just some text for the message body


.   
<---- This is again a dot ('.') followed by an ENTER
```
 Now wait a few minutes and see if the message has arrived or not. If not, see again what 'mailq' tells you. If your mailserver is able to send emails to outside addresses, then you can configure moodle to use it (via SMTP or not, depending on what your local mail server allows you). But remember, even if your local mailserver is working correctly (and you have everything correctly setup in moodle), you still have to make sure your moodle cron jobs are running periodically. Because mail is sent from the cron jobs (if Im not mistaken). Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! I've got a query along similar lines to this one , but it's not using LDAP ... We have a series of Moodle implementations getting their user data from our service provider's MS SQL user database ... this is all fine and dandy (we have things set up so that each school only sees the users whose "school" field matches the school Moodle in question). However, in practice it works like this... School A has a list of 200 users (for example) and we authenticate learning.schoola.bucks.sch.uk (School A's moodle) against a list of users whose "school" field = School A from our big scary database. However, until one of those users logs in to learning.schoola.bucks.sch.uk they can't be seen by Moodle, which means that to add them to a course (or make them a teacher, or admin) they need to log in once, then wait for a teacher or admin to assign them to whatever they need assigning to. We don't want to establish a series of functions / processes and have to re-write them the next time there's an upgrade. If anything isn't clear, I'm happy to try and clarify! as ever, many tia Ian.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Weird session problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, now, for the first time I have actually seen this happen on one of my own servers. You can actually see in the logs how the person morphs from one person to another (the IP address remains constant). Needless to say even if it happens only rarely it's a bit of a worry! I'm almost 100% certain that this is a PHP bug with sessions and nothing to do with Moodle or Apache. This is how sessions work: The first time you connect to the web server, PHP creates a random session name that looks like this - c262d0fd3ec27b5119654e7607350539 - and sends it to your browser as a session cookie. At the same time, it creates a file on the disk with the same name, eg "sess_c262d0fd3ec27b5119654e7607350539". You can find these in moodledata/sessions. Every time you visit a page in the site, your browser sends the session cookie back to PHP. PHP uses this cookie to open the little file, and makes the 'session data' inside it available to the currently running scripts. When the script finishes (and the session data has possibly been updated) the file is written back to disk. Thus we can keep persistent information in the file that is available for the whole session. For example, when you actually use the login form, your user details are stored in the session (ie in this little file) and so all the later scripts know that you are logged in as such-and-such. Now what seems to be happening is that sometimes the wrong file is being selected for a particular user, or perhaps that the updating of the files is sometimes getting confused when trying to write two at the same time. I don't have any answers for this one, and after a quick look I haven't found anything yet in bugs.php.net ... all help would be very welcome ! (Edited to fix link)

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi We're currently testing the LDAP module before we continue looking to roll-out moodle 1.5 to the whole of our university. Activated the LDAP authentication but left bind_dn and bind_pw blank as our systems allows anonymous bind. More importantly we set Force Change Password to No - as we don't want
to allow our users to change their passwords in LDAP through moodle (we
have our own tools to do this). Their passwords are also not replicated
to the moodle db. However, we will also be using manually created accounts for users who
are not members of the university, and hence don't have an account on
our LDAP. The problem is that not allowing for users to change their password
also impacts on the facillity to request their forgotten password. This
isn't a problem for our University account holders, as we have other
resources for them to use to retrieve this (a web-page easily linked to or our helpdesk). The manual account holders
do need the Forgot Password screens though.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LDAP authenticated, but NO Forgot Password for manual accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: OK - I've realised that the sending the user to '1' problem (with a button?? - that's a link, not an action) is down to filling out Administration->Users->Authentication options for LDAP correctly. Specifically at the very end of another long form, under Common Settings -> Change Password URL . It was set to '1' for some reason... So I set it to point to our webpage for our users to retrieve their account details, and fiddled with lang/en/moodle.php to store the messages I wanted displayed on login/index_form.html - I added some additional text in that as well. It now does what I needed it to do, except that we're not allowing manual account users to access the forgot_password.php screens, as there's no way to stop internal users from reaching there at the moment as it seems all tied into *resetting* passwords, not retrieving them. And besides which, we're not storing passwords from LDAP into moodle's db so the system wouldn't be able to give our LDAP-account users their passwords (as we're using anonymous bind). If they got there, they'd probably end up writing passwords into their moodle account even though they're *meant* to be authenticating against LDAP. That's still a problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatic log in
ResponsesInList.Text: There are several tweaks needed. in login/index.php if (isset($_SERVER['AUTH_USER']) && $_SERVER['AUTH_USER'] != '') { $_SERVER['AUTH_USER'] = substr(strrchr($_SERVER['AUTH_USER'], '\\'), 1); //strip domain info $_SERVER['AUTH_USER'] = strtolower($_SERVER['AUTH_USER']); //compatibility hack $frm->username = $_SERVER['AUTH_USER']; $frm->password = ''; } else if ((!empty($SESSION->wantsurl) and strstr($SESSION->wantsurl,"username=guest")) or $loginguest) { in auth/ntlm/lib.php (copied from auth/ldap/lib.php): function auth_user_login ($username, $password) { /// Returns true if the username and password work /// and false if they don't global $CFG; if (!$username) {    // Don't allow blank usernames return false; } if ($_SERVER["AUTH_USER"] !== $username) { // important security check !!!! return false; } $ldap_connection = auth_ldap_connect(); if ($ldap_connection) { $ldap_user_dn = auth_ldap_find_userdn($ldap_connection, $username); //if ldap_user_dn is empty, user does not exist ldap_close($ldap_connection); if(!$ldap_user_dn){ return false; } else { return true; } } else { @ldap_close($ldap_connection); error(" LDAP -module cannot connect to server: $CFG->ldap_host_url"); } return false; }

ResponsesInList.Title: Novell Contexts - My last stand
ResponsesInList.Text: After ranting in the past about Novell contexts, I have gone away, done some reasearch and got my story straight Just to recap, Novell logins allow the user to specify their own context as part of the username with a proprietary dotted format. E.g, username.department.institution I would like Moodle to be able to accept these logins as in Novell EDirectory it is entirely possible to have non-unique usernames. What I propose is having a switch on the ldap configuration page that says something like "Allow user specified contexts for Novell" (note - this will only be active when Novell is selected at the top). When selected (AND Novell EDirectory) the username will be parsed and split around the dots. Turning this into a context is easy as all Novell installations have the same format - a series of ou= followed by an o= at the end. So the above example would become.. cn=username ou=department, o=institution and this context would be tried before any specified in the ldap configuration.

ResponsesInList.Text: Two comments... Keep username unique at all costs. Fudge it if you need to, as Moodle almost never prints it back to the users (exception: when sending lost-password emails). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Novell Contexts - My last stand
ResponsesInList.Text:
Yes - I think adding (in some way) the context to the username
(in the username field) is probably the lowest risk route. The
only thing I wonder is whether to read back the actual context
(if that is possible - I don't know yet) of all LDAP users
regardless of them specifying context or not. This reduces the
possible confusion of a user effectively having two logins - one > with the full context and one without. Users should have only one login -- don't let them login if they haven't selected a context. Offer the valid contexts in a dropdown, like the Windows Novell logon box, to avoid typos and inconsistencies. I think the username field will need to get bigger - but,
explain to me how substr(md5($context), 0, 8) is guaranteed
to uniquely map to the context? The only reason for the context to be appended or prepended is to guarantee uniqueness and for matching the user during login. Spelling out the full context right there is a waste of space. If you need it for reference, you can put it in the user preferences table. Now, you can use md5 to create a unique digest of the context, to append/prepend to the username. The digest is huge -- truncating it weakens it a bit, but you are only worrying about collisions between the very few valid contexts in your environment. In fact, I'd say get just 4 chars from the md5 and you won't need to change the field size for username. I also wonder why you suggested prepending the context
information - my initial though was that putting it on
the end (just like they type it in) would be more natural
- am I missing something? If you prepend it with a prefix of known length (like a 4 char fragment of an md5), you can make liberal use of substr() both on PHP and on SQL . It's fast, and easy to read and document in the code. For example, you can do a SELECT with a WHERE clause to find users based on their user-viewable username, disregarding the prefix, because you can use substr straight there in the WHERE. Suffixes are a pain to deal with -- you can use substr and friends with suffixes but you have to get the length and then count chars backwards, or depend on non-standard implementations that do negative indexes. And it's much much slower. Database queries and anything that looks like an index search or string manipulation has historically been much faster and more powerful doing things from the beginning of the string. I'm off to have a play about with it Have fun!
